name: 15 The Four Realms
description: The opening state of the guide The Four Realms.

covenants.name: Durenmar
covenants.summary:
Domus magna of House Bonisagus and the oldest covenant in the Order, Durenmar fills a hidden, steep-sided valley some fifteen miles inside the northern Black Forest, about fifteen miles south of Hirsau monastery, with Baden to the north-west. Here Bonisagus settled at a ruined Roman temple around 754, here the Order was founded and its first Tribunal held in 767, and here the Rhine Tribunal and the Grand Tribunal still meet, on the Tribunal Field by the Forum of Hermes. The Tower of Bonisagus holds the Great Library, the largest Hermetic collection anywhere, and most Bonisagus magi visit at least once in their lives.

The covenant thinks of itself as the political and traditional heart of the Order and is still greatly respected through its House, but its power is quietly ebbing both in the Rhine and beyond it. Its magi look inward, absorbed in research while the fabric of the place crumbles: an Autumn covenant forever on the edge of Winter, a place of quiet study rather than intrigue, while Fengheld has grown into the Tribunal's largest and arguably strongest covenant. The decline is traced to the Schism War, the failure of House Bonisagus's diplomacy and the exile of the Hercynian lineage whose Waldherz chapter had kept peace with the forest fay; since then Durenmar has been ignorant of the faerie woods about it, and no peace was ever made.

Murion's faction, which now leads, holds that Hermetic theory is to be kept pure of inferior hedge magic and is intolerant of hedge wizards and outsiders; the library's texts on such things are locked away for House elders alone. Critics say this deepens the stagnation and that Murion directs research instead of guiding it; an outward-looking minority gathered round Occultes wants exotic techniques brought in. A Magic aura of 7 lies over the clearing, defended by an Aegis of the Hearth of very high magnitude, devised after the faerie raid of 1085. The clearing is split by a stream and has no walls; the magi's sancta stand on the south bank, forbidden to all but a few trusted servants, and magic items heat, light and clean the towers and carry up the meals. A hidden guard post down the valley conceals the three-mile track in, and unexplored caves run under the north cliffs.

The covenant is led by the Prima of House Bonisagus, who holds the sigil of Bonisagus and is thereby Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal. Its offices are the Colens Arcanorum (the librarian), the Tenens Occultorum, and two honorary posts the Primus fills by invitation: the Protector, traditionally a Flambeau master or archmage who sees to the covenant's defence, and the Artificer, traditionally a Verditius who crafts items for its glory. A Guernicus is always in residence, a Gifted Mercere oversees the Mercer House in the basement of the Tower of Trianoma, and at least one guest magus from every gild is kept in residence. Retired former members may still vote by proxy sigil at covenant meetings. There are no chapter houses at present. Three towers dominate the clearing: the Tower of Bonisagus, enchanted against all decay of its books and wound about by a huge ancient magical vine said to be Merinita's gift; the Tower of Notatus, conjured by the first Primus, which houses most of the Bonisagus magi, Murion's sanctum on its top two floors and two excellent shared labs in its basement; and the shorter, crooked Tower of Trianoma, its top two floors lost to a forgotten accident, home to the Trianoma lineage and the non-Bonisagus members. Lesser buildings include the mill and guard tower where the turb greets visitors and rings a bell for a magus, the standing stone of Notatus where guests are welcomed and given their Aegis token, Verditius' Forge half-buried under a grassy bank, the Protector's Watchtower on the cliffs amid blasted ground, the overgrown ruin called Seneca's Folly, and a hunters' lodge at the top of the clearing.

Up to six peregrinatores lodge here at a time, from a long waiting list; magi accept almost any terms for access to the library, and a guest is usually asked to give two seasons of gild training to a Rhine apprentice, while the Bonisagus members share out the extra season of training owed to every Rhine apprentice. The covenfolk are quiet and peculiar, keep to themselves and have little to do with the magi; born in the aura, all carry Warping and live unusually long, and remnants of an old nature cult linger in their beliefs, with no church. A small band of expert huntsmen forays into the woods for vis and game. Redcaps run south to the Greater Alps and to Harco by the Rorschach chapter on Lake Constance, the Copper Rooster inn at Basel and the friendly covenant Sinews of Knowledge, or directly by the Mercere Portal to Harco.
covenants.what_matters:
Portals: masters, archmagi and Redcaps use Durenmar's Mercere Portals free; anyone else pays two pawns of vis each, a few retainers going free (Guardians of the Forests p. 26)
Income: lab rental, 5 or more pawns a season for a shared basement lab in the Tower of Notatus, 2 pawns for a guest lab across the river
Income: dwindling; barred from faerie sites since 1151, and several magical sites were lost to Zaehringen settlement in the early 12th century
Mundane: Durenmar ignores mundane politics; Hirsau monastery, fifteen miles north, spreads rumours of a hidden city of sorcerers
Mundane: speculation that Durenmar patronised, or withered, the Zaehringens of Baden is thought unlikely
Tension: Dankmar is the old enemy; in 1081 Durenmar accused it of league with the fay and lost, in 1151 Dankmar had Durenmar fined a rook of vis to every covenant and barred from faerie sites for fourteen years
Tension: the 1085 raid of the King of the Black Mountain killed or carried off several Bonisagus magi and many covenfolk; none came back
Tension: Murion's purists against Occultes's inclusive faction, which a sizeable minority of the House would rather see as Primus
Tension: Fengheld and its allies oppose Philippus Niger at every turn; the Ash Gild's war on the Norse wizards has Murion's quiet favour
Tension: no research breakthrough in decades, promising magi leaving, elders lost to age and Final Twilight
Tension: Petrus Virilis's programme of Gifted children, and the young magae writing to him
Tension: the Fane of the Founders, where twelve magi renew the Founders' vows every seventh year during the Tribunal; most Durenmar magi know of it, none has found it
Hook: the library is unhelpful about exotic and non-Hermetic lore; obscure lab notes and old books hint at forgotten artifacts; magi from distant Tribunals pass through

secrets.title: The Black Fir
secrets.text: The Black Fir near the Great Library is the King of the Black Mountain's slow revenge: planted at the Aegis's edge over a century ago after his direct attacks failed, it was taken inside the Aegis when the magi found its cones gave vis, and so breached their own defence.

secrets.title: The Black Fir creeps
secrets.text: The Black Fir creeps about six inches a year toward the Tower of Bonisagus; what happens when it reaches the tower or the vine is unknown but likely severe. The magi think it immemorial.

secrets.title: Murion's raven
secrets.text: Murion sends her raven familiar Kolkrabus to spy on Dankmar and others she counts enemies, against the Code.

secrets.title: Vis for the library
secrets.text: Vis donations are quietly accepted at Durenmar in place of a contribution to the library and prop up the dwindling vis income; this is never admitted.

secrets.title: Occultes and the restricted texts
secrets.text: Occultes knows the restricted texts and has copied or moved the most interesting into his own sanctum, passing them to allies whose research they suit.

secrets.title: Petrus Virilis's ritual
secrets.text: Petrus Virilis means to invent a longevity ritual that would probably leave him infertile; Murion would be furious.

secrets.title: What the Fane holds
secrets.text: The Fane of the Founders is an artifact into which the Cult of Mercury bound much of the Black Forest's original magical essence; if Durenmar fell and the rite lapsed, the King of the Black Mountain hopes to seize that spirit.

secrets.title: Vis at Durenmar
secrets.text:
Vis: Intellego from the golden-green sap of the great vine on the Tower of Bonisagus (amount not given)
Vis: Perdo from the pine cones of the Black Fir, gathered yearly (amount not given)
Vis: Vim from Petrus Virilis's seed
Vis: several kinds cultivated among the exotic plants of Ricardus Caespuus's glass Herbam laboratory
Vis: the hot springs of upper Baden (Magic 2), which Durenmar owns Hermetically
Vis: the huntsmen's forays into the nearby woods

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The Fane's spirit is treated as Magic Might 40.

covenants.name: Dankmar
covenants.summary:
A small Winter covenant in the dampest, darkest part of the Black Forest, about forty miles south-west of Durenmar and a few miles south of the Black Forest Road, founded in 1052 by Aschlaranda, cast out of Durenmar and House Bonisagus, with her apprentice Schadrit, and named in mockery of the Order's birthplace to oppose Durenmar in all things. The firs grow so thick that it is dusk at noon; only fungi live on the poisoned carpet of needles and only ravens call.

A round palisade of split logs encloses wooden huts and four two-storey stone towers, the sancta of its four magae, which run down into linked caves reached only through the towers. Fir and yew lean over the walls and every wooden thing glows day and night with phosphorescent bracket fungi. The Faerie aura is 5, and Orphedra's version of the Shrouded Glen (level 40, Penetration 20, with her darkness sigil) hides the place for at least a mile, turning travellers away in nameless dread; those whose Magic Resistance holds feel nothing. Ancient Schadrit broods at the centre and her descendants do her bidding.

Dankmar keeps a careful working relationship, never an alliance, with the most malign dark fae of the deep forest, the formless beings of darkness and fear that resent mankind, and this has let it outlast Durenmar's hostility and the emperor's clearing of the forests. Its covenfolk are wholly bewitched by Jiphella: fanatically loyal, worshipping the magae as gods and ready to die at a word, but slack-witted, unable to think for themselves and needing to be told to eat each day. There are no consortes.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: not given
Mundane: hostile to the emperor's deforestation; mundanes who feel the Shrouded Glen never return
Tension: Durenmar accused Dankmar at the Tribunal of 1081 of secret league with the fay, and proved nothing; in 1151 Dankmar prosecuted Durenmar for plundering faerie sites and won, with the rare joint backing of the Hawthorn and Elder Gilds
Tension: the destruction of St Georgen monastery in 1208 is widely blamed on Dankmar; at the Tribunal of 1214 Jiphella, its sole delegate, denied it, and with no mundane witness and the Guardians of the Forests ruling to shelter under, a close vote refused an investigation
Tension: Murion's raven Kolkrabus spies on the covenant
Faerie: Orphedra has a pact with the local bockmen to patrol the woods around the covenant
Hook: a cautionary example of what magical domination of mundanes comes to

secrets.title: The destruction of St Georgen
secrets.text: Dankmar's hand is suspected in the destruction of St Georgen, whose monks were found hanging dead in strange dark vines.

secrets.title: Vis at Dankmar
secrets.text: Vis: not given

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The book suspects but never states Dankmar's hand.

covenants.name: Triamore
covenants.summary:
A castle and manorial estate on the Meuse at the edge of the Ardennes in Lower Lorraine, on the western fringe of the Rhine Tribunal, with Liege and Verdun the nearest towns; Verdun and Triamore are where the Redcaps of the Rhine and Normandy usually meet. A comfortable covenant of reasonable magi with a Magic aura of 2 and a famous library, to which guests are expected to add a book.

Triamore has long been tangled in the politics of its neighbourhood, for which the local Quaesitores have repeatedly sought to censure it; only the shrewd dealing of its princeps, Daria la Gris, has held them off. Recent deaths and Twilights have left it magically and politically weak and pushed to the margins, so Daria recruits by welcoming peregrinatores and visiting magi, though the tales of trouble keep numbers low.

As co-leader of the Apple Gild she backs the proposed Lotharingian Tribunal, which would free the covenant's mundane dealings and turn it from a border minnow into the hub of a new Tribunal; to that end she cultivates friendships with several Normandy covenants. Both its Tremere sigils are held by Stentorius of Fengheld, the Tremere exarch of the Rhine.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: a manorial estate (details not given)
Mundane: deep in local politics, details not given; Redcaps pass through on the road between the Rhine and Normandy
Tension: the Lotharingian motion, which would make Triamore the centre of a new Tribunal
Tension: Quaesitorial scrutiny of its mundane entanglements, fended off so far by Daria
Tension: vacancies after recent deaths and Twilights, an open door for new magi or a sign of something sinister
Hook: the library draws visitors, who are expected to contribute a book
Allies: several Normandy covenants, cultivated by Daria

secrets.title: The Quaesitores and Triamore
secrets.text: The Quaesitores have long wished to censure Triamore for its mundane dealings.

secrets.title: Vis at Triamore
secrets.text: Vis: not given

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The cause of the recent deaths is not stated.

covenants.name: Waddenzee
covenants.summary:
A Spring covenant of pirate magi on a deserted stretch of the Frisian island of Terschelling, on the Wadden Sea, preying on the shipping of the North Sea, skirting the Code of Hermes and breaking mundane law every day. It was founded in 1165 as Terschelling by Axior of Flambeau, a dissident of Oculus Septentrionalis, who died in a magical accident within twenty years. Hygwald Veritas and Eric Ribecus arrived in 1200 and by 1207 announced that they were the only magi left, renamed the covenant Waddenzee, a claim to the whole sea, and changed its charter and symbol, to uproar at Tribunal; a Quaesitorial inquiry found no wrongdoing and a vote to treat it as a new covenant needing the Tribunal's leave failed thanks to the Oak and Ash Gilds.

About twenty years ago Hygwald and Eric killed a pirate chief and took his three ships and crews; the covenant now sails five magically enhanced ships, the flagship Nebelkönigin among them, taken from Oculus Septentrionalis while she carried a great cargo of vis and magical books with no magus aboard. It stays within the letter of the Code by leaving no witnesses. Only the failure of the coastal nobles to act together has saved it, and an understanding with Fengheld restrains Oculus Septentrionalis from moving against it.

A Magic aura of 3 covers the covenant building and a few hundred paces round it: a long, low Danish-style long-house sunk partly into the ground for the covenfolk, with four separate buildings for the magi joined to the middle of each wall by sunken covered walkways, each holding a magus, his lab, one or two consortes and some warriors, and a harbour. The magi foster the island's reputation for haunting, in truth the din of thousands of seabirds in spring and summer, and have driven off other settlers. The turb of nearly two hundred pirates and hangers-on from all over Europe is probably the Rhine's largest; about half are at sea at any time in two ships and most of the rest are drunk, but they obey the magi and their deputies.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: piracy on the North Sea with five enchanted ships
Mundane: outlaws to the local nobility, who cannot unite against them
Tension: enemies of Oculus Septentrionalis, which waits for one misstep
Tension: the Quaesitores have warned the covenant repeatedly that it walks a fine line, will get no Tribunal support if the mundane authorities move, and that each pirate magus would likely face charges of High Crimes
Tension: Eric Ribecus's younger cousin Estrid Danesson of Oculus Septentrionalis is his bitter enemy
Allies: a mutual understanding with Fengheld; the Oak and Ash Gilds backed it in the 1207 vote
Hook: a generation hence the Hanseatic League will build bigger ships, sail in convoy and hire soldiers against pirates; with Oculus Septentrionalis at its head an assault on Waddenzee is plausible, but the League is more than twenty years off
Hook: the stolen Hermetic books may have been placed in the pirates' hands and tainted; Lucas may be using infernal lore in his necromancy without knowing it, and only Hachim may have the wisdom to resist

secrets.title: Imanitos and the pirates
secrets.text: Imanitos Mendax of Oculus Septentrionalis feeds Eric advance word of that covenant's ship movements for a share of the plunder, and the Waddenzee magi are party to it; the messages may travel by Astasians, tiny messenger demons taken for airy spirits.

secrets.title: The power in the graveyards
secrets.text: The power of the Pirates' Graveyards may be Infernal rather than Magic; Lucas has barely considered it.

secrets.title: Vis at Waddenzee
secrets.text:
Vis: rich, but mostly other people's, taken as plunder
Vis: Lucas von Beck harvests vis at the Pirates' Graveyards in Drenthe, where the Frisian pirates bury their dead

covenants.name: Oculus Septentrionalis
covenants.summary:
The Eye of the North, a Summer covenant mostly of House Jerbiton spread through the city of Lübeck in Holstein, on the Baltic, in townhouses, warehouses, a shipyard and a fleet. The Tribunal created it by charter in 1144, at the Ash Gild's urging, to learn about the Norse wizards, ruling that a covenant needed no site at its founding, only magi bound by a charter. Its first magi did nothing for two decades, were fined three pawns each in 1158 and ordered to find a site, and three of them settled in Lübeck around 1160 while Axior left to found Terschelling.

It abandoned the Ash mission for peaceful contact and trade with the magical folk of the north, two of whom have married its magi, and became a principal proponent of the Apple Gild. Hermetically weak and aloof from Tribunal politics, it is immensely rich and woven into the city as merchants, scholars and craftsmen; the burghers do not know them for wizards, and its wealth may exceed that of all the other Rhine covenants together. Lübeck has an ordinary Divine aura and the covenant no Magic aura of its own. The Quaesitores wrote into its charter that it may admit only magi with the Gentle Gift.

Its magi seldom raise the Parma daily or cast where they can be seen, though most have some discreet magic; they meet rarely, so their politics are gossipy and conspiratorial. Discreet visitors are welcome and indiscreet ones asked to leave. There is room for one or two more magi, Jerbiton, Apple Gild or Redcaps with the Gentle Gift and a mundane trade, and two seldom-used peregrinator labs above the Novgorod Inn. There is no turb, only a handful of mercenaries guarding the businesses, whose staff blur with the covenant's many servants and two scribes. Lübeck is the usual stop for Redcaps bound for Novgorod, a few weeks away by sea, and the covenant keeps a contact at the trading counter Lübeck's merchants have run there since 1205. Theoderich of Jerbiton recently left to help found Heorot in Denmark and remains friendly.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: trade, shipbuilding and the businesses of its magi; perhaps the richest covenant in the Rhine
Mundane: integrated among Lübeck's burghers as merchants, scholars and craftsmen; a contact at the Novgorod counter; Henri de Tours is likely to be at the heart of the coming Hanse
Tension: Waddenzee has taken several of its ships and cargoes, the Nebelkönigin among them; the covenant wants the pirates ended by Tribunal ruling or a secretly provoked mundane army, but has no proof and fears Quaesitorial scrutiny of its own mundane dealings
Tension: the Quaesitores forbade the trading venture the Nebelkönigin carried, so the ship cannot legally be recovered
Tension: Crintera suspects it of aiding the Danish invasion of Rügen; Urgen killed its leader Prudentum in Wizard's War in 1179, and since Falke's moderate leadership the two covenants ignore each other
Tension: Philippus Niger presses it to investigate the Norse wizards harder and to open a Mercere Portal to Durenmar
Hook: Henri de Tours may negotiate the treaty of Lübeck and Hamburg of 1241 or become Älderman; the League may be the covenant's own idea, and growing wealth brings Quaesitorial risk and the temptation to bribe at Tribunal
Hook: Marcus Navicularius is designing the Baltic cog, round, flat-bottomed, with a centre rudder and one square sail, carrying hundreds of tons of Novgorod timber, which the Hanse will adopt by mid-century

secrets.title: The Verditius magestones
secrets.text: Oculus Septentrionalis holds three Verditius magestones, given secretly in 1144, each giving a Magic aura of 3 over a large room; they are shared so each magus has a Magic-aura lab for up to two seasons a year. Only Durenmar's senior magi also know.

secrets.title: Imanitos's betrayal
secrets.text: Imanitos Mendax betrays the covenant to Waddenzee, selling its ship movements for a share of the loot; discovery would mean expulsion and undying enmity.

secrets.title: The deal with Fengheld
secrets.text: Oculus Septentrionalis has a secret deal with Fengheld: a rook of vis a year in exchange for a huge yearly shipment of luxuries and over a hundred pounds of silver.

secrets.title: Vis at Oculus Septentrionalis
secrets.text:
Vis: chronically short; a few sources, all far from Lübeck around the Baltic, gathered by Estrid Danesson
Vis: Boris of Novgorod buys Novgorod vis cheaply

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: Imanitos might swap the magestones for infernally tainted copies to breed greed in the labs. He may also be a diabolist of a hidden dark Jerbiton lineage serving the demon Radegast, corrupting Lübeck's notables through the Goldenes Kalb and posing as Radegast's prophet to the Mecklenburg family, with low-Might demons for messengers, thieves, spies and seducers.

covenants.name: Fengheld
covenants.summary:
The largest covenant of the Rhine in land, people and magi, twenty-three of them with about a dozen at the main site, and the most diverse, with no House or gild dominant: an Autumn covenant in a sprawling hilltop fortress in a lonely spot among the hills of the eastern Harz, on the borders of Saxony and Thuringia, with a Magic aura of 5 on the hilltop and half a dozen chapter houses across northern mainland Europe. It presents itself as the Tribunal's neutral peacemaker and often arbitrates between covenants; both the Apple and the Linden Gilds were founded by its members.

Founded in 1039 by Flambeau and Tremere veterans home from the Schism War in Stonehenge and Normandy, approved readily as a quiet retreat for ageing war heroes away from mundanes, it became instead the base from which its political Tremere, with the Transylvanian Tribunal, served Emperor Henry III's conquests of Bohemia, Poland and Hungary and seized many vis sites. When the main site filled, the Tribunal blocked its daughter covenants of young Tremere, so it founded chapter houses instead, citing Greater Alps practice and trusting its martial strength to hold several sites. Every chapter magus accepts Fengheld's charter, a ruling on Fengheld binds the chapters and the reverse, and most chapters have a local charter too. Ties with Transylvania have lately loosened and it is no longer seen as a Tremere covenant.

Its hierarchy is rigid: the Archmage Stentorius; eight masters, five at the main site (Eule, Horst, Peter von Würzburg, Dorana, Indulius) and three in chapters (Clemens, Hassan El-Megrayhi, Wilhelm Weiss); then fourteen journeymen, the six at the main site ranking a little above the eight in chapters. Of the eleven chapter magi six are detailed in five chapters and five are left to the storyguide, as is the site of the biggest chapter, run by Clemens filius Stentorius, which could sit near the player covenant; or the player magi could themselves be a chapter under Fengheld's seniors.

An immense curtain wall rings a summit of some twenty buildings: a tower for every resident magus, an elaborate guest house, a huge meeting hall and housing for covenfolk and grogs, with outlying hamlets. Vineyards and orchards cover the south slope, grain and roots the valley floor, sheep and goats the rest, feeding well over two hundred people: about fifty soldiers, fifteen companions and nearly ten dozen smiths, glassblowers, parchment-makers, scribes, huntsmen, herders and serfs, each hierarchy ending in a magus. Eight guest labs at the main site and at least one at most chapters make it a famed host of peregrinatores, with up to six Redcaps present at a time. It is rich in minor enchanted items and raw vis.

Fengheld holds one of the Rhine's two Mercer Houses and its senior Redcap, and is the busier of the two for its central position and its generosity: Redcaps serving the north, Boris of Novgorod among them, meet those serving the south here at agreed times, and Redcaps from other Tribunals who will not cross the Black Forest come here instead of Durenmar. This near-monopoly of the Order's news serves Fengheld well.
covenants.what_matters:
Income: a vast farming estate, Peter von Würzburg's wines, and the trade of the Rheingasse and Cherbourg chapters
Mundane: the local nobility has somehow never noticed the scale of the estate, and nobody has openly accused Fengheld of magic to keep it so; Peter's wines are prized by the nobles of southern Saxony and Thuringia
Mundane: the Rheingasse chapter in Cologne manages supplies and contacts; Fengheld House in Cherbourg trades with England and France
Votes: more than forty Tribunal votes, nearly a quarter of the whole, though seldom cast as a bloc; Stentorius holds about three-fifths of the Rhine's Tremere sigils
Tension: the more paranoid magi of the Tribunal suspect a hidden agenda behind the neutrality
Tension: Fengheld and its allies oppose Philippus Niger of Durenmar at every turn; Dorana urges Stentorius to contest Murion's leadership of the Oak Gild and Occultes to contest her Primacy, while the familiars Oswald and Kolkrabus feud over the gild
Tension: a planned chapter at Durenmar, Rudolph of Bonisagus's idea, is backed cautiously and doubted by some seniors
Tension: the Lusatia chapter, ten miles from the agreed Novgorod border, caused the latest boundary dispute with that Tribunal; Odorpes has been accused at Tribunal more than once of neglecting her duties
Allies: a mutual understanding with Waddenzee; Hassan El-Megrayhi is parens of Hachim of Waddenzee, and Imanitos Mendax of Oculus Septentrionalis won his Master rank here
Hook: the library is vast but weighted to low-level books, so Fengheld-trained magi are generalists; specialists are invited as guests to improve it
Hook: Balastor means to return others to a feral state whether they consent or not

secrets.title: Fengheld's real policy
secrets.text: Fengheld's real policy is to keep every other covenant so tangled in politics that nobody notices its own growing power; it has worked so far, and its vote bloc is the Tribunal's largest.

secrets.title: Eule's wisdom
secrets.text: Eule has passed into Final Twilight, and her celebrated wisdom is her filius Günther Lupus's fraud.

secrets.title: The Bears' Cave
secrets.text: The Bears' Cave in the northern Harz is the private vis source of a hidden lineage of bear-heartbeast Bjornaer descending from the Founder: Urgen of Crintera and his filia Odorpes of the Lusatia chapter.

secrets.title: Vis at Fengheld
secrets.text:
Vis: about two dozen sites, some hundreds of miles away, many seized in the eastern conquests of the 11th century; none is named
Vis: a rook a year goes to Oculus Septentrionalis (secretly) for luxuries and silver

covenants.name: Heorot
covenants.summary:
A newly founded covenant on the Danish island of Zealand, raised on the site of the hall of Hrothgar, the Danish king of legend whom Beowulf rid of Grendel. It is not yet a member of the Rhine Tribunal and hopes to be admitted at the Tribunal of 1221.

Zealand is by tradition Novgorod territory, but no covenant of the Order has ever lasted long enough in the Norse lands to attend a Tribunal, the Order of Odin being thought too great a danger, so whose ground it is remains a grey area. All Heorot's magi come from the Rhine, and their declared purpose is the one Oculus Septentrionalis was founded for and never pursued: to learn about the Order of Odin. Unlike that covenant, they have the skills for it.

Oculus Septentrionalis sponsors the application; Crintera, close by on Rügen, opposes it. Meanwhile the kin of Grendel, trolls of the island's bogs, harass the covenant.
covenants.what_matters:
Membership: not yet a member of the Rhine Tribunal; applies at the Tribunal of 1221, and the Novgorod Tribunal, whose territory Zealand nominally is, has not been told
Border dispute: many Rhine magi enjoy the thought of taking ground from Novgorod, and the Tribunal would like to push its claim east
Opposition: Crintera, close by on Rügen, fears a rival for the region's vis sources and objects to the admission
Support: Oculus Septentrionalis sponsors the covenant; Waddenzee does not object, since Heorot will bring it more victims and serves the Ash Gild's chief interest
Purpose: to learn about the Order of Odin, the aim Oculus Septentrionalis once held, and this time with the skills to pursue it
Trolls: the kin of Grendel still haunt Zealand's bogs and attack the covenant; Signum Irruptus's study of them has already cost fourteen grogs and his own left arm
Mundane relations: not recorded; Zealand is Danish, under King Valdemar II

secrets.title: The price of sponsorship
secrets.text: Oculus Septentrionalis has very likely struck some private bargain with Heorot as the price of its sponsorship.

secrets.title: Vis at Heorot
secrets.text: Vis: no sources recorded

covenants.name: Crintera
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Bjornaer, deep in the Stubnitz Forest on the Jasmund peninsula of Rügen, inside a Magic regio of four levels whose auras run 1, 3, 5 and 8. Its only members are the six Elders of the Bjornaer council, who govern the House from here. It was founded by the followers of Bjornaer in the Order's first days and has stood ever since.

Once a quiet and powerful force in the Tribunal, Crintera has been in turmoil since the Danish conquest of Rügen in 1168 and has spent the fifty years since in Winter, as new churches and a Cistercian monastery push the Dominion towards it and a Christian island yields fewer recruits for the turb. The council is divided between Harmonists, who would live alongside mundanes who leave the wild alone, and Wilderists, who would defend the wilderness against all men.

Religion of every kind is forbidden inside the regio in honour of the Animal Powers, who held the forest before the Bjornaer came; it is among the covenant's oldest laws. Every twelve years the whole House meets here for the Gathering of Twelve Years, which the islanders call the Devil's Year.

Crossing each boundary of the regio works a Corpus effect that draws the crosser's heartbeast forward, a personality trait at the first and small bodily changes at the others, so that someone who has crossed all four looks a quarter or a third animal. The Parma usually resists this, but resisting is thought rude; Bjornaer can shrug the changes off with their Heartbeast. Visitors reach it by the Watching Path, the one route through Stubnitz, marked at its start by two mossy, crumbling stones in a glade near the forest's edge and known to Redcaps and Bjornaer; covenfolk and animal allies watch everyone who walks it.

The covenant of Rethra in Pomerania, once a sister community of Slavic magus-priests, fell silent and was declared abolished by the Tribunal of 1207, leaving Crintera the Order's only presence in the Marches.
covenants.what_matters:
Factions: Harmonists against Wilderists on the council, with Urgen's Wilderists gaining ground as the occupation drags on; the next Gathering, in 1227, is expected to be explosive
Heorot: Crintera opposes its admission in 1221, fearing competition for vis near Rügen
Oculus Septentrionalis: a feud since 1179, when Urgen accused them of helping the Danish invasion and slew their leader in Wizard War; lately the guest Caprea blinded the familiar of their peace envoy Carolus by accident, and relations are worse than ever
The Danes: King Valdemar II's occupation, the churches of Bergen and Altenkirchen, a Cistercian monastery, monks farming Mönchgut and a church planned at Sagard, five miles away; the turb shrinks as recruits grow scarce
The Baltic thaw: each early spring Falke casts Appease the Queen of Winter at Arkona, where Svantovit's lingering presence gives the ritual a bonus, to break the sea ice and reopen shipping
Faerie trod: the volkhvy of the Forest Brothers alone can open the gate in the Ziegensteine barrow, and often let Bjornaer use it; it leads one way to Pripet Major in the Novgorod Tribunal
Pagan allies: friendly with the volkhvy of the Forest Brothers and the priestesses of Hertha; the Svantovit priests of Arkona helped Falke learn her ritual
Mundane relations: hostile or wary towards the Danish crown and the island's churches; islanders shun Stubnitz and tell of animal attacks, shadow-monsters and witches, which suits the covenant
The Gathering of Twelve Years: all Bjornaer come every twelve years (last 1203, next 1227), fifty to a hundred magi, for lineage rites, remembrance of the dead, most Mystery initiations under the Swan Elder, Ardea's re-enactments of old legends, visions of the Animal Powers and House politics; nothing is confirmed or denied to outsiders
The council: Wolf (the Primus), Bear (Senior Elder, always a bear heartbeast, casting vote), Horse (keeps track of all Bjornaer), Stag (protector), Eagle (watches the Order), Swan (leads rituals, long held by a line of heron-heartbeast seers); a bear Primus merges Wolf and Bear and a Seat of the Fox fills the sixth place
Succession: a dead or Twilit Elder waits for the next Gathering, when the rest choose by an ancient divination (once a Great Beast pointed out the heir); the whole House elects the Primus from the council's candidates
Guests: visiting Bjornaer may raise a temporary sanctum on the third regio level and stay for years

secrets.title: Urgen's campaigns
secrets.text: Urgen is widely suspected of driving mundanes from the wild with covert animal attacks, and is stepping them up now that the Primacy no longer restrains him.

secrets.title: The look of Stubnitz
secrets.text: Stubnitz only looks untouched: the forest hides many settlements of covenfolk, concealed by magic.

secrets.title: The fetishes of the Animal Powers
secrets.text: The fetishes of the Animal Powers on Crintera's fourth level (a wooden squirrel on a stump, a stone otter among cattails, a rush-woven snake in a hollow boulder, a clay wolf with shell teeth, stone birds in willow saplings hung with feathered thongs, and one for every other beast, only a few visible from any spot) are truly ancient and said to hold primordial nature spirits. Touching one's own brings a deep sense of connection; anyone who resisted the regio's changes, or nears another's fetish, feels compelled to leave it alone. Covenfolk leave offerings at the fetish of their heartbeast.

secrets.title: What the Founder was
secrets.text: Bjornaer the Founder was a Pomeranian shapeshifter-witch; the werewolves of Pomerania count her a traitor who sold their secrets to the Roman priests.

secrets.title: Vis at Crintera
secrets.text: Vis: Creo vis every year from Zora, priestess of Hertha, in return for protection of her priesthood and a promise that no victim is taken from Crintera's covenfolk; other sources not recorded, though the invasion is said to have damaged them while leaving them largely intact

covenants.name: Irencillia
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Merinita, hidden in faerie woodland where the northern Bohemian Forest meets the plain, among beech and oak full of fallow deer, boar, lynx and bears. Quendalon, the second Primus, built it after his return from Arcadia, when he turned the House towards the fae, so it dates from the late eighth or ninth century. The land about it is kept wild by the covenant's meddling.

An Autumn covenant, now larger than ever as human encroachment on faerie lands drives Merinita magi home to it; three further magi beyond those named live here, left to the storyguide. It holds aloof from the politics of region and Tribunal alike, prizing its seclusion.

Its Faerie aura is patchy: at least 1 everywhere within the boundary, up to 6 where the sancta stand, with odd high spots such as a covered walk to the kitchens at 4 along its length. Many of the stronger patches, most sancta among them, lie in fragmented regiones whose entrances bear symbols (a badger's head, a crescent moon) that outsiders cannot read. The theory is that all this is the wreckage of the vast magical war between Quendalon and Myanar.

The covenant shows itself to each visitor as expectation shapes it: a castle of living wood with courtiers, a hamlet of foresters in green and brown, a wooded hill with a trilithon over a labyrinth, a gully of caves peopled by twisted folk; those who do not know it is there see open woodland and wander through unaware, avoided by its people. Every view shares an enclosing boundary (palisade, drystone wall or thorn hedge), a single gateway, and over it an inscription said to be Merinita's last words before she vanished in 785, to the effect that the spirits of old endure unchanged in the depths of rivers and the endless twilight of forests.

The glamour is lived, not merely seen: materials, covenfolk's looks and even a plucked leaf differ from one observer to another, and anything carried out of the aura turns to dust and dry twigs at sunrise or sunset. No usable map can be drawn; only the sancta (each magus's firm notion of his own, as castle, town house, garden or barrow) and to a lesser degree the shared library, council chamber and dining hall reach a consensus. No magus's Magic Resistance has ever stopped the effect, and nobody knows whether it is a spell, a faerie power or something else. Every magus who stays more than a season gains a caricature, a faerie double.
covenants.what_matters:
House politics: Handri outmanoeuvred Vinaria and took the Primacy from her; she went into what is called Faerie Twilight and came back after seven years apparently unchanged
The God of Truth: a dualist faith reverencing the wild and its faerie angels has sprung up in the villages near the forest over the last ten years, wherever the Prophet Iacob and his white crow are seen
Handri's diplomacy: long private embassies into faerie lands, and rumours that he has met survivors of House Diedne
Caricatures: every resident magus gains a faerie double (a Faerie Friend for the stay); a double can serve as an Arcane Connection, may be kidnapped to strike at its magus, or be sent to Tribunal in a busy magus's place
The lost domus magna: Merinita was the last Roman priestess of Diana, drawn into the Order only by Trianoma's persuasion as her cult died under Charlemagne's Christianisation; Irencillia was never her home, and the House has forgotten where her temple stood or what it was called
Maddenhofen Woods: the covenant closely guards the nearby woods where Tytalus vanished in 807 and a powerful faerie grants a Heart's Desire for a task never yet completed, yet seems to take no vis from them
Two societies: human and fae live side by side; the Primus's caricature is always the monarch of the Faerie Court, at present Queen Rosmert, though whether one shapeshifting ruler or a new one with each Primus is unknown
Gild: the Elder Gild, which Iacob leads
Mundane relations: deliberately none; wanderers are shunned, and the only indirect tie is the God of Truth in the nearby villages

secrets.title: Merinita's true home
secrets.text: Irencillia was not Merinita's home; the true first domus magna, her temple of Diana, is lost and its name forgotten.

secrets.title: Magi and their caricatures
secrets.text: A magus of Irencillia who takes on his caricature's manner grows hard to tell from it, and the two become Arcane Connections to each other.

secrets.title: Who the Prophet is
secrets.text: The Prophet Iacob of the God of Truth is Iacob filius Handri, carrying out the Primus's secret plan to found a religion in the name of the fae; the Quaesitors would be appalled.

secrets.title: Vis at Irencillia
secrets.text: Vis: no sources recorded

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: A caricature's Might grows over time to a cap set by its magus's standing at Irencillia, in politics or in faerie understanding rather than raw power.

covenants.name: Roznov
covenants.summary:
An Autumn covenant in a valley at the edge of the Carpathians on Mount Radhost, in the far east of Moravia on the Hungarian border, founded in 1067 by three Ex Miscellanea magi and admitted to the Rhine Tribunal in 1074. A Magic aura of 4 covers the whole valley, rising to 6 at the crude stone temple on the summit.

It joins two strong and utterly different traditions. One half is the pagan priesthood of the old Slavic god Radegast, Ex Miscellanea magi in Roznov Castle; the other an arch-conservative stronghold of House Tremere in Roznov Fort. The two act independently, their political aims often coinciding, yet one half commonly hears of the other's schemes only from third parties. Seven magi live here in all: Igor Rastvan and his two former apprentices, the three Ex Miscellanea of the Castle; Severicus and two more Tremere, the three of the Fort; and a follower of Tytalus.

Its allegiance looks split between the Rhine, whose Tribunals it attends, and the Tremere-run Transylvanian Tribunal, with which it is thought to keep regular contact, so most Rhine magi distrust it; even so it has grown into a significant political force in the Tribunal. Radegast's worship once centred on his Oracle at Rethra in Pomerania, a covenant of Slavic magus-priests that the Tribunal declared abolished in 1207, but Mount Radhost was always his sacred place.
covenants.what_matters:
Founding suspicion: Roznov could have joined Novgorod or Transylvania but took Durenmar's and Crintera's richer offer; two Transylvanian Tremere joined almost at once in 1074, and some Rhine magi think the whole affair a Tremere ploy for a foothold, with the Ex Miscellanea as dupes
The festival: if Severicus and his filii learned what really happens at the solstice they would be horrified, with charges of diabolism, a pre-emptive March or Wizard War to follow in both Tribunals; unless the Tremere already know, and keep silent for a very good hidden reason
Kingdom of the Slavs: three young companions each believe themselves the rightful heir of a Slavic kingdom and dream of uniting their people against German dominance; the magi encourage all three to spur them on, and Igor has no favourite so long as the kingdom is Radegast's
The slave trade: Ladislaus, a companion of the covenant, buys at the Prague slave market, where the Knights of the Sword sell their Pomeranian captives
Sigils: Severicus holds his own, one of only two Rhine Tremere to do so (the other is Stentorius of Fengheld), and controls about two-fifths of the other Tremere sigils, his two filii's and Hygwald Veritas's of Waddenzee among them
Gilds: every magus belongs to the Ash or the Oak Gild
Mundane relations: the village below the Fort, whose folk guard the only trail up, and the Prague slave market; otherwise not recorded
Covenfolk: about a score of servants and soldiers at the Castle and four times as many at the Fort, rotated continually; many are devotees of Radegast and many bought slaves, who work feverishly hoping a summons uphill means merit rather than expendability; some earn freedom and a place in the turb by a blood oath
Transylvania: the Tremere of the Transylvanian Tribunal across the Hungarian border make their influence felt here

secrets.title: The solstice festival
secrets.text: Every summer solstice the whole covenant and village celebrate Radegast at the summit temple with orgiastic drinking and debauchery, and a few celebrants, usually slaves, are quietly seized and sacrificed inside the temple, seen only by Igor's most loyal servants. It is never spoken of, though most covenfolk guess why people vanish each summer.

secrets.title: The victims' blood
secrets.text: The blood of Roznov's solstice victims yields Corpus vis and feeds the harvest of dozens of pawns.

secrets.title: A hidden keeper
secrets.text: Some supernatural agency seems to keep Roznov's sacrifices secret.

secrets.title: The Tremere of the Fort
secrets.text: The Tremere of the Fort know nothing of the festival's true nature and, unusually for their House, neither discourage nor disapprove of the paganism.

secrets.title: Castle and fort
secrets.text: Roznov Castle, a small twin-towered castle inside a curtain wall two-thirds of the way up Mount Radhost and visible only from its own valley, and Roznov Fort, the fort and village at the foot that command the single pass, are joined by tunnels through the mountain.

secrets.title: Ladislaus at the market
secrets.text: At the Prague market Ladislaus picks out Gifted children among the slaves, who go to Coeris, the Tremere domus magna in Transylvania; the rest are traded or put to work at Roznov.

secrets.title: Vis at Roznov
secrets.text: Vis: dozens of pawns gathered every summer solstice at the Radegast festival in the summit temple, and Corpus vis from blood

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: Or, at the storyguide's choice, the Tremere of the Fort know and hold their tongues for a hidden reason. Ladislaus uses Magic Sensitivity to pick out the Gifted children.

covenants.name: Laniena
covenants.notes:
History. About a century ago a dead magus's vampire hunted out dhampirs, saw them schooled as hunters, then slew them so they would rise as vampires; House Tremere has suffered vampire infiltration after a dhampir magus's death more than once, and now forbids its magi to take dhampir apprentices. The famous hunter Murat of Terezin came to Coeris then, and with Radomir of Tremere cleared the House of every vampire, Murat killing the nest's master himself. The two asked the Tribunal for an oppidum to train hunters, and once Murat had joined House Ex Miscellanea the Praeco agreed.

The founders. Murat brought initiation scripts set down by a Gnostic scholar who had spied on a taltós clan for months; after years of trials he and Radomir learnt to Open a Gifted person to the Hunters' Arts. Radomir named them interfectores, slayers, soon shortened to Fectores. Radomir, a gifted young idealist, studied the necromancers called the Disciples of the Worm, whom he took for heirs of the Dacian necromancers who served Tremere, and his lore of ghosts and the walking dead fitted Murat's lore of vampires. Murat had found that the Arts work on more than vampires. Murat of Terezin trained three apprentices, the first Hermetic Fectores, a new societas of House Ex Miscellanea; the youngest, also named Murat, lives here.

The law. Some magi say training a Gifted child as a Fector makes a delinquent master, since the child is kept from the Hermetic Arts. Laniena answers that trainees are not yet of the Order, so the Code does not protect them, and that each is offered the Order's protection as soon as trained, as Join or Die demands. The Tribunal, that is House Tremere, lets it go on, but could at any time accuse it of the High Crime of robbing a magus of his power.

Hermetic Fectores take one Practice Art as their free Major non-Hermetic Virtue with its Foe Art, a Minor Magical Focus in harming one kind of creature as their free Minor Hermetic Virtue, and Weak Spontaneous Magic as their Major Hermetic Flaw. The Foe Arts the Fectores hold so far are five: Vampire, Werewolf, Ghost, Nightwalker and Witch. Murat's scripts can Open the Hunters' Arts or teach a new Foe Art, but hold nothing for the Practice Arts alone, so no unGifted Fector can be trained.

Covenfolk: a band of elite warriors trained to fight under a Fector's command; Bendis is the ablest of the non-Hermetic Fectores. The book gives no founding year (soon after the purge of about a century ago) and no season.

Story seeds: a character may be one of Murat of Terezin's children, doomed to slay her own father; and if Lexander learns that Murat the Younger has let a vampire live, House Tremere's anger could fall on the whole oppidum.

params.detail: the Fectores
elite warriors trained to fight under a Fector
whether training Gifted children outside the Order is lawful
Murat of Terezin's undeath

covenants.summary:
The 'slaughterhouse': an oppidum at the mouth of Baradla Cave, the largest of the Aggtelek caves in northern Hungary, whose business is training the Fectores, House Tremere's hunters of supernatural foes, who use non-Hermetic Hunters' Arts drawn from the native magic of the Balkans. House Tremere counts the experiment a success. It began as part of the Scholomance and moved here when it became an oppidum of its own.

A few solid houses lean against a tall half-moon wall across the cave mouth, and a dense hedge of black hawthorn, grown on purpose, rings the homes of the magi and covenfolk. Inside are an arena, smithies and carpenters' shops, a chirurgeon and an apothecary's laboratory.

Two of every three Gifted youngsters found or sent here are trained as Fectores, five years under a Fector with Scry, Ban and Slay and three Foe Arts, and then join the Order as Gifted companions of House Ex Miscellanea; the other third become Murat's Hermetic apprentices, Hermetic Fectores. House Tremere forbids Hermetic training for dhampirs, who may still become Fectores. Trainees who prove unreliable never swear the Oath or learn Parma, and are spent on the most dangerous fronts. The Fectores serve House Tremere first, which makes some magi wonder what they are really for.

Its two magi are the filii of its two founders and, unlike them, are always at odds. Anyone keen on the Hunters' Arts is welcome to join.
covenants.what_matters:
Services: trained Fectores for House Tremere, three in the time one apprentice takes
Boon: Hedge Tradition (the Fectores)
Boon: Veteran Fighters (elite warriors trained to fight under a Fector)
Hook: Superiors (House Tremere, on whose sufferance it exists)
Hook: Hermetic Politics (whether training Gifted children outside the Order is lawful)
Hook: Dark Secret (Murat of Terezin's undeath)
Tension: Lexander against Murat the Younger, over the scripts and the training

secrets.title: What Murat of Terezin was
secrets.text: Murat of Terezin was secretly a dhampir himself. On his death he rose as a vampire, and has lasted long enough to become a kukudhi, a vampire that passes as human.

secrets.title: Murat of Terezin's family
secrets.text: Murat of Terezin, risen as a vampire, lives far from Laniena with his fourth mortal wife and has fathered more than twenty children, every one a dhampir.

secrets.title: Murat the Younger's silence
secrets.text: Only Murat the Younger knows that Murat of Terezin lives on as a vampire. He lets the vampire be, because it gives the Fectores a steady stream of Faerie-blooded hunters and has given at least one Gifted child.

secrets.title: Vis at Laniena
secrets.text:
Vis: Baradla Cave, Imaginem and Muto
Vis: Dobsinska Cave, Ignem
Vis: Ochtinska Cave, Rego (the flowers of iron, also lesser enchantment vis)

secrets.title: Library at Laniena
secrets.text: Library: Murat of Terezin's initiation scripts for the Hunters' Arts, which Murat the Younger keeps from Lexander

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The kukudhi: see the Bestiary.

covenants.name: Evredika
covenants.notes:
The book gives no season, and no single aura for an oppidum spread over many sites; the Devil's Throat's 4 is used. Three of its six magi are unnamed.

Story seed: a hunting party led by a noble with a tame white wolf strips all of Evredika's vis sources, and Gigas, the Tremere's ill-hidden cat's paw in the Theban Tribunal, seems the obvious thief. If its protests are honest, who is framing Gigas, and why?

params.detail: its vis, which Gigas has been told not to contest

covenants.summary:
The oppidum of the Cult of Orpheus, a societas of House Ex Miscellanea, spread across the Rhodope Mountains to guard the places of Orpheus's legend, and named for his lost love Eurydice in her Bulgarian form. Its magi live alone in caves, strong houses and hidden towers and seldom visit one another, meeting once a year in a meadow near Gela when the silivriak is in flower. Its sites are Gela, the Devil's Throat, Perperikon and the Rock Womb.

When the Cult joined the Order, its two holiest places, on Lesbos and in the Rhodopes, came into the Hermetic world; the Rhodope cult, decades old by then, became an oppidum in 1001. Its five Orphic magi are foederati; the sixth is the aedile, always a Tremere, whom the House takes care to pick for respect for the Cult's ways and some love of music. Oeagrus drives most of them to ask for a new posting within about ten years.

Approaches to the Theban Tribunal, where Evredika might seem to belong, met scorn from the Theban Jerbiton, who think its music a peasant's jig and its paganism an offence; its magi would rather House Tremere ignored them than House Jerbiton sneered.

By the old Orphic rule women may not enter the cult's holy places and stay in the oppidum's unconsecrated buildings.
covenants.what_matters:
Aura: Magic 4 at the Devil's Throat, 3 at Perperikon
Hook: Contested Resource (its vis, which Gigas has been told not to contest)
Hook: Superiors (the Tremere aedile the House posts there)
Tension: Oeagrus and each Tremere aedile, Yekaterina most of all
Tension: the Cult on Lesbos, which Oeagrus thinks hides Orpheus's head

secrets.title: Oeagrus's treasure
secrets.text: Oeagrus keeps the mummified arm of Orpheus and means to remake the god by grafting his scattered limbs onto his own body.

secrets.title: Vis at Evredika
secrets.text:
Vis: Imaginem from the year's first silivriak flowers
Vis: Corpus, bone fragments washed up in the Devil's Throat (now and then)
Vis: a yearly grant to the teacher at Gela (a Personal Vis Source)

secrets.title: Library at Evredika
secrets.text: Library: no books named

covenants.name: Seuthopolis
covenants.notes:
The book gives no season or founding year. Of its fourteen magi eight are unnamed: four younger Guernicus and four lictors.

Lictors: hoplites sworn to long service, who guard the Quaesitors and do as they say. Here a lictor may claim reasonable help from any cives, socius, foederatus or colona, the Tribunal judging afterwards how much was reasonable by how great and how near the danger was. All the Tribunal's lictors belong to the same body, so all wear the same red and silver sash on formal occasions, fastened with a silver brooch called an astraea, usually enchanted: at least three inches long, a pair of wings spread from a forked lightning bolt, each with its own mark. Saturnino's is set in a six-inch oval studded with gems in the pattern of Virgo. Carrying a copy of a lictor's badge is a serious crime. The mediation and domestic teams' lictors change often, most serving three years; Terencia and Saturnino stay longer. The unnamed hoplites are mostly Tremere, but the Prima has lately moved some of them to Lycaneon, which leaves room for player characters.

The townsfolk are Greeks, Bulgars and mountain Slavs who went where the wars of the other two could not easily reach them; the town has bowed to Byzantine and Bulgarian crowns in turn and is, with the Latin Empire so weak, under Bulgaria in name. They are the oppidum folk least shaped by Hermetic service, without the Tremere virtues of loyalty, letters, arms and merit, and with no former Redcaps among them: like many Western covenants it is staffed by people who fled the world for a different life, and the Quaesitors find their skills, some a little shady, useful.

params.detail: laboratories and libraries in the caverns beneath the town
Transitionalist against Traditional Guernicus

covenants.summary:
A walled town at the Tribunal's southern edge and the base of its Quaesitors and hoplites, on the border with the Theban Tribunal, where its magi fairly well keep the two Tribunals' quarrels from turning into raids across the line. It also looks after the Tribunal's meeting place in the Shipka Pass nearby.

Seuthopolis was the Thracian capital when Rome came, ruled by a priest king of underworld gods whose rites Rome stamped out. A small sect of Verditius magi revived them in a Theban covenant, the Covenant of the Four Divinities, always two senior Verditius and two juniors (one now and then of another House), four being a holy number to the Cabeiri cult. After some friction its members came over to Transylvania as foederati. Over the centuries the cult faded and the oppidum became the Tribunal's seat of justice.

House Guernicus forbids its members to worship the old Thracian gods: three of the House have been removed from office for irrational conduct, and the cult seems the thread linking them. Its initiates take on hubris, as Verditius magi do, and with it a taste for vendettas.

Outwardly it is an ordinary small Bulgarian walled town, owing homage to no lord. Local nobles know nobody has ever taken it, and that those who tried died in ghastly, wondrous ways; the Quaesitors observe that no neighbouring lord has been melted into a puddle of boiling gold since they took over, being subtler than the Verditius, but the tales live on. The magi and their people live about the town in houses like rich merchants'.

Eight Guernicus magi live here with six lictors. Benilda, the leader, keeps research, enchanting and Hermetic law for herself, and sends Vigilia to look into crimes within oppida, Scipio to mediate between oppida, and Caledonia to punish or to investigate by force, each with two lictors and a young Guernicus. For safety only two of the three teams are ever out at once.

In other Tribunals crimes fall between covenants; here, where magi share oppida, they happen within them, and centuries of puzzling over how to investigate magi who live side by side have made these Quaesitors pioneers of their House's Transitionalist movement. Mediation is a common alternative to a case at Tribunal, where the Tremere always win but make enemies doing it.
covenants.what_matters:
Aura: Magic 5 in the caverns; the vault of the libraries is Divine 3
Boon: Hidden Resources (laboratories and libraries in the caverns beneath the town)
Boon: Prestige (no lord has ever taken the town, and the locals know it)
Hook: Hermetic Politics (Transitionalist against Traditional Guernicus)
Hook: Superiors (House Guernicus; the lictors serve House Tremere too)
Duty: keeps the Shipka Pass Tribunal site and calls the yearly Tribunals
Tension: the Valley of the Thracian Kings, which Benilda holds closed against House Tremere
Tension: the Red and Black Libraries, which many think should be burnt
Tension: the old cult of the Cabeiri, banned to Guernicus

secrets.title: Seuthopolis's charter
secrets.text: The town of Seuthopolis's charter from Diocletian is a clever forgery.

secrets.title: Red Spells in the Red Library
secrets.text: Rumour, perhaps true, says the Red Library also holds magic items, seized in investigations and never destroyed, that cast some of the Red Spells; the House might argue they are lawful to own, and lawful to use on hedge wizards, the Orders of Odin and Solomon, and Renounced magi, whom the Code does not protect.

secrets.title: Saturnino's doubts
secrets.text: Saturnino thinks gathering the Red and Black Libraries was a grave mistake.

secrets.title: Library at Seuthopolis
secrets.text: Library: the Red and Black Libraries, Benilda's charge

covenants.name: Tablinum
covenants.notes:
The book gives no season. All four magi are named.

Past Curators:
878-900 Akilina, the first, who found the site in the mid-800s, named her apprentice Potitus to follow her, resigned and vanished in 917; presumed dead, though magi as late as 1137 claim to have met her, or someone using her name, in the regiones.
900-948 Potitus, the first to live there, who opened the storehouse to study.
946-1007 Tiberia, a Tremere general named by Potitus and briefly Curator with him; killed in the Schism War.
1007-1018 Anatolus, also a Tremere general and the first chosen by the Tribunal, known for strange battle magic said to come from Tablinum; killed in Wizard's War.
1018-1020 no Curator.
1020-1027 Silus, charged with infernalism and Marched.
1027-1080 Justius, said to have dismantled several Infernal exhibits and driven demons from many levels.
1080-1102 Scribonius, who wrote the first 'complete' catalogue, then resigned, left House Tremere for House Jerbiton in Thebes, and died in 1137.
1102-1170 Calpurnius, who greatly enlarged the Faerie collection.
1170- Nestor, known for his study of regiones.

How so many sealed regiones came to lie here is unknown; they and their Arcane Connections existed by 900, when the Chronicle first mentions them. One story says a ritual path through a labyrinth once led into all of them, and the founders walked it fixing Arcane Connections and destroying the labyrinth behind them.

Laboratories:
Nestor's true laboratory, in an otherwise empty level, used by Curators for centuries: Greater Feature (orrery), Palatial, Extensive Stores, Specimens, Missing Sanctum Marker, Regio, Impregnable, Predecessor; Size +3, Quality +1, Refinement +3, Safety +1, Upkeep +4, Health +2, Warping +2, Aesthetics +4; Experimentation +1, Teaching +2, Rego +2, Vim +3.
Demetrius's: Greater Feature (desk), Specimens (now Aquam, changed in a few days), Studio (where new acquisitions wait), Cramped; Size 0, Quality -1, Refinement +3, Safety 1, Upkeep 0, Health 0, Warping 0, Aesthetics +4; Texts +4, Aquam +1.
Theodora's: Greater Feature (an ever-boiling cauldron), Faerie Ingredients (faerie rocks), Dirty, Disorganized, Chaotic; Size 0, Quality +1, Refinement +2, Safety -1, Upkeep -1, Health -1, Warping +2, Aesthetics -1; Experimentation +6, Muto +2, Perdo +1, Terram +1.
Theodore's: Greater Feature (a still pool), Superior Heating, Flawless Equipment (dwarf-made), Grand Entranceway, Guard, Highly Organized, Spotless, Undecorated; Size 0, Quality +3, Refinement +3, Safety +3, Upkeep +2, Health +2, Warping 0, Aesthetics +6; Vis Extraction +1, Creo +1, Intellego +2, Ignem +1.
The Vim Distillery, shared: Greater Feature (vis still), Lesser Feature (vis balance), Missing Ingredients (Intellego, Muto, Perdo and Rego Lab Totals halved), Superior Equipment, Greater Focus (vis still), Missing Sanctum Marker, Cramped; Size 0, Quality 0, Refinement 0, Safety -1, Upkeep -3, Health 0, Warping 0, Aesthetics +1; Vis Extraction +10.
The Empty Laboratory, stripped and haunted by a magus murdered there in Wizard's War, with a window open on a void: Vis Source, Empty, Undecorated, Abyss, Haunted; Size 0, Quality 0, Refinement 0, Safety -3, Upkeep -1, Health -1, Warping +2, Aesthetics -3; Perdo +1, Mentem +3.
The guest laboratory in the Scriptorium: Gallery, No Stores, Undecorated; all Characteristics 0 save Upkeep -1 and Safety -1; Teaching +1.

Story seed: a Church delegation arrives while the magi study here. Since 1204 the Latins hold much of Constantinople, and scholars there have read in Greek Church records of Tablinum's hoard of relics; a papal legate comes to learn whether it exists and, if so, to take the relics to Rome. Nestor asks the visiting magi to help him deal with it.

params.detail: the Curators' necklaces of Arcane Connections
rival scholars, and owners of collected objects

covenants.summary:
The Tribunal's museum and storehouse, keeping records, spell texts and artifacts in dozens of regiones in the Danube delta, each hall reached only by Arcane Connection. It was founded in 878, after the Sundering, where so many regiones overlie one another; with the Tribunal held to five covenants it had no standing and no lawful residents, only a place to keep things, until the idea of oppida spread and it remade itself as one, with resident Curators. The Curator holds office for life.

Any Tremere may use the open exhibits, and others usually by the Curator's leave; vandals and thieves, Tremere too, are thrown out for good, at least in theory. Most of the restricted exhibits open to Tremere with good reason and to others now and then, sometimes for a fee. Exhibits are studied as realia, of Source Quality from about 5 (cursory) to 11 or more (unparalleled), lessened when several share one; a rival for an exhibit turns up unless a stress die beats 3, and certamen for love often settles who studies.

Upkeep, checking wards, renewing preserving spells, feeding the Animal exhibit, takes one magus full time, with about a dozen grogs housed in the Scriptorium; the four residents each give it a season a year.

Nestor pays collectors, in vis or access to restricted exhibits (or duplicate objects), for things from a named place or for a named exhibit; grogs and companions are paid in money. Owners, magi among them, may call it theft. Tremere collectors may serve in the vexillation Convectoris-Tablinum.
covenants.what_matters:
Aura: Magic 5 in the Curator's Sanctum; ten listed levels from Infernal 3 to Divine 6
Defence: an Aegis of the Hearth of magnitude 8 round the village palisade
Boon: Regio (dozens of halls reached only by Arcane Connection)
Boon: Hidden Resources (the Curators' necklaces of Arcane Connections)
Hook: Superiors (the Tribunal appoints the Curator; Tremere has rights of access)
Hook: Contested Resource (rival scholars, and owners of collected objects)
Tension: the Dungeon and the Chapel's relics, which many want destroyed or returned
Tension: Nestor's fear of a Tremere plot against him

secrets.title: The Empty Laboratory's window
secrets.text: The Empty Laboratory's void window is a vis source the residents do not know of: now and then frost forms on its sill that can be gathered as Mentem vis before it melts, 2 pawns a season. The ghost knows.

secrets.title: The Curators' necklaces
secrets.text: Nestor keeps most of the Curators' necklaces hidden and carries only the one for the most visited levels.

secrets.title: Nestor's real laboratory
secrets.text: Nestor's real laboratory is in a level of its own.

secrets.title: The Dungeon's excess
secrets.text: Either infernalists with their own Arcane Connections use the Dungeon to hide their cult's paraphernalia, coming and going by Leap of Homecoming, or Hell has got in, and possessed exhibits are summoning more demons into the hall.

secrets.title: What Theodore said
secrets.text: Theodore once told Nestor many exhibits should be destroyed, and lately told Demetrius the Order has outlived its purpose.

secrets.title: Vis at Tablinum
secrets.text: Vis: Vim, extracted from the aura in the shared Vim Distillery (Vis Extraction +10)

secrets.title: Library at Tablinum
secrets.text: Library: the Transylvania Chronicle, the Spell Hall and the exhibits as realia

covenants.name: Old Histria
covenants.notes:
Origins. The Incantation of Lightning, usually thought Druidic, was in fact invented here, as a tool for farming.

The Strange Vis. Folk witches break fevers with a potion of the roof tar of a village's four outermost houses. Hermetic scholars found that on Saint John's Eve the tar of the corner houses of seemingly random villages takes on a little Creo vis, so the tar of many villages is gathered and tested every year. Odd enough that it forms only in the Dominion, and only when the four houses' tar is kept unmixed and complete; odder still, it began to appear in Istrian villages once Histria joined, as if it spreads with the Tribunal. Some magi think whatever makes it knows the Tribunal's border; others scoff.

The vis register. Most Transylvanian magi may not sell vis or enchanted items abroad; only the socii, the Praeco, the Tremere Primus, and those acting for them may. Sales need not pass through Old Histria: matching letters, notarised by a Quaesitor, suffice. The Praeco's agents may bid for anything of interest to the Tribunal, which can raise sellers' prices and hurts buyers of rarities, while buyers of common vis can compare the speculative promissory notes on file with Old Histria's vis-trading master. The same bar on sales covers many magical beasts, letting House Tremere, always after breeding stock for war, buy exports first and bid on imports.

Mansiones. Mercere rest houses, a day apart on the main roads between oppida, some secret and for the Order alone, others half-public and open to merchants and clergy. They are not oppida, having no resident cives. Small towns of the founders' descendants have grown round the biggest; since their holders owe the King of Hungary no fealty this is no trouble yet, but some heirs are marrying into the lesser nobility.

The Redcap families. Only Gifted Mercere vote in this Tribunal; in return the Redcaps have been let multiply. An oppidum can have a 'Redcap' each week if it likes; whole families tour as players, carrying messages and swaying the common folk with their plays; retired Redcaps keep businesses in most towns; magi's spouses are sometimes named Redcaps to give them rights under Hermetic law. They think of themselves as one big, fond, odd family of near-magicians, and call each other cousin. House Mercere formally counts only fifteen Redcaps in Transylvania; the Tremere reckon about forty-five are needed (two for each major oppidum, the House's staff, and the retired, trainees and honorary members). The children of several kinds of local vampire make good Redcaps, and the House seeks them out; those not taken become grogs.

Harco. House Mercere has only some 150 members, and the Tremere wish to add thirty-five Transylvanian Redcaps looks to Harco like a lever on the House. The local Mercere side with the Prima, see no reason their children should not all be Redcaps, and are unmoved by a recluse in Piedmont. The present truce: Harco accepts the heads of the Redcap families as members, and the rest as the House's agents, whom Transylvanian magi treat and call Redcaps. The Roman Mercere find the vampire-blooded ones creepy and recognise none of them, and Redcaps proud of heroic blood despise them, though the bloodcaps of the Celtic lands, faerie-blooded themselves, get on with them. If someone on the Roman side pushes for control the truce may fail; player magi could broker a new one.

Stories. The Mercere House's duties are the usual ones (recruiting, training, supporting and rescuing Redcaps), but at this scale whole troupes of players or shiploads of messengers vanish, and every oppidum then gets a formal plea for help that it would be shameful to ignore. New coloniae in interesting country may find a small Mercere school bolted on; trainee Redcaps are always trouble. Histrian magi are the usual envoys to the domus magnae of the west (Harco, Magvillis, Valnastium, the Cave of Twisting Shadows), always at least two, one Tremere and one not; a saga of envoys reaches Autumn covenants, royal courts and Arab, Cuman and Hebrew sorcerers.

The Venice lodging. Three Gifted members live at the chapter house in Venice, in the Roman Tribunal, Merit of Tremere among them; a Mercere's Portal from Old Histria to it has been mooted for years (see the Tribunal's docket).

Vigilia of Seuthopolis may not be given cases touching the Histrian oppida, after her censure. The book gives no founding year and no season. Of the unnamed magi, one is Gifted and in Istria and two are in Venice.

params.detail: the Mercere House: Redcaps, the vis register, the Tribunal's envoys

covenants.summary:
The elder of the two Mercere oppida of Istria, and the Tribunal's Mercere House: its gatekeeper to the west, its chief negotiator with foreigners, and a recruiting ground, school and market for the Redcap families. It sits in a much-rebuilt hill fort above Pazin in a Magic aura of 7. House Tremere bases its merchant navy and the Tribunal's diplomats here and at Shrouded Bay; some say the House's spies in the Roman Tribunal are run from here too, which the Tremere deny.

Histria was a covenant of the Roman Tribunal, claiming the whole peninsula through its name. Worn down by that Tribunal's endless politics, its magi came over to Transylvania as foederati, bringing their outpost on Cres with them. The Tribunal has since made the camp, where socii now dominate, the place of record for every sale of vis and enchanted items.

Its members are the same as Shrouded Bay's: eight Gifted magi between the two, three more who live at the chapter house in Venice, and many unGifted Redcaps, who are full members and vote in the oppidum's own ballots. Magi of the two camps often add Adiran, of the Adriatic, to their names, which the swarm of same-named Redcaps makes useful.

It is roomy enough for formal gatherings and for the Redcap families' many projects, but cold and stormy in winter; the strong aura is what keeps researchers there through the sleet.
covenants.what_matters:
Register: the place of record for all sales of vis and magic items in the Tribunal, with the master of vis trading's list of promissory notes
Laboratory: Accursius's suite and excellent laboratory, used by Volante
Items: the House's cache of magic items, and the potent items guarding the fort
Boon: Aura (Magic 7); Fortified site (a layered hill fort)
Hook: Hermetic Services (the Mercere House: Redcaps, the vis register, the Tribunal's envoys)
Hook: Harsh winters
Tension: Harco recognises few of the Tribunal's Redcaps, and none who are vampire-blooded
Tension: the proposed Mercere's Portal to the Venice chapter house

secrets.title: Pahniro's frailty
secrets.text: Pahniro's frailty is an act: he was a hoplite for twenty years and has killed three magi in single combat.

secrets.title: Pahniro the spymaster
secrets.text: Pahniro may well be the House's spymaster for the Roman Tribunal.

secrets.title: Vis at Old Histria
secrets.text:
Vis: the mercury pool, a rich Terram source (a child dipped in it gains Visions and often worse Flaws)
Vis: the truffles of the northern Istrian woods (Herbam), sought by faeries, worth their weight in gold
Vis: the Strange Vis, a little Creo in the roof tar of the four corner houses of random villages on Saint John's Eve, collected Tribunal-wide

secrets.title: Library at Old Histria
secrets.text: Library: no books named; the Mercere House's records

covenants.name: Shrouded Bay
covenants.notes:
Naval stories. The Adriatic is the safer of the Tribunal's two coasts and one of the world's busiest trade lanes. The fleets have their works here and in a hidden cache somewhere in the southern Dalmatian isles, Leviathan in the Tremere plans (see the hidden fortresses). Trade, piracy and salvage stories can draw on City & Guild. Phillip of Lycaneon, who builds naval parts, is often here tinkering.

The book gives no founding year and no season. One Gifted member is unnamed.
covenants.summary:
The younger Histrian oppidum, a large villa on the Venetian island of Cres, hidden by The Shrouded Glen in a Magic aura of 6. Old Histria's magi set up a chapter house here to guard the island's storm-washed Rego vis, too far from the fort to protect, against raids by Transylvanian Tremere; when Histria joined the Tribunal, the settlement became an oppidum too. In law it stands alone, but the two camps share their members and are close allies.

Most Histrian magi like it better than Old Histria, above all in winter, and Accursius, the chief Mercere, lives here. It holds the support works for the small Mercere and Tremere trading fleets, and its aedile, Placido, runs the Tremere fleet from it.
covenants.what_matters:
Laboratory: Accursius's, less good than his suite at Old Histria
Fleet: the support base of the Mercere and Tremere trading fleets
Boon: Aura (Magic 6); Hidden (The Shrouded Glen)
Hook: Ruled by Venice
Tension: Leviathan, the secret base in the southern Dalmatian isles, is to be opened if Shrouded Bay seems unsafe in war
Tension: the Grave of Aspytrus and its serpents, on the island

secrets.title: Vis at Shrouded Bay
secrets.text:
Vis: the well of blood, a major Corpus source, used for the Redcaps' longevity rituals
Vis: Rego washed up on one beach after storms among ships' wreckage, accruing through the year

secrets.title: Library at Shrouded Bay
secrets.text: Library: no books named

covenants.name: Lycaneon
covenants.notes:
Gold is worth little. Grogs with magic tools mined the mountain's gold out in the oppidum's first decades. The Tremere learned by owning more of it than anyone that gold is only worth what you can spend, and few in Mythic Europe can pay a high price for it; silver spends more easily but floods an economy (as happened lately in Stonehenge), and ruin breeds poverty, and poverty diabolism, so the House now urges laws limiting how much wealth magi may make. Gold is soft and heavy, poor stuff for enchantment; silver at least tempts or repels local faeries, so it can be traded for vis or made into weapons. Few other Houses see it, but the mines ended Tremere's hunger for territory: land is worth only the work of its people, so the House grows by having more magi doing what it wants.

Look and feel. Tremere designed it before Gothic building, so its grandeur is in texture, ornament and size: walls carved with battle scenes, his sayings and Roman motifs, and gold everywhere, which modern Tremere think vulgar. None of his statues is life size: in the Grand Refectory a twelve-foot Tremere rests his hand on a cowed golden dragon. Renovation has never been a priority.

The people. The covenfolk and the little towns around descend from the miners Tremere brought; generations under the House have made them unlike any other folk. They speak a Latin dialect, mostly read and write, and reckon like merchants. Each village elects three leaders, who meet in a council they call a Tribunal over borders, trade and crime, and women often lead. Their fighters are mountain skirmishers with bow, axe and short sword, retired grogs settle among them, and the descendants of the specialists keep their crafts, so many curious wares are made here, which Redcaps carry round the Tribunal.

The wolves. Tremere took the mountain's lead wolf as his familiar, and many of his line seek a white wolf in turn; the House's pack loyalty and shared rearing of the young may have come to him through that bond. The wolves say they descend from men changed in a rite and left in wolf shape when the Oracles fell silent. Now and then a cub is born a throwback, human on summer's first night, its midpoint and its last; trained, such children master the change and serve the House. Wolves who wed humans have children more given than most to nightwalking in wolf shape.

A refuge.
