cases.against: A papal legate lodged with the Teutonic Knights
cases.charge: Legends of the Devil's School have reached Rome, and a legate has come to look into the Scholomance and its supposed diabolism, staying with the Teutonic Order while he builds his case. So far he has only hearsay, since only magi and former pupils know anything real; the Tribunal must decide how to keep it so without breaking the Code.

rulings.title: The five legal covenants
rulings.says: After the Sundering a Grand Tribunal capped the Tribunal at five named covenants: Coeris, Domostron, Asclepius, Diodorus and Pannonia. All five have since moved or changed how they admit members, but in law they still stand, and no new covenant can be added. A body of outsiders that joins the Tribunal enters Pannonia. The Tremere do not ask for the limit to be lifted, lest it stir old fears, and no one else gains by asking.

rulings.title: Privileges
rulings.says: Every resident magus holds a privilege: a written agreement with the Praeco, on the Tribunal's behalf, that sets the magus's place in Transylvanian society. A Quaesitor witnesses it and it is read into the Peripheral Code at a meeting. There are five broad kinds, one for each legal covenant, but each is bargained for, and terms may be added later as reward or punishment. A magus may leave the Tribunal freely, returning what he was paid for unfinished work; one who goes with great items, much vis or other treasures is pursued by the Tremere.

rulings.title: Cives (Coeris)
rulings.says: Every Tremere belongs to Coeris, and may resign and rejoin at will. Other magi may be made cives as a mark of the Tribunal's esteem. A cives may draw on House Tremere's aid, send a Tremere proxy to the House's Decennial, stand for any office including Praeco, raise apprentices, move between oppida (if not Tremere), and wear black or grey at meetings; where cives are the larger group of an oppidum they choose its aedile from the others. In return a cives must live as the Tremere admire: cooperate, work usefully, muster for war and pay taxes.

rulings.title: Socii (Domostron)
rulings.says: The socii are allies of other Houses treated much as if they were Tremere: nearly all the Quaesitores, Redcaps and dedicated hoplites, who are socii unless they are cives. They may hold any office but Praeco, raise an apprentice, draw dedicated resources and crisis taxes for their work, and wear designs like Decorations; where they are the larger group they name three candidates for aedile and the Praeco picks one. They must do their duty or renegotiate, give no one a fair cause for Wizard's War (as the Praeco judges), ask leave to found an oppidum, stand in as aediles when none can be found, and wear their badges at meetings.

rulings.title: Coloniae (Asclepius)
rulings.says: The coloniae are young magi from other Tribunals settled under close terms to open up neglected corners of the land. They are promised aid in war or disaster, the resources named in their privilege and a share of new ones found. They may not choose their aedile, seek any office but aedile, call themselves archmagi, take apprentices without leave, invite other magi in (save Quaesitores, Redcaps and hoplites), behave scandalously, or wear what looks like a Decoration they have not earned. At meetings they go unshod (sandals and slippers are now allowed) and may eat no aphrodisiac, from shellfish and truffles to carrots and pepper.

rulings.title: Hospites (Diodorus)
rulings.says: The hospites, the Tribunal's guests, are magi hired to practise a skill for House Tremere, and most live at Lycaneon. They are paid fairly, use what their task is given, escape many taxes, are protected if War is declared on them, and are not called to Wizard's Marches. They must ask leave before seeking office, taking an apprentice, binding a familiar, making a talisman, founding or changing oppidum, voting for a particular aedile, or wearing what looks like a Decoration; a privilege may grant some of these in advance, for less pay.

rulings.title: Foederati (Pannonia)
rulings.says: The foederati are magi of covenants that left neighbouring Tribunals for shelter here, and each keeps the customs written into its privilege, offensive to the Tremere or not, so long as it breaks neither the Code nor the Tribunal's peace. They keep the resources they held when they joined, train apprentices (the eldest is taken on as a foederatus too), move oppidum with notice and may stand for any office. They need leave to drop the duties their privilege names, which only the Praeco and the magus together can change, to use the title archmagus, found oppida, invite magi in, or trade vis or items with outsiders other than the socii. Should Pannonia ever lack outsiders, some magi of other covenants join it automatically, so it never lapses.

rulings.title: The leaders of the legal covenants
rulings.says: To keep the Tribunal whole after the Sundering, Tremere granted concessions to the other covenants' leaders, now paid by the Tribunal. Asclepius's members elect a leader each year, who is invited to Coeris for the Triumph of Asclepius: sixteen pawns of vis, three pounds of pure gold, six books of his choosing copied from a certain library, a fine dinner and lesser tokens, in return for minor duties to the other leaders that take about two seasons. Magi of any covenant, and non-residents, may hold it. The hospites elect their leader every seven years, with the Praeco's approval, for a smaller yearly payment. Domostron is led by the senior Quaesitor and Pannonia by the Orphic cult of the south, whose members long ago sold their concessions to the chief Mercere.

rulings.title: Oppida
rulings.says: Every magus must belong to an oppidum in some sense, and keep broadly aware of what its other members are doing. An oppidum must have at least two members, at least one of them cives, and may not be made up wholly of one House, so in practice each has a Tremere and someone who is not.

rulings.title: Aediles
rulings.says: Each oppidum has an aedile, the odd member set there to keep House Tremere from corruption and the others from treason; where cives and non-cives are equal in number it has two. Aediles have no set duties, but may demand an urgent audience with the Praeco and the chief Quaesitor, and the Quaesitores treat an aedile's disappearance, or War declared on one, gravely.

rulings.title: Decorations
rulings.says: The Tribunal honours service with five Decorations, worn as jewellery or embroidery on a magus's robes, never awarded twice to the same magus; a higher one replaces a lower. The Laurel goes to the magus who leads a campaign against a foe that could destroy the Order (no one now wears it); the Myrtle to the general of a lesser campaign of more than one magical battle; the Oak to one who plans such a campaign without fighting in it; the Grass to a magus who saves other magi from death, first given to the defenders of covenants against the Diedne; and the Parsley for the killing blow on a magus the Tribunal has cast out.

rulings.title: The Praeco
rulings.says: The Praeco is chosen by vote, not by age, and needs the Prima of Tremere's approval to take office and her goodwill to keep it. He has wider powers than Praecones elsewhere, ceded by the House slowly and reversibly. The Praeco appoints the Tribunal's envoys and asks magi to settle when the Prima wants an oppidum founded.

rulings.title: Taxes and stipends
rulings.says: The Praeco gathers taxes for the projects each meeting assigns him, and the cives, socii, coloniae and some foederati must give reasonable aid to them. A large vis source is reserved for his use, once meant for the upkeep of the meeting site's wards, which the Quaesitores now see to. He also collects the stipends the Peripheral Code sets for the Redcaps and Quaesitores, and his Redcaps deliver them, so the Tremere can see what is claimed without spying and no one can call it a bribe from the House.

rulings.title: Promissory notes
rulings.says: Before he could tax, the Praeco borrowed against his reserved vis by issuing notes promising payment, and he still issues them for trade and diplomacy. Old notes never redeemed pass from hand to hand as a currency of great value. Forging one is a crime, held to be fraud aimed at robbing a magus of the vis that is his power.

rulings.title: Annual emergency Tribunals
rulings.says: Elsewhere the Quaesitores call emergency Tribunals when they must; in Transylvania House Guernicus calls one every year at the Tribunal site, to give swifter justice and accept newly trained apprentices sooner. A group of Tremere advocates holds proxies for every Transylvanian Tremere, so the vote always suits the House, which uses these meetings to keep its allies content and often concedes more than the votes require.

rulings.title: Wizard's War
rulings.says: Magi keep their right under the Code to declare War, but the Tribunal strongly prefers that wizards fight wizards only in Marches voted at an emergency Tribunal. Quarrels go first to mediation by the Quaesitores or the Prima's people, and then to certamen; private Wars are very rare.

rulings.title: Certamen in place of War
rulings.says: A challenge to certamen says the challenger would kill his rival if he were less civilised. The winner is treated as having spared a life he could have taken, the loser lives by his mercy, and the winner has the right to strike the loser once in the face. Certamen rules are otherwise the Definitive Edition's.

rulings.title: Certamen for love
rulings.says: Most duels are fought for love, as sport or over small matters. Before two witnesses the Tribunal could question, the duellists declare that it is for love, the stake, how it is won if not by yielding (first sound blow, first wound or unconsciousness are common), forgiveness in advance for any hurt, and that the loser yields. They may not strike a blow at the end, use vis, gamble basely, wager an officer's duties, duel naked or drunk, use spells or items (or let onlookers) to sway the result, couple during the duel, or challenge one worn down by an earlier duel.

rulings.title: Dealings with outsiders
rulings.says: Many oppida may not make treaties with foreign covenants or Tribunals. Trading arrangements with outsiders need either a place in the Peripheral Code or the Praeco's approval, witnessed by a Quaesitor; the Praeco's appointees speak for the Tribunal abroad.

rulings.title: Settlers and Gifted children
rulings.says: No magus may bring a Gifted child into the Tribunal or invite a magus to settle. He may instead ask the Praeco to do it, which lets the Tremere govern how many magi live here.

rulings.title: Sales of vis and enchanted items
rulings.says: Only the Praeco, the Prima of Tremere, the socii and their agents may sell vis or enchanted items to outsiders. Old Histria is the registry for every such sale in the Tribunal; the goods need not go there, as matching letters notarised by a Quaesitor suffice. The Praeco's people may bid for anything of interest, and buyers of common vis may consult the list of notes kept by the master of the vis trade at Old Histria.

rulings.title: Magical animals
rulings.says: Magical animals may not be exported without licence, which lets House Tremere, ever seeking breeding stock for war, buy first on exports and bid alongside on imports. Selling through the Redcaps is lawful but recorded.

rulings.title: One name to a Tremere
rulings.says: No two Tremere magi in the Tribunal may share a name, so that the House's records can tell each apart; a maga who arrives bearing a name already held may have to defend it by certamen.

rulings.title: Amaranth
rulings.says: Amaranth, a faerie flower whose vis gives magi pleasant visions, addiction and Warping, is destroyed wherever it is found in Transylvania.

rulings.title: Lictors
rulings.says: Lictors, magi sworn to long service as hoplites, guard the Quaesitores and follow their orders. They may call on any cives, socius, foederatus or colonus for reasonable aid, the Tribunal judging afterwards what was reasonable for the danger. All belong to one legal covenant and so wear the same red and silver sash, pinned with a winged silver brooch, the astraea, each with its own variation. Carrying a copy of a lictor's badge is a serious crime.

rulings.title: The zenodochia
rulings.says: The Tribunal keeps safehouses for sick or wounded magi along its roads, and wants them used. Taking vis from one is a Low Crime, though a magus who cannot repay is usually let work off the debt for the Tribunal; damaging or destroying one on purpose is a High Crime, while one who repairs accidental damage unasked is not prosecuted. Items and casting tablets must stay; vis and supplies used must be replaced.

rulings.title: The Curantis
rulings.says: Each meeting elects a Curantis to serve until the next, usually the single candidate the elders agree on beforehand; no one may serve two terms running. He tours the zenodochia for about a season a year, repairs them, must build at least one new one in his term, and has a Quaesitor's powers in cases touching them. He is paid generously in vis and may draw on the Tribunal's stores. His Notary, chosen by the previous Curantis and often a Redcap, serves as his aedile.

rulings.title: The Curator of Tablinum
rulings.says: The Curator, who keeps the museum oppidum of Tablinum, holds office for life. The Transylvania Chronicle kept there is the authoritative record of the Tribunal's history and its rulings.

rulings.title: Mercere votes
rulings.says: By the terms of their covenant with the Tribunal, only Gifted Mercere vote at its meetings; in exchange the Tribunal lets the families of unGifted Redcaps grow as large as they like.

rulings.title: Hedge wizards and Laniena
rulings.says: The Code's Join or Die provision applies to Gifted hedge wizards. The Tribunal's policy lets Laniena train Gifted children as Fectores, hunters who are not Hermetic magi, on the ground that trainees are outside the Order and so outside the Code; once trained, each is offered the Order's protection. Laniena knows it lasts only on sufferance, since the High Crime of depriving a magus of his magic could be charged whenever the Tremere wished.

diary.title: The Order of Hermes founded
diary.details: The Order is founded. The Transylvania Chronicle, kept in Tablinum's exhibit hall, begins its record with this year, though sceptics note how little it says of House Tremere's beginnings.

diary.title: A skirmish at the Shipka Pass
diary.details: In the Order's first years the Founder Tremere fights a band of Theban magi at the Shipka Pass, the best road through Bulgaria's mountains. A regio lies beside the battlefield: some say Tremere knew of it and laid his ambush from it, others that a Twilight born of the fight's strain made it. For long afterwards House Tremere and the Theban covenants meet there to reflect and to sign their treaties. (The book gives no year.)

diary.title: Krum takes Hungary and Transylvania
diary.details: Khan Krum the Conqueror adds the lands of Hungary and Transylvania to the First Bulgarian Empire.

diary.title: Tremere wears the Roman dragon's face
diary.details: Early in the ninth century, when dragon raids flare up in defiance of the Pax Draconis, the Founder Tremere takes the shape of Fetillusclaviceps, the Roman dragon who made the peace, and puts down the rebels. He never speaks of it, and whatever record of his reasons existed was lost in the Sundering. (The book gives no exact year.)

diary.title: Death of Krum
diary.details: Krum, who had beaten two Byzantine emperors in battle and laid siege to Constantinople, dies suddenly, and no one knows quite how.

diary.title: The Sundering
diary.details: Tremere's bid to master the Order ends in the Sundering. No longer trusting his domus magna at what is now Lycaneon, he moves his seat, and its name, to Coeris in Maramures, where the Covenant of Asclepius then stood; Lycaneon stays the House's manufactory. His successor Albanus turns the Order's anger at Tremere's memory into a means of binding the House together. A Grand Tribunal caps the Tribunal at five named covenants, Coeris, Domostron, Asclepius, Diodorus and Pannonia, which still exist in law though every one has since moved or changed its membership. To keep the others from seceding, Tremere grants concessions to their leaders, and the covenants bind one another by contract; the Triumph of Asclepius is still paid from them.

diary.title: Akilina finds Tablinum's site
diary.details: The maga Akilina comes upon a place in the Danube delta where many regiones lie one over another, the future site of Tablinum. (The book says only the middle of the ninth century.)

diary.title: Tablinum founded
diary.details: In the years after the Sundering Tablinum is founded as a storehouse for artifacts, with Akilina its first Curator. Since the Tribunal may hold only five covenants, it has no official standing and no recognised residents until the custom of oppida spreads, when it remakes itself as an oppidum with Curators who live there. Its founders are said to have walked a ritual path through the regiones, fixing an Arcane Connection to each level and destroying the path behind them.

diary.title: Cyril and Methodius's church in Bulgaria
diary.details: Boris I, the first Christian khan of Bulgaria, baptised Michael, welcomes the mission of Saints Cyril and Methodius, from which the Bulgarian Church takes its descent.

diary.title: Potitus opens Tablinum
diary.details: Akilina names her apprentice Potitus her successor and resigns. The first Curator to make his home at Tablinum, he opens what had been a closed storehouse to study. By this year the Chronicle already mentions its regiones and the Arcane Connections that reach them.

diary.title: Akilina vanishes
diary.details: Tablinum's first Curator disappears and is presumed dead.

diary.title: Symeon's Bulgarian Church
diary.details: Symeon, son of Boris and the first Bulgarian ruler to style himself tsar rather than khan, makes the Bulgarian Church autonomous. By the peace of 927 the patriarch of Constantinople accepts its independence, and it soon has a patriarch of its own.

diary.title: Tiberia shares the Curatorship; Saint Ivan of Rila dies
diary.details: Potitus appoints Tiberia, a Tremere general, as his successor, and for a short time the two share the office; Potitus's term ends in 948. In the same year the hermit, healer and mystic Ivan Rilski dies; his body, still uncorrupted, now lies at Tarnovo, and he is Bulgaria's patron saint.

diary.title: Evredika instituted
diary.details: The Cult of Orpheus had worshipped in the Rhodope mountains for decades as an informal cult, and when it joined the Order its sacred sites there became Hermetic ground. In this year Evredika, named for Eurydice in the Bulgarian tongue, becomes a formal oppidum.

diary.title: The zenodochia devised
diary.details: During the Schism War the Tremere generals plan a network of tiny hidden hospitals, the zenodochia, reasoning that one hospital oppidum would be found and destroyed in time, while a web of small ones could not be, and that no single captured magus would know more than a few of them. Hundreds are planned; many are never built. (The book gives no year.)

diary.title: Tiberia falls; Anatolus Curator
diary.details: Tiberia is killed in the Schism War. Anatolus, also a Tremere general, succeeds her, the first Curator of Tablinum chosen by the Tribunal rather than by the one before. He becomes known for strange battle magic, said to come from Tablinum's halls.

diary.title: Kezdö Válasz founded
diary.details: Norsius of House Tremere, more scholar than soldier, founds Primum Responsans, better known by its Hungarian name Kezdö Válasz, to guard the Tribunal's borders in the Schism War. Taking Trajan's Wall as his model, he builds a few forts in magic auras near the frontier, each with two magi who study between alarms; his own first fort stands in the ruins of Sarmizegethusa, Decebalus's palace. The war never reaches Transylvania, and the forts are never tested. Later his filius Gasparus spreads the forts across the whole Tribunal and has each pair of magi move to a new one after every Tribunal meeting.

diary.title: Bulgaria falls to Byzantium; Anatolus slain
diary.details: The First Bulgarian Empire, founded by Asparukh's Bulgars, falls to Byzantine rule. The Bulgarian Church loses its independence, is reduced to an archbishopric at Ohrid and filled with Greek clergy. In the same year the Curator Anatolus dies in a Wizard's War, and Tablinum has no Curator for two years.

diary.title: Silus Curator
diary.details: Silus becomes Curator of Tablinum.

diary.title: Silus Marched; Justius Curator
diary.details: Silus is accused of infernalism and Marched. His successor Justius is said to have taken apart a number of infernal exhibits and driven demons out of many of Tablinum's regio levels during his long tenure.

diary.title: Scribonius Curator
diary.details: Scribonius becomes Curator of Tablinum and writes the first catalogue of its exhibits to claim completeness.

diary.title: Croatia offered to Hungary
diary.details: The Trpimirović line of Croatian kings ends in a feeble quarrel between brothers, and the nobles of the north invite Ladislaus I of Hungary to rule. Croatia has been a vassal principality of Hungary ever since.

diary.title: Villages bound to their churches
diary.details: A Church council in Hungary rules that a village with a church may not move far from it, beginning the end of the Magyars' wandering villages.

diary.title: Jeremiah enters the ghostly castle
diary.details: The Order had long known of a phantom castle in the Carpathians; this year Jeremiah of Tremere solves the secret of its regio and becomes the first magus to enter the tower. One inhabitant waits there, and he has not aged since.

diary.title: Coloman's law: witches do not exist
diary.details: King Coloman the Learned of Hungary decrees that, as witches do not exist, no one may be tried for witchcraft. The Quaesitors look into it as discreetly as they can but find no magus behind it, and the law still stands. (The book says only the eleventh century; Coloman reigned from 1095 to 1116.)

diary.title: Scribonius leaves; Calpurnius Curator
diary.details: Scribonius resigns as Curator, quits House Tremere and joins House Jerbiton in the Theban Tribunal. His successor Calpurnius greatly enlarges Tablinum's Faerie collection.

diary.title: Murat and Radomir purge the vampires; Laniena founded
diary.details:
The vampire of a dead magus hunts out dhampirs, has them trained and then kills them to make more vampires, the latest of the infiltrations that have dogged House Tremere. The famed hunter Murat of Terezin comes to Coeris and with the young Radomir of Tremere clears every vampire from the House; Murat kills the nest's master himself. The two ask the Tribunal for an oppidum to train hunters, and once Murat joins House Ex Miscellanea the Praeco agrees. Working from old initiation scripts a Gnostic scholar took down while spying on a taltós clan, they learn after years of trials to Open the Gifted to the Hunters' Arts; Radomir calls them interfectores, soon shortened to Fectores. Laniena begins as part of the Scholomance and later moves to the Aggtelek caves. House Tremere now forbids its magi to take a dhampir as apprentice. (The book says about a hundred years ago.)

Secrets
Murat of Terezin was himself a dhampir, and became a vampire when he died. He survives as a kukudhi, a vampire passing as a man, living far from Laniena with his fourth mortal wife and fathering dhampirs. Only Murat the Younger knows, and lets him be for the hunters his children give Laniena.

diary.title: Coeris takes the Scholomance
diary.details: Thirty years after Jeremiah's entry Coeris claims the ghostly tower and makes it a mansio for the Redcaps of the Tribunal's north. Within a few years it is training Redcaps, and soon after mundanes of use to House Tremere.

diary.title: Akilina seen again; Scribonius dies
diary.details: Magi studying at Tablinum report meeting Akilina, or someone who claims to be her, in the maze of its regiones, two centuries after she vanished. Scribonius, the former Curator, dies this year.

diary.title: Stefan Nemanja serves the emperor
diary.details: Stefan Nemanja, a Serbian prince of modest beginnings and then a Byzantine vassal, helps the emperor in his war on Hungary.

diary.title: The Roman dragon's last sighting
diary.details:
Fetillusclaviceps, keeper of the Pax Draconis, is seen for the last time. He had shown himself only half a dozen times in three centuries, never to a magus, and his lair has never been found. (The book says only more than fifty years before 1220.)

Secrets
Some Tremere wonder whether the later sightings were the dragon at all, or magi of their own House repeating the Founder's disguise.

diary.title: Pantino
diary.details: Stefan Nemanja turns on his Byzantine overlord and beats an imperial army at the Battle of Pantino.

diary.title: Nestor Curator
diary.details: Nestor succeeds Calpurnius as Curator of Tablinum, an office held for life, and becomes known for his research into regiones.

diary.title: Nemanja taken to Constantinople
diary.details: Nemanja allies with Venice, Hungary and German princes to throw off Byzantine rule, but Serbian feuds, a Venetian mutiny and plague wreck the campaign. Manuel Komnenos invades Raška, besieges Ras and carries Nemanja to Constantinople in chains; against all expectation the two become friends, and Nemanja returns as the emperor's strategos and the sole lawful ruler of the Serbs.

diary.title: The Asen brothers free Bulgaria
diary.details: Three brothers, Teodor Petar, Ivan Asen and Kaloyan, lead the Bulgarians out of Byzantine rule and found the Second Bulgarian Empire. Their origins are a mystery, perhaps Bulgarian, perhaps Vlach or Cuman, and their inherited gift for swaying crowds troubles the Order. Cuman tribes shelter the rebel princes after their first army is beaten and supply the core of the next.

diary.title: The Teutonic Order founded at Acre
diary.details: Barbarossa died in 1189 and most of his German nobles went home, but a faithful few stay for the siege of Acre. Ill and neglected by the French and English Hospitallers, crusaders from Bremen and Lübeck found a hospital order for Germans, backed by Duke Friedrich of Swabia, and Pope Celestine III approves it. (The book says some twenty years before 1220.)

diary.title: Nemanja abdicates
diary.details: Stefan Nemanja retires and hands Serbia to his second son, Stefan, passing over the eldest, Vukan.

diary.title: Kaloyan tsar
diary.details: Kaloyan begins his reign and restores the Bulgarian Empire; his Cuman bride seals an alliance with the nomads that must be renewed by rite each summer. New German crusaders reach the Holy Land and find the Teutonic hospital flourishing.

diary.title: The Teutonic Knights take up the sword
diary.details: Seeing the crusader kingdom's border forts badly manned, the newcomers decide the Teutonic brothers, former knights, can fight as well as nurse, and the pope gives the Order a new charter as a military order.

diary.title: Death of Stefan Nemanja
diary.details: Nemanja dies, and holy oil begins to flow from his tomb, so the people call him the Myrrh-flowing.

diary.title: Saint Simeon; Eudocia driven out
diary.details: Less than a year after his death the Eastern Church canonises Stefan Nemanja. Stefan II accuses his first wife, Eudocia Angelina, daughter of Emperor Alexios Angelos and mother of five of his children, of adultery and drives her from Serbia. About this time Hungary stops exporting slaves, probably as part of the king's plan to people the kingdom's edges.

diary.title: Zadar sacked
diary.details: Crusaders raid and destroy Zadar, Croatia's richest port and a possession of the King of Hungary, and little is done to dislodge the Venetians.

diary.title: Tarnovo's primate; the Zadar zenodochium
diary.details: Pope Innocent III names the Archbishop of Tarnovo primate of all Bulgaria and Wallachia, tying the Asens' church to Rome, though Ohrid stays Orthodox. Soon after the violence at Zadar, House Tremere builds a zenodochium in a regio within a magical lacuna in the city and staffs it with a skilled surgeon and his assistants. Some months later the House loses touch with them, and the regio itself seems to vanish.

diary.title: Constantinople falls; Adulio joins Kezdö Válasz
diary.details: Constantinople falls to the Latins, and the Latin Church soon controls much of the city; the magi of Thebes learn what crusading armies can do. Two months later Adulio of House Tremere, just out of his apprenticeship, joins Kezdö Válasz to keep the same fate from Transylvania. In Serbia Vukan's resentment breaks into civil war against his brother Stefan II, who wins but cannot take any of the lost Byzantine lands. A loyal Croatian noble wrests Zadar back from the crusaders.

diary.title: Baldwin captured; Venice takes the coast
diary.details: Tsar Kaloyan captures Emperor Baldwin of the Latin Empire, who is held in the tower above Tarnovo's Frankish quarter that still bears his name. Venice takes Dubrovnik, which pays it tribute and harbours its galleys, and regains Zadar, this time by a treaty that makes the Venetians overseers rather than occupiers; the townsfolk see through it.

diary.title: Saint Simeon comes to Studenica
diary.details: Nemanja's relics are carried from Mount Athos to the monastery of Studenica.

diary.title: Death of Kaloyan; the singers' war at the Wartburg
diary.details: Kaloyan's reign ends. In Germany the Landgrave of Thuringia (the book calls him margrave) holds a contest for the crown of poetry, on the terms that every losing singer must die; Henry of Ofterdingen loses to Wolfram von Eschenbach and is let go to fetch the one bard he says is better, Klingsohr.

diary.title: Sava returns to Studenica
diary.details: Sava, Nemanja's youngest son, who had left family politics for the monks of Mount Athos, comes back to Studenica and begins to organise the Serbian Orthodox Church.

diary.title: Hermann von Salza hochmeister; Simium writes to Polyaigos
diary.details: Hermann von Salza is elected hochmeister of the Teutonic Order. About this time Simium, headmaster of the Scholomance, begins writing to Polyaigos in the Theban Tribunal, a covenant that also prepares pupils before apprenticeship; an exchange is talked of, but old enmity between Thebes and Transylvania stands in its way. (The book says within the last ten years or so.)

diary.title: The Burzenland granted to the Teutonic Knights
diary.details: Straight after a marriage contract between King Andrew II and Landgrave Hermann of Thuringia for their children, Hermann von Salza's Order is invited to Transylvania (the book also credits a King Bela, and makes Hermann of Thuringia head of the Salza family). Andrew gives it the Burzenland, free of taxes and dues, keeping the right to mint and half the gold and silver mined, and charges it to hold the Carpathian passes against the Cumans. Brother Theoderich commands the mission; Saxon settlers follow in numbers, and the Knights begin five castles, Marienburg, Kronstadt, Rosenau, Schwarzenburg and Kreuzburg.

diary.title: Macrobius slain; Essedarius leads Kezdö Válasz
diary.details: Macrobius, filius of Gasparus and leader of Kezdö Válasz, is torn apart by an angry griffin he met by chance in the Prokletije, the Accursed Mountains. His filius Essedarius, the fourth leader in Norsius's line, takes command. Leona, his partner, was not with him; she hunts the beast down and still hunts griffins in her grief.

diary.title: The Valley of the Thracian Kings found
diary.details: A Tremere necromancer serving as a hoplite finds the burial ground of the ancient Thracian kings close to Seuthopolis, their old capital. Tremere's necromancers rejoice and House Verditius wants a dig too, since the Thracians honoured smith gods; Benilda, wary of cheerful necromancers, bars the way.

diary.title: Stefan the First-Crowned; Andrew II goes on crusade
diary.details: A papal legate crowns Stefan II king of all the Serbian and coastal lands, and most Serbian dioceses take up the Latin rite, though Kotor and Ston keep the Greek. Andrew II of Hungary sets out on crusade.

diary.title: Poena becomes Prima; Ivan Asen II tsar
diary.details: Poena becomes Prima of House Tremere, and Monica Ierne takes the post of legata, the House's field commander. The former Primus is given charge of the Burning Acorns Vexillation, which hunts surviving Diedne, a post that lets him roam as he pleases. Ivan Asen II takes the Bulgarian throne at Tarnovo and marries a daughter of the King of Hungary. Andrew II comes home from crusade to a hostile nobility (the book dates his return to 1222).

diary.title: Sava archbishop of an autocephalous Serbian Church
diary.details: At Sava's request the patriarch of the Greek Church makes the Serbian Church self-governing and consecrates Sava its archbishop. Sava's Nomocanon becomes the book of church law for all the Slav churches.

members.office: Chief aide to the secretary for contingencies
Troubleshooter for the secretary for operations

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: What follows 1220. If the saga follows history, Andrew II's nobles force the Golden Bull on him in 1222; the Mongols break the Cumans at the Kalka in 1223; Hermann von Salza has the Burzenland made a fief of the Holy See in 1225 and the Knights are driven out; Ivan Asen II spreads his rule over Thrace, Macedonia and Epiros within the decade; a crusade against Bosnia comes in 1237; and the Mongols invade in 1241.

neighbours.name: The Rhine Valley and Lorraine
neighbours.summary:
The river country from Basel, where the Rhine turns north and ships begin to sail it, down past Strassburg, Speyer, Worms and Mainz to Cologne and the marshy delta about Utrecht and Deventer, together with the lands west of it: the Vosges, Upper Lorraine round Metz, Toul and Verdun, and Lower Lorraine with Aachen, Liege and the Ardennes on the Tribunal's western fringe.

This is the oldest settled part of Germany, built on Roman colonies and legionary camps, and the Church is strongest here: the cathedral of Mainz has a Divine aura of 7 as a Holy See, those of Speyer, Worms, Trier, Aachen and Cologne 6, and most cities 3. Trade along the river makes its archbishops rich and its cities large; the Jewish communities of Mainz, Speyer and Worms are the greatest in Germany.

The Middle Rhine between Mainz and Koblenz, the Mosel and the Lahn belong to the Rhine Gorge and its curse, which the saga chapter describes.

The Rhine was Rome's frontier, and its west bank is the oldest settled land in Germany: Trier, Mainz, Worms, Speyer, Strassburg and Cologne all began as Roman towns, and Trier was an imperial capital under Constantine. The Burgundians held Worms from 413 until the Huns destroyed them, the matter of the Nibelungenlied, and the Merovingian Franks ruled Austrasia from Metz before Charlemagne made Aachen his seat and Boniface made Mainz the Church's centre for all Germany. The Treaty of Verdun in 843 left the river's western lands as Lotharingia, long disputed between the kingdoms, and the Salian emperors made Speyer their favourite seat and resting place. The First and Second Crusades brought massacres of the Jews of Worms, Speyer, Mainz, Cologne and Trier, and in 1122 the Concordat of Worms ended the Investiture Contest. Today the three archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier rule the valley with the prince-bishops and the Count Palatine, Cologne is the greatest city of the empire, and robber-baron castles live off the tolls of the Gorge.

neighbours.name: The Black Forest
neighbours.summary:
The largest forest of western Europe fills the south-west of the Tribunal: over a hundred miles north to south and up to forty across, all hills under an unbroken canopy, with the Rhine plain to the west and the Neckar and the Swabian uplands to the east. Oak and beech grow on the lower slopes and fringes; in the centre and on the heights the fir stands so thick that no sunlight reaches the floor. There are no clearings, little level ground, a few villages at the edges and about a dozen monasteries drawn by the seclusion.

A Faerie aura of 3 lies over the whole forest, broken only by the Divine islands of its monasteries and a few Magic sites: Durenmar, the Fane of the Founders and the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls. Bears, boars and deer share it with stranger beasts; bockmen, goblins and giant bats hunt by night, villagers who go too deep vanish, and the few folk living inside are said to be half fay. Only the old Roman road crosses it; anywhere else is weeks on foot.

The forest was once the south-western part of the Hercynian Forest, cut off when the Romans built the limes, and its spirit split with it. The Cult of Mercury bound the greater part by its own oath-magic into what is now the Fane of the Founders, and the peaceful remnant withdrew to the Glade; a rebellious splinter fled south, dwindled, and regrew on mortal fear as the dark faerie King of the Black Mountain (Faerie, Might 60), who now rules every dark court of the forest. Since Durenmar's condemnation in 1151 the forest has been a hazard to magi, and no peace with the fay was ever made. The Swabian lands east of the forest, the Jura and the sources of the Danube, belong to this region too.

The Black Forest was the south-western part of the great Hercynian Forest until the Roman limes and the Black Forest Road of the first century cut it off; the Romans held its edges and never its heart. It became part of the duchy of Swabia, and from the eleventh century the Zähringen dukes cleared and settled its fringes, founding Freiburg in 1120, while Hirsau (1059) and its daughter houses such as St Georgen (1084) planted monasteries in its seclusion. The Hohenstaufen rose from their castle on the Kaiserberge nearby, and Barbarossa made Ulm a Free Imperial City in 1164. With the death of the last Zähringen duke in 1218 much of the forest's lordship passed to the Hohenstaufen; its interior remains unbroken wilderness, and the monasteries within it suffer attacks no one can explain.

neighbours.name: The Lowlands
neighbours.summary:
The northern third of Germany, flat and much alike from end to end: from the North Sea eastward the Frisian islands and the Wadden Sea, then swamp and moor, then some two hundred miles of farmland with prosperous cities and few forests, reaching Saxony, Westphalia, Holstein and the Baltic coast about Lübeck.

Its cities are ruled by trade rather than by princes. The southern ones were founded by Charlemagne after he conquered the Saxons or grew from missionary bishoprics; the northern ports are newer, rich, and reaching for Free Imperial status, though Holstein and Pomerania lie for the moment under King Valdemar II of Denmark.

Magi here feel themselves on a Hermetic frontier: most know of some Scandinavian wizard beyond the border, Lübeck is the Redcaps' usual stop toward Novgorod, and the Divine auras run a little weaker toward the Baltic than in the Rhineland.

Hermann's destruction of Varus's legions in the Teutoburger Forest kept Rome out of the north, and the Saxons and Frisians held it as pagans until Charlemagne conquered the Saxons in the late eighth century and planted missionary bishoprics at Bremen, Münster, Paderborn, Hildesheim and the rest. Vikings founded Haithabu and burned Hamburg in 845, and the Poles burned it again in 1030; the coast stayed a frontier. In the twelfth century Henry the Lion, duke of Saxony, made Lübeck a city (1157) and built up Brunswick, until Barbarossa broke his duchy in 1180 and divided its lands. The northern towns have since grown rich on trade: Hamburg became a Free Imperial City in 1189 and Lübeck's merchants have traded at Novgorod since 1205, but Valdemar II of Denmark took Holstein in 1201 and occupied Hamburg in 1216, and holds the coast with Frederick II's acknowledgement.

neighbours.name: Central Germany
neighbours.summary:
The heart of Germany and of the Empire: from the Harz on the edge of Saxony down through Thuringia and Franconia to the Danube, and the smaller part of Bavaria north of the river that was never Roman and belongs to the Rhine Tribunal (the Danube cities, Regensburg chief among them, are claimed by the Greater Alps).

Rolling hills, rocky isolated wildernesses and countless magic and faerie forests of every size, only moderately peopled. Its cities are younger than the Roman ones of the Rhine but weigh heavily in trade and imperial politics, and its courts and cathedrals have grown a distinctly German culture: the Wartburg's minnesänger, Nuremberg's imperial castle, the great abbeys of Fulda and Hersfeld.

Fengheld, the Tribunal's largest covenant, sits in the eastern Harz, and the Harz, the Kyffhäuser and the Thuringian Forest hold some of the strongest spirits of the old Hercynian Forest.

The heart of Germany, from the Harz to the Danube, was pagan country until Boniface felled the Donar Oak and planted the Church at Erfurt, Würzburg and Hersfeld in the eighth century, and Charlemagne founded Frankfurt, which became the capital of the eastern Franks under Louis the German in 843. Henry the Fowler and the Ottonians ruled from Saxony, Henry II made Bamberg a bishopric in 1007 and set out to build a second Rome there, and the silver of the Harz enriched Goslar. The Wartburg, founded in 1067, became under Landgrave Hermann I of Thuringia (1190 to 1217) the centre of German song, where Walther von der Vogelweide won the singers' contest of 1204. The Hohenstaufen enlarged and fortified Frankfurt, where imperial elections are now held, and the Wittelsbachs have ruled Bavaria since 1180; Frederick II's court has visited Erfurt four times since 1214 and held its last German Diet for many years at Frankfurt in 1220.

neighbours.name: The Eastern Marches
neighbours.summary:
The lands between the Elbe and the Oder: lakes and forest, thinly settled, with the reputation of a home of werewolves, witches and giants and the decaying temples of the Slavic gods. Christianity came in the tenth century from the frontier bishoprics of Magdeburg and Merseburg; since then war and peace with the Slavs have alternated, German settlers have poured in, and German speech now prevails.

Meissen in the south-west is wholly German, Lusatia in the south-east mostly Sorbian, and Rügen and Pomerania in the north a mixture under Danish overlords. Land is so plentiful that the local rulers seldom quarrel with one another. Nearly every pagan or magical site of the southern Marches has been destroyed; more survive in Pomerania.

Apart from Crintera the Order has little presence here, but the Rhine Tribunal claims the Marches firmly, disputes its eastern border with the Novgorod Tribunal, and would gladly push further into Polish lands. The Baltic freezes for months every winter and must be thawed each spring by a ritual cast at Arkona.

The Marches between the Elbe and the Oder were Slavic lands, and Christianity came only in the tenth century from the frontier bishoprics of Magdeburg, Merseburg, Brandenburg (948) and Meissen (963), after Henry the Fowler fortified Meissen in 929; the Slavic counter-attack later that century briefly undid the work. Since then war and peace with the Slavs have alternated with intermarriage and heavy German colonisation: the Wettins have ruled Meissen since 1089, Albert the Bear founded the March of Brandenburg in 1150, and the Saxon crusade of 1147 fell on the Wends of Pomerania. Valdemar I of Denmark conquered Rügen in 1168 and broke the temple of Arkona, Barbarossa made Bogislaw duke of Pomerania in 1181, and the Knights of the Sword, founded in 1202, crusade along the Baltic. Meissen is now wholly German, Lusatia mostly Sorb, and Rügen and Pomerania a mixed people under Danish overlords, with land so plentiful that the lords rarely quarrel.

neighbours.name: Bohemia and Moravia
neighbours.summary:
The Tribunal's south-east: the subject kingdom of Bohemia and its March of Moravia, broad half-wooded plains along the upper Elbe and its tributaries, ringed and divided by long wooded mountain chains. There are no great cities, only modest towns thinly spread, and in 1220 the only notable ones lie about and north of Prague.

The Premyslid dynasty, descended from the legendary Czech, has ruled since the eighth century; Christianity came in the ninth with St Methodius and took generations to root. Barbarossa raised the duchy to a kingdom a generation ago, and King Otakar reigns now as a semi-independent tributary of the Empire. Farming, hunting, mining, glass, brewing and horse-breeding are its trades.

Moravia is the Empire's easternmost reach, bordering Hungary and the Transylvanian Tribunal, whose influence, especially House Tremere's, the magi here feel often. Irencillia, the domus magna of Merinita, hides in the Bohemian Forest, and Roznov holds the Carpathian border.

Bohemia has been ruled since the eighth century by the Premyslids, the line the Gifted princess Libuse founded when her vision at Vysehrad chose the ploughman Premysl as her husband. Christianity came in the ninth century with St Methodius and took generations to root; Duke Wenceslaus was murdered by his pagan brother early in the tenth, and the bishopric of Prague was created under Mainz in 973. Moravia passed to Poland in 999 and to Bohemia in 1019, and the kingdom has since been a semi-independent tributary of the empire, suffering Hungarian attacks early in the twelfth century, while Strahov (1140) and Sedlec (1142) brought the new monastic orders. Barbarossa raised the duchy to a subject kingdom a generation ago; King Otakar rules from Prague, and silver newly found at Sedlec promises to change a land of modest towns.

neighbours.name: The Hercynian Forest
neighbours.summary:
The primeval oak forest the Romans found beyond the Alps, nine days wide and of a length nobody knew, covering all of Germania. It had a single vast spirit of the Magic realm (Magic, Might not given), a reflection of the Ideal Forest that some magi call Eden. The rituals of the Cult of Mercury, who guided the legions in building the limes and its magically linked roads, and later St Boniface's felling of the Donar Oak in the eighth century, shattered that spirit into the genii loci of today's forests.

Each fragment met one of four fates: survival as a Magic forest (the Teutoburger Forest, the Drudenbaum, the Romowe oak), dissolution into a mundane wood (the Hertogenwald), replacement by a being of another realm, usually Faerie (the Black Forest, the Ash of Nortorf, the Donar Oak), or alliance with a faerie (the Four Seasonal Courts). The forests have hardly shrunk since Charlemagne's day and resist clearance as if by will. Each still holds a direct link to the Magic realm, the primal power that drew the Cult of Mercury and Bonisagus himself, and the paths through the forest that House Bjornaer and some Merinita can show lead to it.

neighbours.name: The Four Seasonal Courts
neighbours.summary:
Four linked faerie forests, Holly, Alder, Oak and Willow, that the storyguide places where the saga needs them, ideally in a ring at the cardinal points about the player covenant; the names are conveniences, not true names. They are four fragments of one spirit, perhaps once as strong as the Black Forest's, each too weak to live alone and each allied with or possessing a faerie lord. The aura of each is Faerie, rising to 3 across the whole wood at its court's solstice or equinox and shrinking month by month to nearly nothing at the opposite season; patches of Magic aura linger in the Oak Forest, and every ruler has the Regio power (levels not given).

King Holly (Faerie, Might 30, pool 15 to 35; north, winter; Tyrannical +3, Cold-hearted +2) rules a court of ice and frost faeries from a holly grove by an iron will and a detailed law; the spirit forcibly possessed a rebellious winter faerie. The Alder Prince (Faerie, Might 30; west, spring; Compassionate +3, Secretive +2) is red-hued, shy and benign, keeps a shrouded court in a serene vale and rules many holzfrauen. King Oak (Faerie, Might 30; south, summer; Regal +3, Generous +2) holds court under a great oak as a generous host whose honour is touchy and who takes words literally, so a slip binds a guest in an enforced contract. The Willow Maiden (Faerie, Might 30; east, autumn; Manipulative +3, Uncaring +2) seems generous but every gift has a hidden price; she has slipped the spirit's pact and all but owns her wood, and is obsessed with the Alder Prince.

The courts are bound in a yearly drama of stolen power in which the coming season's court raids the reigning one: in December Holly at full strength slays Oak, who is reborn in his forest; in March Alder heals the Willow Maiden's malice with love and she flees home; in June Oak captures Holly and imprisons him in the heart of the Holly Forest; in September the Willow Maiden weds and drowns the Alder Prince in her river. Each ruler keeps Might 30 for resistance and Penetration all year while its pool swings by five a month. Summer against Winter is open war; Spring against Autumn is subtle politics and should pay better, and vis is the obvious wage for taking a side.

neighbours.name: The castle of Triamore
neighbours.summary: A castle and manorial estate on the river Meuse at the edge of the Ardennes, in Lower Lorraine on the western fringe of the Tribunal, with Liege and Verdun the nearest towns of note. The Magic aura is 2. Redcaps bound between the Rhine and Normandy Tribunals make it, with Verdun, their usual meeting point.

neighbours.name: The Rhinefalls
neighbours.summary:
The greatest falls of Europe, five hundred feet wide and eighty high, on the Upper Rhine below Constance near the south-eastern edge of the Black Forest. In their midst stands a rock island taller than the falls with a copse on top; it can be reached only by boat from downstream (Profession: Boating against 9) and climbed only on slippery rock (Athletics against 12), and the summit is a deafening place of raw elemental power. The island's Magic aura is 2, rising to 4 at the summit, and a regio of several levels climbs from it.

Under the rock lies the Spirit of the Rhine (Magic, Might not given), a river elemental pinned there long ago when the Nibelungs, dwarves and giants tamed the wild river; it is said to guard the Rhinegold in revenge. Those who climb the rock and hurl valuables into the maelstrom find the smashed fragments washed up downstream later, each worth a pawn of Aquam vis; it is never found by accident.

details.tethers: The Spirit of the Rhine pinned beneath the rock

levels.name: The lower levels of the rock
levels.enter: Climbing alone cannot enter the regio; powerful magic is needed
levels.notes:
Several levels rise with the climb; their auras are not given.

Secrets
Schwall of Bjornaer, an elderly Wilderist of the Hawthorn Gild formerly of Rheinstein, keeps a hidden sanctum here. His heartbeast is believed a fish, he can also become a mass of water, and his many Twilight Scars leave him always wet. He has completed several Quests for the Rhine spirit.

levels.name: The elemental summit
levels.enter: Powerful magic; no climb reaches it
levels.notes: A turbulent realm of raw elemental water (aura not given). The Rhinegold and the other treasures hurled into the falls over the centuries may lie here.

secrets.title: Schwall's final Quest
secrets.text: Schwall's final Quest is to free the Rhine elemental and merge his mind with it, a kind of immortality before Final Twilight takes him; the floods that would wreck shipping, towns and cities along the whole river are to him a welcome bonus.

secrets.title: Signs on the river
secrets.text: The early signs of Schwall's plan are disturbances on the river.

secrets.title: Schwall and the Tribunal
secrets.text: The Tribunal would March anyone involved, but Schwall expects to be beyond its reach.

neighbours.name: Mount Saint Odile
neighbours.summary: The Hohenburg, a convent two and a half thousand feet up in the northern Vosges on the Alsace side, founded by St Odile, who was born blind and given sight at her baptism by her uncle St Erhard; a rock opened to hide her from her father Duke Adalric, who afterwards gave her the castle. Small chapels, Odile's crypt and an ancient Merovingian cemetery stand on the summit. Below the convent the spring she struck with her cane cures the sick, above all diseases of the eye, and has a Divine aura of 4 (the convent's own is not given). She died in 720 and pilgrims have come ever since.

neighbours.name: Thann Chapel
neighbours.summary: A chapel of 1161 in the southern Vosges about a dozen miles west of Mulhouse, built over the staff of the servant of Bishop Theobald of Gubbio, who had hidden his dead master's ring and thumb inside it; the staff rooted itself in the fir forest under three lights and could not be moved. The lord of the nearby Engelburg raised the chapel, a village grew about it, and the Engelburg peasants ceremonially burn three fir trees before it each summer. Its Divine aura is 3 and it draws pilgrims.

details.tethers: The rooted staff of Bishop Theobald's servant beneath the altar

secrets.title: The fir spirit of the Vosges
secrets.text: The Vosges once had a secretive fir spirit like the Black Forest's. Villages, monasteries and felling wore it down, and the planting of the holy staff extinguished it, which is why no continuous Vosges forest remains.

secrets.title: What the holy staff might do
secrets.text: If the holy staff of Thann were removed it might be the one artefact able to counter the spirit of the Black Forest.

neighbours.name: The Sanctuary of Hercules
neighbours.summary: A hidden cave on the isolated western slopes of the Vosges where three spring-fed pools lie in a Magic aura of 3. The Gauls kept it as a shrine to Ogmios, god of strength, eloquence and poetry; the Romans recast him as Hercules and built a Greek-columned shrine. Grateful petitioners left altar stones in a ring about the pools, and they stand there still for whoever finds the place.

neighbours.name: Andresina
neighbours.summary: An abandoned Roman city in Upper Lorraine, two dozen miles south-west of Toul, built round a great temple of Apollo and its sacred pool, fed by miles of piping; the emperors Caracalla and Constantine both visited. The temple ruins, a half-oval amphitheatre, a crumbling basilica with a mosaic floor, underground chambers and an old rampart remain, with a small village beside it. The Magic aura is 2 and would likely rise if the temple were restored; the book suggests it as a covenant site.

neighbours.name: The Vosges Mountains
neighbours.summary: The range on the west bank of the Upper Rhine facing the Black Forest, as high as it and fir-clad on the upper slopes, but not wholly forested: villages lie among the hills. The southern peaks are rounded granite, the northern hills red sandstone. Many springs, some of them hot, feed the tributaries of the Mosel, and the storks that arrive each spring are thought lucky. The mountains have no general aura; Mount Saint Odile, Thann Chapel and the Sanctuary of Hercules are its sites.

secrets.title: The fir spirit of the Vosges
secrets.text: The fir spirit of the Vosges is extinct, put out by the holy staff at Thann.

neighbours.name: Burg Trifels
neighbours.summary: An eleventh-century Hohenstaufen fortress on the crag of the Sonnenberg at the edge of the Palatinate Forest, twenty miles west of Speyer, and Barbarossa's favourite castle; it has never been taken. Henry VI held Richard the Lionheart prisoner here in 1193 for a ransom of 150,000 marks. It has a large dungeon and one of the Empire's greatest treasuries. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Schwanenburg
neighbours.summary: The Swan Castle on its steep hill over Cleves on the Lower Rhine, named for Lohengrin, the Knight of the Swan, who came in a barge drawn by a swan to defeat Telramund for the widowed Duchess Elsa of Brabant, married her on condition she never ask his name, and left when she did, as Wolfram von Eschenbach tells in Parzival. The lords of Cleves bear a swan in their arms. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Hertogenwald
neighbours.summary: A forest south of Aachen in Lower Lorraine, and the book's example of a Hercynian fragment that dissolved: farmland and the strong Divine aura of Aachen drained its spirit away, and it is now a mundane wood with no aura at all.

neighbours.name: Heiliger Sand
neighbours.summary: The vast and ancient Jewish cemetery just outside the west walls of Worms, elaborate in its stones, overgrown and deserted except at the newest plots, since the dead are left in peace. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Rheingasse
neighbours.summary: Fengheld's chapter house in the centre of Cologne, a city house in the Rheingasse near the market, where two Gentle-Gifted magi of the Apple Gild very ably arrange the covenant's supplies and its dealings with the mundane world. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The valley of Durenmar
neighbours.summary:
A steep-sided hidden valley some fifteen miles inside the northern Black Forest, about fifteen miles south of Hirsau monastery, with Baden to the north-west. A guard post lower down is enchanted to hide the three-mile track up to it, and the covenant's towers stand below the surrounding treeline. The clearing on the valley floor, split by a stream and unfortified, has a Magic aura of 7 and is protected by the strongest Aegis of the Hearth in the Order; the Cult of Mercury's temple stood here before Bonisagus came in 754. Caves of unknown extent run under the north cliffs, with wild rumours of enslaved gnomes mining gems.

Covenfolk born in the aura all carry Warping, and their longevity is unexplained. A lone fir near the Great Library, the Black Fir, is tolerated for the Perdo vis of its cones; the great vine on the Tower of Bonisagus yields Intellego vis in its sap.

secrets.title: How the Black Fir came
secrets.text: The Black Fir was planted over a century ago by the King of the Black Mountain at the edge of the Aegis after his direct attacks failed; when the magi found it gave vis they moved the Aegis boundary to take it in, breaching their own defence.

secrets.title: The Black Fir creeps
secrets.text: The Black Fir creeps about six inches a year toward the Tower of Bonisagus, and nobody alive remembers it being young. What happens when it reaches the tower or the vine is unknown but likely severe.

neighbours.name: The hollow of Dankmar
neighbours.summary: The dampest and darkest part of the Black Forest, about forty miles south-west of Durenmar and a few miles south of the Black Forest Road, where the fir stands so thick that noon is dusk, only fungi grow on the poisoned carpet of needles and only ravens call. The Faerie aura is 5. A circular palisade of split logs encloses wooden huts and four stone towers whose cellars join caves beneath, fir and yew lean over the walls, and every wooden thing glows with phosphorescent bracket fungi day and night. For at least a mile about it a version of The Shrouded Glen (level 40, Penetration 20) turns travellers away in nameless dread, and bockmen (Faerie, Might 20) patrol the surroundings by pact with Orphedra.

neighbours.name: The Black Forest Road
neighbours.summary: The only road across the forest, from Offenburg up the Kinzig valley to Rottweil, built in the first century under Vespasian by the Eighth Legion under Cornelius Clemens to shorten the way from Strassburg to Augsburg. Mercurian priests raised magical milestones along it that still ward off the forest's supernatural denizens, so wise travellers camp beside them. The paving is weathered and overgrown but it remains the one way to bring a cart through; the central stretch of nearly thirty miles between Gengenbach monastery and the village of Waldmoessingen on its ruined Roman fort has no human dwelling and takes two days, so one night in the forest cannot be avoided. Bockmen (Faerie, Might 20) lurk along it, and Dankmar lies a few miles to the south. Its own aura is not given; the forest's Faerie 3 lies over it.

details.tethers: The Mercurian milestones that ward off the forest's faeries

neighbours.name: The Feldberg and the Hoellental
neighbours.summary: The highest peak of the southern Black Forest, reached only through the Hoellental, and the seat of the King of the Black Mountain, King Fir (Faerie, Might 60; Malicious +5, Secretive +3, Vengeful +3), pictured as a huge black-cloaked man with a terrible face. He commands the weather, grants flaws such as depression, fear, lameness and loss of direction, possesses, shrouds and holds a regio of several levels with Faerie auras from 3 to 8; victory and virtue he grants very rarely. He is the dread and undisputed ruler of every dark faerie court in the forest, and his influence covers all of it. Monasteries inside the forest suffer his attacks: vanishing monks, blight, landslides and earthquakes.

details.tethers: The great dark fir on the summit, King Fir

levels.name: The Hoellental
levels.notes: Hell Valley, a haunted winding valley climbing from the centre of the forest, the only way to the mountain; the lowest of the regio's several levels, whose auras run from 3 to 8.

levels.name: The Black Mountain
levels.notes: The bare summit with its one great dark fir, King Fir: no mortal who sees it ever leaves the forest. Beneath lies a vast dungeon where hundreds of enslaved humans who strayed too deep toil without end.

secrets.title: Beyond the King's dominion
secrets.text: The King of the Black Mountain's dominion cannot reach the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls or the Fane of the Founders; lacking the original spirit's nature, they are unknowable to him.

secrets.title: What the King wants
secrets.text: The King of the Black Mountain craves revenge on those who bound the old spirit and wants to be whole again, so he seeks Durenmar's destruction: were it to fall, the rite of the Fane would lapse and the bound spirit would be his to dominate and absorb.

secrets.title: The raid of 1085
secrets.text: The raid of 1085 was the King of the Black Mountain's, and its captives never returned.

secrets.title: The King's long plan
secrets.text: The Black Fir at Durenmar is the King of the Black Mountain's centuries-long plan.

neighbours.name: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls
neighbours.summary: At the exact centre of the Black Forest, in a place nobody has found or admitted finding, a stream falls through a precipitous valley over seven waterfalls, and the one way up is a narrow path beside the water through hazel and beech. The regio has seven levels, one for each fall, and the Spirit of the Glade (Magic, Might 50; Enigmatic +4, Wise +3), the peaceful female remnant of the forest's original genius locus, lets a climber past each fall only after a Quest; she guides, swears oaths, shrouds and grants clear thought. Each ascent brings a deeper understanding of the Forest and the top a complete one, at the price of escalating Sacrifices such as parts of one's Hermetic magic. The Hercynian lineage of Bonisagus held it the place the Mercurian priests and Bonisagus sought; some prophesy godlike power for a destined finder, others guess the spirit has faded and been replaced by a powerful maga in Final Twilight, perhaps the Founder Merinita. The bell of St Georgen was carried here, and the forest took its revenge on the monastery. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The Spirit of the Glade, the peaceful remnant of the forest's spirit

levels.name: The first waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The second waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The third waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The fourth waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The fifth waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The sixth waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given).

levels.name: The seventh waterfall
levels.enter: Complete the Quest the Spirit of the Glade sets for this fall
levels.notes: A new level of understanding of the Forest, won by the Quest that let the climber pass this waterfall (aura not given). The top level gives a complete and harmonious understanding.

neighbours.name: The Fane of the Founders
neighbours.summary: A quiet glade not far from Durenmar, its whereabouts hidden by powerful magic, with a twelve-sided stone slab at its centre and a Magic aura of 6. Here the Oath of the Founders was composed and sworn, and every seven years during the Rhine Tribunal twelve magi, one of each House, come secretly to renew the Founders' vows in a rite believed to preserve the Order; they leave with vis as their reward, and the place encourages clear and calm thought. Only the Primi and their chosen know it exists, though most Durenmar magi know of it, and all who have sought it have failed. It is older than the Order: many truces were made here, among them one between Germanic chiefs and a Roman general that fixed the Empire's northern limit. The rite was skipped only at the Tribunals of 997, 1004 and 1011 and resumed in 1018 with an Ex Miscellanea magus in Diedne's place. Rumour says the attendees met Hermes himself, or a powerful faerie posing as him who extracted a terrible service from the Founders.

details.tethers: The twelve-sided stone slab and the spirit bound in it

secrets.title: What the Fane is
secrets.text: The Fane is an artefact into which the Cult of Mercury bound much of the Black Forest's original magical essence by a great ritual. It behaves as a spirit with limited forest powers: it produces vis, shrouds, swears oaths and grants clear thought for a time.

secrets.title: The Fane's rite
secrets.text: The rite of the Fane must be renewed regularly or the spirit escapes the stone, which the King of the Black Mountain hopes for so that he may seize it.

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The Fane behaves as a spirit of Magic Might 40.

neighbours.name: Mummel Lake
neighbours.summary: An enchanted and isolated lake deep under the mountains near Seebach. A Nixe (Faerie, Might not given), a water-nymph, lives in it and now and then visits the nearby settlements to bewitch a young man with her beauty; she must return every night, and the jealous elemental spirits of the lake (realm and Might not given) kill any mortal who follows her home. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Source of the Danube
neighbours.summary: In the eastern Black Forest an enchanted spring runs from a crack in the rock into a small pool, deceptively deep, which is the source of the Danube. The Faerie aura is 3 about the pool and 5 within the water. Unlike the Rhine's, the river's spirit is a faerie: Danu (Faerie, Might not given), once a goddess of countless peoples before Rome, whose power fades elsewhere but is strong here. The pool seems bottomless because of the regio; at its top level, with Faerie aura 10, lies the true bottom and a gateway into Arcadia. Vast Aquam vis could be taken here, at the near-certain cost of Danu's anger.

details.tethers: Danu, the river's spirit

levels.name: The true bottom
levels.notes: The top level of the regio, where the pool's real floor lies, and a gateway into Arcadia that feeds the river. The levels between are not given.

neighbours.name: The Swabian Jura
neighbours.summary: Harsh limestone hills between the valleys of the Danube and the Neckar, east of the Black Forest, whose defensible peaks the Hohenzollerns and other local lords have forted. They are riddled with stalactite grottos such as the Nebelhoehle, the Misty Cave. On the south side near Zweifalten monastery the Wimsener Hoehle swallows the river Ach, a Danube tributary, which runs underground for a couple of miles through a tunnel that can partly be navigated by boat. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Blautopf
neighbours.summary: A large round pool of startling deep blue at the southern edge of the Swabian Jura beside Kloster Blaubeuren, the source of the little river Blau, with a Faerie aura of 2. It is the home of the Schoene Lau (Faerie, Might not given), a beautiful, reclusive, long-haired water maiden with webbed feet, banished here by her husband, a faerie king of the Black Sea, because she cannot laugh: the future holds no surprise for her. Those who come for wisdom, Blaubeuren's monks among them, bring a modest gift and she foretells their future; her predictions always come true and seldom bring the happiness hoped for. Whoever makes her laugh breaks the curse and earns her eternal gratitude.

neighbours.name: The Limes
neighbours.summary: The Roman frontier fortifications of the first century, whose ramparts, forts and temples lie in ruins along their whole route past Gmuend and through the Odenwald, the Swabian Forest and the Swabian Jura. The Cult of Mercury guided the legions in building it and its magically linked roads, and its building first split the Black Forest and its spirit from the Hercynian Forest. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Kaiserberge
neighbours.summary: Three round wooded hills south of Gmuend in the Stauferland, each topped by a castle: the Hohenstaufen to the west, the lowest and grandest, ancestral seat of the imperial dynasty; the Hohenrechberg; and the Stuifen to the east, the highest. The Stauferland about them is the rolling country between the Swabian Forest and the Swabian Jura, named for the Hohenstaufens. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Terschelling
neighbours.summary: A deserted, weather-beaten island of the Frisian chain on the Wadden Sea, the shallow water the sandy islands enclose, shared by the pirate magi of Waddenzee and many thousands of seabirds whose noise in spring and summer has earned it a name for haunting, which the magi encourage; they have driven off every other settler. The Magic aura is 3 over the covenant building and a few hundred paces about it. A long, low Danish-style long-house sunk partly into the ground houses the covenfolk, four separate magus buildings join its walls by sunken covered walkways, and there is a harbour for the covenant's five ships.

neighbours.name: The Pirates' Graveyards
neighbours.summary: Dozens of graves marked with standing stones and boulders on a low ridge some fifty feet above the swamp in Drenthe, a couple of dozen miles up the river Ems from its estuary; they are the only stones in Friesland. The pirates of Frisia, Waddenzee's among them, bury their dead here, and the place is haunted. Lucas von Beck of Waddenzee takes vis and corpses from it for his necromancy. The aura is not given and its realm is uncertain.

secrets.title: The power in the graveyards
secrets.text: The power in the Pirates' Graveyards may be Infernal rather than Magic; Lucas has barely considered it.

neighbours.name: Haithabu
neighbours.summary: The old Viking trading city a few miles from the fishing town of Schleswig on the Schlei fjord, founded at the start of the ninth century where the land crossing between Baltic and North Sea is shortest. Only earth ramparts and burial mounds remain, and, the locals say, ghosts. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Ash of Nortorf
neighbours.summary: A small ash seedling in the churchyard of the little town of Nortorf in Holstein, where the roads to Schleswig, Lübeck and Hamburg meet. Every New Year's Night a white rider on a white horse cuts it down while a black rider on a black horse tries and fails to stop him. The prophecy says that one day the black rider will win, the shoot will grow into a tree, and once it is big enough to tether a horse under, a king will come with a great army; while his horse stands under the tree he cannot be beaten and gains fell powers. The tree's spirit (Infernal, Might 10, potentially 40; Ambitious +2) grants victory and the virtues of entrancement, inspiration and toughness; the white horseman is Divine and the black an Infernal agent. Agents of the black rider may tell magi of the ash as a future vis source and not of the prophecy, hoping they will guard it on New Year's Night: if the Divine rider is driven off or killed he never returns. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The ash seedling itself

neighbours.name: The Giant's Grave
neighbours.summary: A rectangular bed of stones forty yards by ten in the Everstorf Forest north of Schwerin in Mecklenburg, near Naschendorf. The farmers of the village found a cattle-stealing, crop-trampling giant asleep, rolled him into a huge grave and buried him; his wife dragged stone blocks in her apron to cover it so he could not escape, and he suffocated while she was never seen again. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Teutoburger Forest
neighbours.summary: Forested hills in Westphalia where Hermann's Germans destroyed the Roman legions in the first century and Charlemagne fought in the late eighth, the beachhead of every conqueror and so a wilderness with strong guardians, one of the last on the northern lowlands. At its heart a great clearing is ringed by ancient trees of different kinds that together are the forest's spirit (Magic, Might 40; Patient +3, Unforgiving +1), which grants simple-mindedness and victory, shrouds, holds a regio and keeps the legionaries in stasis. The surviving Romans withdrew into the forest after the battle and vanished; they are trapped in the regio's top level and would make loyal, well-trained grogs for anyone who bargained their release with the trees, unless a renegade magus or hedge wizard hidden in the forest already uses them as his turb. The Externsteine stand on its south-eastern edge. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The ring of ancient trees about the great clearing

levels.name: The legionaries' camp
levels.notes: The top level of the regio (its levels are not numbered and their auras not given): a fortified Roman camp in the clearing where the surviving legionaries of Hermann's battle still live, kept from aging and from leaving, free to hunt and forage, heavily Warped and reverent of the trees.

neighbours.name: The Externsteine
neighbours.summary: Thirteen jumbled sandstone rocks, some over a hundred feet tall, in a large clearing on the south-eastern edge of the Teutoburger Forest near Paderborn, with a Divine aura of 4. Once a pagan site, its caves were consecrated as a chapel in 1115; a carving of the Descent from the Cross stands at the foot of one rock, and inside another a bare upper chapel has a window that catches the sunrise of the summer solstice. It is enigmatically peaceful and home to a handful of ascetic hermits.

neighbours.name: The Teufelsmoor
neighbours.summary: A vast swampy waste of dark peat for miles north-east of Bremen, bare of grass and trees, always misted and foul-smelling; strange shapes and lights move in it at night. The locals think it cursed and keep away, though peasants cut peat at its edge for fuel. The book suggests it as an unpleasant but workable covenant site. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Lüneburg Heath
neighbours.summary: A sprawling open heath south of Lüneburg with small woods, a few villagers and shepherds tending Heidschnucken, the goat-like sheep descended from Corsican mouflon brought here about two hundred years ago. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Teufelsküche
neighbours.summary: A forgotten circle of round stones about an ancient altar deep in the Haldensleben Forest north-west of Magdeburg, where Woden was worshipped: tall red-bearded priests in long white cloaks came in the hour before dawn with men in skins and other dark shapes, slaughtered a sacrifice and burned its vitals to greet the day. The missionaries who purged the cult named it the Devil's Kitchen; whether any priest of Woden survives is the storyguide's choice. The Wild Hunt, the troupe of storm and winter faeries led by the Wild Huntsman (Faerie, Might 50) with its Horsemen (Faerie, Might 20 each) and Hounds (Faerie, Might 10 each), rises from here on stormy winter nights, so winter is a bad time to visit. The aura is not given.

details.tethers: The ancient altar of Woden at the circle's centre

neighbours.name: The northern swamps
neighbours.summary: The bogs and marshes of northern Germany generally, the haunt of the Boglin (Magic, Might 25; Greedy +5, Reclusive +2, Guileful +1): a carapaced sac of a body the size of three men with eight slimy dark-brown tentacles twelve feet long and a toothy maw, lying under murky water and betrayed only by a foul stench and a faint murmuring. It chokes prey with a cloud of stinking gas, paralyses it with venomous barbs, drags it to the maw in three rounds and regrows a lost tentacle each season it hibernates; it is blind, gluttonous and a cunning hunter. Its tentacles hold a pawn of Animal vis each and its brain six of Perdo. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Münsterland
neighbours.summary: The flat, highly fertile plain of Westphalia round Münster, the prosperous market city founded as a monastery in 805 to convert the Saxons. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Heorot on Zealand
neighbours.summary: The site of the hall of Hrothgar, the legendary king of the Danes, on the island of Zealand in the kingdom of Denmark, where Beowulf fought Grendel; Rügen lies not far across the water. Zealand is by tradition Novgorod Tribunal territory, but no covenant of the Order has lasted in Norse lands long enough to attend a Tribunal, so the claim is a grey area the new covenant of Heorot means to exploit. The kin of Grendel (trolls; realm and Might not given) still haunt the island's bogs and have killed fourteen of the covenant's grogs and taken its leader's left arm. The aura is not given.

neighbours.name: Fengheld House
neighbours.summary: Fengheld's most remote chapter house, a single fortified townhouse in the city of Cherbourg in Normandy, outside the Rhine Tribunal altogether, owned by Sir Jozef of Poznan, a crusader of Polish birth. It runs a small trading business with England and France. Its aura is not given.

neighbours.name: The Harz Mountains
neighbours.summary: Germany's northernmost range, fifty miles of high granite hills on the edge of Saxony, a desolate wilderness ringed by the civilised Saxon towns. Wind off the northern plain, rain and fog prevail, and low cloud hides the peaks and cuts them off from the lowlands; the lower slopes are gloomy forest with strange hidden rocks, whispering streams, lakes and caves.
