A small river running off the western slopes of the Hargitta mountains, which might be the lost Sargetias. When Trajan marched on Dacia in 105, Decebalus had captive Romans turn the Sargetias aside, sealed his and his nobles' gold and silver into its bed under stones, let the water back, hid more in caves along its banks, and killed the workmen. Captured Dacian nobles betrayed the secret, but a Byzantine official's report says the hoard was never recovered and says nothing of the caves. Neither river nor caves has been found.

Kezdö Válasz has not looked for it: the hoard is small beside Lycaneon's.

secrets.title: A dragon and Decebalus's hoard
secrets.text: Slavonic dragons line their lairs with gold and silver, and a treasure the size of Decebalus's hoard has very probably drawn one.

neighbours.name: The Bran Pass Zenodochium
neighbours.summary:
A zenodochium House Tremere built in the Bran Pass, an important road, atop a sheer cliff at the pass's southern end. A band of southern knights has lately moved in and preys on the merchants passing below; their leader, kin at some remove to the royal house, is a rebel who hopes to raise the Vlachs against the royal army.

Story seed: the House's elders want it back and send young magi; killing the knights and hiding the bodies may bring the king's men, and a subtler way may be wiser.

neighbours.name: The Plague House
neighbours.summary:
A rural zenodochium near a village whose people have found it and learnt that the sick who lie in its hall usually get better. They use it as a pest house: at the first sign of illness the strong men carry the sick there and come back a month later to collect them or bury them.

Story seed: grogs bring their badly hurt magus in and find Lucia, a village girl, near death of plague in the hall; the grogs may take her for an intruder, a servant or a maga, and the villagers, returning, may think the Gifted stranger means harm to their refuge, all the more if Lucia has died. The Tribunal does not mind villagers using it, so long as they keep it in repair.

neighbours.name: The Lost Zenodochium of Zadar
neighbours.summary: After the bloodshed of 1203 the Tremere set up a zenodochium inside a regio, in a magical lacuna in Zadar, and, expecting more bloodshed, staffed it with a skilled surgeon and some helpers. Within months the House lost touch with them, and the regio itself seems to have vanished. The search has dwindled, but young magi still try now and then to find the surgeon. The book gives no aura.

secrets.title: Zadar's Infernal places
secrets.text: Zadar's violence breeds Infernal auras and regiones over its worst killings.

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: What became of the lacuna and its people is left to the storyguide.

neighbours.name: Leviathan's Cache
neighbours.summary: A hidden naval base somewhere among the southern Dalmatian islands, its place undisclosed, where House Tremere keeps the stores to support its small Adriatic fleet in a war. The book gives no aura.

neighbours.name: Gigas
neighbours.summary:
A covenant of the Theban Tribunal, a hunting lodge south-west of Sofia, well to the north-west of Evredika's sancta in the Rhodopes. It is House Tremere's thinly veiled cat's paw among the Theban magi (described in The Sundered Eagle and the Theban pack), and has been told not to contest the vis Evredika claims. Not a Transylvanian oppidum, so not a covenant here. The Theban book gives it a weak Magic aura (1 here).

Story seed: a hunting party led by a nobleman with a 'pet' white wolf strips all of Evredika's vis sources, and Gigas is the obvious suspect. If its denials are true, who is framing it, and why?

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The book leaves the true raiders to the storyguide.

neighbours.name: The Storm Wizards
neighbours.summary:
A lonely, ancient Gifted tradition found only in Transylvania. Mountain villagers have long exposed unwanted babies (the deformed, the seemingly mad, the children of incest) on the bare slopes to rid themselves of whatever curse they feared; nearly all die, but the few with The Gift are carried off by bearded giants striding above the storm clouds, and so the storm wizards find their apprentices and open their Gift. The grown wizards are huge, bearded and solitary.

Magi know only that they raise and steer storms and are said to number fewer than six; peasants blame every storm on them, and since a called storm looks wholly natural, nobody can be sure there are not many more. Being Gifted, they fall under Join or Die, but they are so rare and seem so harmless that hardly any magus has found out. Some joined House Ex Miscellanea in the Schism War and fought beside the Tremere, a service the Order has forgotten; no text on their powers is known to survive. Their aims, if they have any, are unknown.

Twice they have banded together to storm the Scholomance's tower, holding it out of its regio, and twice been driven off; they talk of taking back something they lost. A Transylvanian tale of a dragon-riding weather wizard, the tenth scholar the Devil keeps from the Scholomance, may owe something to them. Thietmar is one of them.

Story seeds: travellers caught in a mountain storm see, by the lightning, a giant fleeing bolts that keep finding him, and must choose whether to help the giant or the young wizard whose initiation they have walked into; or they find an ice cave carved with runes and full of Auram vis, and with it the wizards who harvest it.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

Their magic: three Supernatural Abilities, Storm Calling (Communication + ability: raise a storm, local, provincial or national, lasting from a Diameter to a Moon, for 1, 2 or 4 pawns of Auram vis, or move any storm without cost, even against the wind or indoors), Storm Riding (Perception + ability: see from, travel to, or send a touched person to any point of a storm in sight) and Storm Fighting (buffets, deluge, hail, erosion that topples a building, and lightning at +20), with the Arcane Ability Organization Lore: Storm Wizards and Penetration. Once raised a storm is natural, so it needs no Penetration and crosses an Aegis. In a season of ice harvesting a wizard gathers (Int + Organization Lore + aura) / 3, rounded up, pawns of Auram vis as ice that never melts, at sites he keeps secret. A wizard who takes two or more Warping Points at once, or reaches a new Warping Score, may become a storm for a Moon (Strength + stress die against 3 + Warping Score), and dies if he cannot gather himself again before it blows out. The Heart of the Storm initiation (Ease Factor 21, script bonus +15: the giant's heart as a Quest, the Feud with the giants' tribe as a Major Ordeal) gives Giant Blood, free to a storm wizard. The Virtues Storm Calling, Storm Riding and Storm Fighting and the Social Status Storm Wizard are in the catalog.

details.rules: Every one is Gifted, nearly every one a man; each lives alone in a cave high above the snow. An apprentice ends his training by hunting down a true giant and eating its heart.
details.wants: Their ice sites kept secret; giants hunted; to be let alone
details.offers: Storms moved away from a village, for gifts of food left out

secrets.title: What the Tremere bury
secrets.text: The Tremere may be burying what they know of the storm wizards on purpose: their powers baffled the Diedne in the Schism War, and the House may want that surprise kept for the next war.

neighbours.name: A storm wizards' ice cave
neighbours.summary: A cave high in the Carpathians whose frozen walls are cut with strange runes and pictures of shadowy giants walking over stormy peaks: one of the sites where the storm wizards harvest their ice, which they guard as their deepest secret. Its Magic aura is strong (the book gives no number); where it lies is left to the storyguide.

secrets.title: Vis at A storm wizards' ice cave
secrets.text: Vis: Auram, soaked into the ice of the walls, drawn out with a spell like Gather the Essence of the Beast (amount not given). Magi who use it will have to share or fight for it with the storm wizards, who are angry at first but may be talked round to trade or alliance.

neighbours.name: The Fectores
neighbours.summary:
House Tremere's corps of monster hunters, named from interfectores, slayers. A century ago the vampire of a dead dhampir magus was trying to fill the House with vampires; the famed hunter Murat of Terezin came to Coeris and with Radomir of Tremere cleared every one out. Murat joined House Ex Miscellanea, and the two used a hoard of initiation scripts, a Gnostic's notes on a taltós clan he had spied on, to learn how to open a Gifted person to the Hunters' Arts. Laniena, by the Aggtelek caves, trains them (see the Hungary chapter).

Two in three of the Gifted children Laniena finds are trained as Fectores: peasants, soldiers and dhampirs with no taste for fifteen years of books, three of them made in the time one apprentice takes. The other third become Hermetic Fectores, magi Ex Miscellanea who also hold one Practice Art. Those who prove untrustworthy never swear the Oath and are spent where the danger is worst. Some magi call the training a deprivation of magical power, since the trainees could have learnt the Hermetic Arts; Laniena answers that they are not yet members of the Order, and the Tribunal, which is to say House Tremere, lets it go on. Bendis is the best of the non-Hermetic Fectores.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

The Hunters' Arts, the scattered remnant of the old taltós magic: three Practice Arts like Techniques, Scry, Ban and Slay (each a Major Supernatural Virtue), joined with Foe Arts like narrow Forms (Minor Virtues; the first Practice Art brings one free). All are Difficult Arts, raised on the Ability table; against a mortal foe with no Might every level is 10 higher. Scry forges a lasting bond to a foe (Per + Scry + Foe + aura) that gives its direction, then its smells, sounds or sight, and a sympathetic bonus; a botch ties the foe to the scryer. Ban makes amulets lasting a Sun from twelve hours' work, one soaking up wounds from the foe and one cutting short its powers, and staked hawthorn wards that lower the Might of a foe inside for three days. Slay charges a new weapon in a day's chanting; each true fact about the foe lowers the level by 5 and each false one raises it, and a hit that penetrates leaves the foe Incapacitated, after which the weapon is spent. A Fector has The Gift, the free Fector Social Status, Second Sight, all three Practice Arts and three Foe Arts, 120 experience points from training, and no magical defence but Ban; the Fectores know the Foes Vampire, Werewolf, Ghost, Nightwalker and Witch. Hermetic Fectores take a Practice Art as their Major non-Hermetic Virtue, a Minor Magical Focus against their foe, and Weak Spontaneous Magic. The Virtues Fector, Scry Art, Ban Art, Slay Art and the Foe Art are in the catalog.
neighbours.ruler: The magi of Laniena, for House Tremere

details.rules: Gifted hunters trained at Laniena for five years in the Hunters' Arts; most then join House Ex Miscellanea as Gifted companions and learn the Parma Magica, but owe their loyalty to House Tremere. No dhampir may be given Hermetic training.
details.wants: Vampires and other supernatural threats destroyed
details.offers: Trained hunters, Hermetic or not, on the Tribunal's front line

links.note: Teaches them the Ban Art; Hermetic Fector

secrets.title: What Murat of Terezin was
secrets.text: Murat of Terezin was a dhampir and rose as a vampire when he died: he is now a kukudhi.

secrets.title: Murat of Terezin's family
secrets.text: Murat of Terezin, now a kukudhi, lives far from Laniena with his fourth mortal wife and has fathered over twenty dhampir children.

secrets.title: Murat the Younger's silence
secrets.text: Only Murat the Younger knows that Murat of Terezin lives on as a vampire, and lets him be for the hunters his children make.

neighbours.name: The Sabotnici
neighbours.summary:
Those born on a Saturday, a day many vampires cannot go out on or harm anyone born on: such a vampire's direct powers do not touch them. The Bulgarians call them sabotnici, the rest of the Balkans vaperari, the Greeks alaphroiskiotoi. A child born in the Unclean Days between Christmas and Epiphany, or in the Wolf Holiday of November, is a sabotnik too, but will rise as a vampire after death; the Wolf Holiday's children often turn into wolves and become pricolici when they die.

Not every sabotnik hunts. Many sense the unseen, and can find a vampire even when it has no body, or tell a magician or witch. Most who gain powers are men; the few women are stronger, and read dreams. Dogs can be sabotnici too, the four-eyed dogs with a black mark over each eye: Zuban is one (see the Bestiary). Looking through the sleeve of a sabotnik's shirt shows whether a corpse is a vampire, though the vampire may strike whoever is looking.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

A sabotnik should take Second Sight, perhaps Magic Sensitivity, and a woman Dream Interpretation; one who hunts most likely knows the Scry Art. In a team of hunters they research the foe, gather its connections and track it.

details.rules: None: a sabotnik is made by the day of his birth, not by any school
details.offers: Finding vampires, and safety from their direct powers

neighbours.name: The Glogove
neighbours.summary:
Hunters marked at birth across the Balkans: born feet first, with teeth, or with red hair. They take their name from glog, the black hawthorn, a strong defence against vampires, and carve staves and swords from it, mostly to guard rather than to strike. Where a sabotnik finds vampires, a glog shields people from them and sometimes kills them. Glogove are hot-tempered and quarrelsome, often in trouble with their neighbours, and usually strong and athletic.

Black hawthorn grows slowly and twists, too crooked for planks; as a material it gives +7 to protect from vampires, +4 to protect from evil and +4 to prevent disease. Laniena has grown a hedge of it around its houses.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

A glog should take Second Sight and often Warrior, an Affinity or Puissant Single Weapon, and too often Wrathful or Fury; a trained one knows the Ban or Slay Art. In a team they fight the foe hand to hand and ward the ground and their allies.

details.rules: None: a glog is marked at birth (feet first, with teeth, or red-haired)
details.offers: Protection from vampires, and their destruction

neighbours.name: The Taltós
neighbours.summary:
Hungarian magicians born to fight evil. A taltós who wins the childhood dream-fight becomes a nightwalker, one of a band whose spirits go out while they sleep to fight evil things and keep their villages safe. Among the Székely they were shape-changing shamans who led their warriors to war.

More than a thousand years ago the taltós were a mighty tradition of the Balkans, the wise men of the Huns, with powers from shapeshifting and spirit-walking to potions and vampire slaying. Quarrelsome, and made worse by The Gift, they split into factions as their tribes went to war; one side turned its vampire-killing magic on rival taltós, the other copied it, and within a few years they had all but wiped each other out. Today's taltós keep only scraps, and the Hunters' Arts descend from the same wreck.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

The taltós are Nightwalkers (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, the Nightwalker chapter), and may have other powers; one who knows the Hunters' Arts most likely has Scry or Ban. In a team of hunters they ward the ground and their allies.

details.rules: Marked at birth by a caul or extra fingers or toes; at seven the child dreams of an elder taltós in beast shape and must beat it in a fight to be initiated.
details.wants: Their villages kept safe from evil creatures by night

neighbours.name: The Kresnici
neighbours.summary:
The Balkan counterpart of the taltós, strongest in Serbia and Slovenia. A kresnik, born with a clear or white caul, has powers that bring fertility. Their sworn enemies are the kudlaci, sorcerers and vampires born with a red or black caul who kill livestock and drain the crops; the kresnici fight them in their phantasm form by night, and a kudlak who dies becomes a vampire (see the Bestiary).

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

The kresnici are Nightwalkers (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, the Nightwalker chapter); one who knows the Hunters' Arts most likely has Scry or Ban.

details.rules: Born with a clear or white caul
details.wants: Crops and herds kept fertile; the kudlaci beaten

neighbours.name: The Dhampiri and Vampirdzhia
neighbours.summary:
Hunters born of vampires. A risen vampire often goes first to its old home and, if its widow is there, gets a child on her; that child grows up to hunt its kind. Across most of the Tribunal it is a dhampir (feminine dhampiresa); some are legends, like Obrad of Niš, priest and dhampir, and Murat of Terezin, who killed more than two hundred vampires. A dhampir earns fame, a fee and gifts of beasts, clothes and food from grateful villages, but hides that he will rise as a vampire himself when he dies.

A vampire's son is a vampirdzhi in Bulgaria and a vampijerovik elsewhere in the Balkans (lampijerovik in Bosnia and Albania); vampires' daughters become witches instead. A vampirdzhi hunts because he must, with no lore of his own unless he finds a gift or a teacher, and an untaught one may not know that he too will rise, so the curse runs on down a family.

House Tremere forbids its magi to take a dhampir as an apprentice, after dead dhampir magi let vampires into the House.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

Such a hunter takes the Dhampir Virtue (in the catalog: Second Sight free, sight in darkness, aging from 50 at -3, +1 Faerie Lore, rising as a vampire unless the rites are done), most likely the Slay Art if trained, and Enemy or Plagued by Supernatural Entity for the parent vampire. In a team they fight the foe hand to hand. Tibor of Borša is one.

details.rules: A dhampir's fee is fixed by custom and never haggled down; each arranges, usually with his son, for his own corpse to be destroyed before it can rise.
details.offers: Vampire slaying, for a fee

neighbours.name: The Lampijeroviki of Sanžak
neighbours.summary:
A whole district of the Sanžak in Serbia peopled by lampijeroviki, the sons of one vampire's line. They have made their prey their trade: they know vampires better than anyone, and hire out as hunters and teachers.

Each of them will rise as a vampire unless the rites are done on his body.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

details.offers: Vampire hunting for hire, and training in it

neighbours.name: The Wolf Brotherhoods
neighbours.summary:
Varcolaci (Slavs say vukodlaci or kudlaci) are living men who take wolf shape, born to it with a red or black caul, feet first or with teeth, or turned by magic; some become other beasts. All are distrusted and all rise as bestial vampires when they die, good or bad. Some band into secret wolf brotherhoods that guard their people and hunt vampires, the wolf being the vampire's old enemy; others kill cattle, steal milk and blight herds, and are said to eat the moon in eclipses. The mischievous kudlaci are nightwalkers, fought by the kresnici.

Story seed: House Bjornaer hates brotherhoods of shapeshifters, which look to it like the Infernal cult it fears, and may order a Bjornaer magus to root one out, though the brotherhood is all that keeps a strigoi viu's vampires off the village.

No tradition record covers them: their powers are summarised here, and a member who needs them is played from Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

A varcolac takes Shapeshifter if born to it or Skinchanger if he learned it, perhaps Lycanthrope and Animal Ken.

details.rules: Secret; its members are varcolaci who change into wolves
details.wants: Their communities kept safe from vampires

neighbours.name: The Folk Witches
neighbours.summary:
Folk witches (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, chapter three) are common in the Tribunal, drawn, like many lesser traditions, by Hungary's old law that witches do not exist and so may not be tried; the Tribunal itself polices hedge wizards instead, and most keep their heads down. In the southern mountains around Maramures the Vlach vrajitoarele lead the scattered cults of Zalmoxis; their powers belong to the Magic realm, with no Infernal taint. Ludmilla, a Romanian strigoica who tutors at the Scholomance, leads a coven and recruits for it among the school's pupils.

Their lore has a use for magi: witches break fevers with a potion of roof tar from the four corner houses of a village, and on Saint John's Eve that tar holds a little Creo vis (see the Slav lands).

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

details.wants: To be left alone, and new recruits

neighbours.name: The Strigoi Vii
neighbours.summary:
Living vampires: Romanian strigoi vii (strigoi viu, feminine strigoica), the vjestitze of the Balkans. They are human witches, not faeries, and need no blood to live, though they drink it. By night one leaves her body as an owl, a black hen, a moth or a fly and feeds on the heart-blood of sleepers, most often children. They gather in covens of women, and folk say they rule the dead vampires, meeting them at district boundaries to plan the year's harm. When one dies, powerful vampiric faeries gather.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

They are Nightwalkers (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, chapter six) and may have more: Infernal witches with maleficia or Goetic Arts to rule the dead, or faerie wizards using the Ars Fabulosa to call and bind vampires.

details.rules: Only women; a girl may learn the craft by joining a coven
details.wants: The heart-blood of the young; command of the dead vampires

neighbours.name: The Cuman Shamans
neighbours.summary:
The magicians of the Tengrist Cumans, who worship a sky god as creator. Their powers resemble the taltós's: scrying, weather-working, quick healing and fast travel. None seem as strong as the Bulgar shamans were before Christianity; some Tremere think something else destroyed those, others that the Cumans' strongest shamans simply stay out of the border wars.

A member is played from the tradition record the faction names: its powers are summarised here, and what the record only notes is in Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

neighbours.name: The Pecheneg Shamans
neighbours.summary:
When the Byzantines took the Pechenegs' lands and the Hungarian kings settled them in the southern Carpathians, their shamans went into House Tremere's service with many of their warriors. They count as hospites.

No tradition record covers them: their powers are summarised here, and a member who needs them is played from Against the Dark (chapter nine) and Hedge Magic Revised Edition.

neighbours.name: The Dragon War
neighbours.summary:
Hundreds of dragons, perhaps thousands, lair in the Tribunal's mountains, gorges, lakes and forests. They are of two kinds that hate each other: the aždaje, Infernal beasts that plunder for the joy of harm and rank themselves by force, and the zmajevi, Magic dragons that covet wives and gold as much but hardly notice the misery they cause, and rank themselves by remembered favours and slights. Intellego Vim tells the two apart, one realm at a time.

Since the second century they have been held to the Pax Draconis, the treaty of Fetillusclaviceps, a Roman dragon who beat the twelve-headed zmaj Abur-ciocîrlie in a duel and brought the aždaje to heel by helping Slomljenakrila kill the oath-breaking Britvazub. Under its terms dragons do not league against one another, keep their quarrels local, defer to the stronger and leave men alone unless attacked; a wife may be taken only with a superior's leave, and a dragon that takes one without it is outlawed and may be hunted for its hoard. The peace holds only while its keeper is feared, and Fetillusclaviceps has not been seen for fifty years. Early in the ninth century Tremere himself put down a rising of raiders while wearing the Roman dragon's shape, and some Tremere wonder whether later sightings were their own sodales doing the same.

If the peace fails, every dragon settles old scores and seizes what it can, raiding towns for gold and slaves. Dragons of one kind may band together, rarely with the other. House Tremere, the Order's self-appointed soldiers, would see in such a war both a catastrophe and its chance to prove itself to the whole Order.

A saga frame, not a single story: choose the spark that suits the troupe (best of all one the player characters struck themselves, perhaps with charges laid against them for it), escalate through situations that come ever closer to what they hold dear, and let them make the ending. A peasant legend that a devil's wizard from the Scholomance rides an aždaja and makes the storms can be woven in: a storm wizard, a shapechanged magus, or a magus corrupted to lead the Infernal dragons.

details.antagonist: The dragons of the Tribunal, once the Pax Draconis fails

stages.title: The spark
stages.clues: Choose one, or let the player characters strike it. Veles wakes as the Slavs return to Perun, and drives his dragons to war (zmajevi if he is of Magic, aždaje if he is a demon). Abur-ciocîrlie leaves his castle and persuades other zmajevi that the magi serve the Roman dragon, perhaps killing a zmaj and leaving its hoard in an abandoned Kezdö Válasz fort. Dragons find the lost treasury of Decebalus and fight over it. The aždaja Rabidanadas, seeing Akgah's success in Thebes, leads a band against Bulgaria. Dragons or magi learn that the Roman dragon has long been a magus in disguise. Leontine of Old Histria quarrels with her zmaj partner over the Golden Mean, their column goes missing, and the zmaj's kin fall on Old Histria. Or magi rescue a boyar's stolen daughter, or drive a zmaj from a regio they covet, and the dragon they humbled rouses others.
stages.ignored: One band breaks the peace; others test their bounds, and raids become war.
stages.stopped: The quarrel is mended, the hoard shared out or the rumour quashed before a second dragon joins in.
stages.turned: The troupe learns early who struck the spark, the key to the ending.

stages.title: Sound the alarm
stages.clues: Word must go to the five legal covenants and from them to every oppidum, to the Prima, the Quaesitors, the Redcaps and the hoplites. Messengers cross the worst country in the Tribunal, hunt for absent magi, and convince doubting elders that this is more than one dragon's raid.
stages.ignored: The Tribunal is caught unready when the first blows fall.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal mobilises in good time.
stages.turned: The bearers of the news win the Prima's ear and a place in the councils of war.

stages.title: Rush to the front
stages.clues: House Tremere moves while other Houses debate. Orders go out according to rank and privilege, forces are mustered and the site of the first fighting is searched. The dragons fly, so the front is hard to find; they favour the mountains, and the defences of Laniena, the Scholomance, Coeris and Lycaneon are seen to first.
stages.ignored: The mountain oppida stand alone.
stages.stopped: The oppida's defences are readied in time.
stages.turned: Player magi take command of a sector of the war, or of its supplies.

stages.title: The first assault
stages.clues: The Scholomance closes its classes and sends its apprentices and mundane scholars south through the Bran Pass into Bulgaria in the troupe's care. On the road, aždaje fall on a smaller band of zmajevi in the sky and the fight comes down around the column.
stages.ignored: Scholars die, and with them the school's future agents.
stages.stopped: The column reaches safety unseen.
stages.turned: Magi who can tell the two kinds apart help the zmajevi, and win Magic dragons as allies.

stages.title: Consequences
stages.clues: The war tears through the Tribunal's other supernatural folk, killing faeries and driving others from their homes. Three enraged giants wreck a crowded village.
stages.ignored: The giants' rampage spreads.
stages.stopped: The giants are slain.
stages.turned: The giants are calmed or resettled, perhaps with the help of storm wizards who know their kind.

stages.title: A city in flames
stages.clues: A flight of zmajevi comes to burn Veszprém, home of the college library many magi have quietly read and borrowed from.
stages.ignored: The city and its library burn, a loss to Hermetic scholars.
stages.stopped: The dragons are driven off.
stages.turned: Saving the city wins the bishop's gratitude, and in time the king's.

stages.title: The first to fall
stages.clues: An oppidum is lost, best of all one the troupe cares for. For example, an aždaja finds Laniena and is beaten back, but kills several hunters; hours after the troupe arrives, twenty-five aždaje fill the sky, and Lexander resolves to abandon the caves and save what he can.
stages.ignored: The oppidum and its people are lost.
stages.stopped: The evacuation saves its magi, books and vis, though the site is gone.
stages.turned: The troupe earns the gratitude of the oppidum's survivors, and perhaps the right to rebuild it.

stages.title: Returning the blow
stages.clues: A mountain nest is found where more than fifty zmajevi rest between raids, and there is time to gather the Tribunal's forces against it.
stages.ignored: The nest keeps feeding the raids.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal's strike scatters the nest.
stages.turned: The troupe plans and leads the blow, and its names go into the Tribunal's chronicle.

stages.title: Containing the fire
stages.clues: The war threatens to spill into the Greater Alps, Novgorod, Thebes and Rome. House Tremere has staked its standing, perhaps its existence, on keeping it inside the ring of mountains.
stages.ignored: The war reaches other Tribunals, and the Order holds House Tremere to account.
stages.stopped: The dragons are held within the Tribunal's mountains.
stages.turned: The House's credit across the Order rises.

stages.title: The climax
stages.clues: Each ending answers a spark. Destroy Veles, first quelling Perun's revived worship, by knights or by magi turned missionaries. Prove Abur-ciocîrlie a liar and beat him in a duel, or find Fetillusclaviceps to fight him. Share Decebalus's gold out among the zmajevi by rank and enforce the share, perhaps destroying every aždaja beside them. Go to Thebes and destroy Akgah, without which Rabidanadas cannot be beaten. Unmask the magus who plays the Roman dragon and find a true keeper for the peace. Or recover the stolen column so Leontine and her zmaj can make peace.
stages.ignored: The dragons level cities and topple kingdoms; rivers boil dry and the face of the Tribunal is changed for ever.
stages.stopped: A new peace binds the dragons, or the aždaje are destroyed.
stages.turned: Ending the war through Thebes could heal the old wound between the two Tribunals and clear House Tremere's name at last.

links.note: Giants the war could drive to rampage
Its old forts could be used to frame it

secrets.title: Who keeps the peace
secrets.text: A renowned Flambeau hunter tracked Fetillusclaviceps to its lair and killed it about a century ago, then, seeing that the peace died with it, has played the Roman dragon ever since rather than confess. If the troupe uncovers this, continuing the pretence is probably a breach of the Code, since it means dealing with Infernal beasts, and House Tremere's good name rides on whether a substitute keeper can be found.

secrets.title: The stolen column
secrets.text: The stone column where Leontine of Old Histria argues ethics with an ancient zmaj was taken by Dominic of Tytalus, aedile of Coeris, perhaps to test his protégé and perhaps to start the war on purpose. Dominic then vanishes, dead or in hiding, and the column may lie somewhere within Coeris's defences.

secrets.title: Sebastian and the zmaj king
secrets.text: Sebastian, the ageless caretaker of the Scholomance, may be the seven-headed zmaj king Aževastjepan, who rules the Carpathian dragons and has banished aždaje from his realm.

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: Who keeps the peace and the stolen column are two of the endings the book offers.

neighbours.name: The Teutonic Expulsion
neighbours.summary:
In 1211 King Andrew II granted the Burzenland to the Teutonic Knights, free of taxes and dues though he kept the coinage and half the gold and silver mined, to hold the Carpathian passes against the Cumans. Brother Theoderich runs the mission almost alone while the hochmeister, Hermann von Salza, divides his time between the Holy Land and Egypt. In nine years the knights have built forts and are finishing five castles around Kronstadt, settled Saxons to feed them, quarrelled with the local bishop over his rights, and courted the pope to slip free of Hungary. They mean to push down the Danube to the Black Sea and reopen the land road to Constantinople.

House Tremere has forbidden formal contact with the knights. The pope has charged them to root out heresy and diabolism, and the Tremere fear they will count the Order of Hermes among the pagans and idolaters; the knights have also heard of the Scholomance. The Order cannot stay hidden from them much longer. An isolated order with few friends among the Hungarians might accept a hand held out, but the Code makes such friendship delicate.

details.antagonist: The Teutonic Knights under Brother Theoderich

stages.title: The captured hedge wizard
stages.clues: A pagan hedge wizard with a grudge against the Order of Hermes falls into a garrison's hands and tells the knights all he knows of magi, and more. Soon the garrison chooses Hermetic targets.
stages.ignored: The knights move against the Order as heretics, and the secret is out.
stages.stopped: The troupe deals with the garrison, revealing as little as it can or leaving no witnesses, and answers for breaking the Tremere edict either way.
stages.turned: The troupe sets the knights' errors right with care, and opens a quiet channel to the order.

stages.title: The Golden Bull
stages.clues: If history holds, the nobles, restless since Andrew II came home from crusade in 1218, force on him the Golden Bull, which lets them check the king's acts. He still refuses to take back the Burzenland.
stages.ignored: The nobles' grudge against the knights deepens.
stages.stopped: The king revokes the grant while there is still peace.
stages.turned: Magi who can sway the barons decide which way the Burzenland goes.

stages.title: A fief of the Holy See
stages.clues: If history holds, Hermann von Salza uses his credit with the pope to make the Burzenland a papal fief. The king cannot lose the land; the knights demand a second hearing and will not go.
stages.ignored: Royal troops drive the knights out by force, and their castles stand empty.
stages.stopped: The knights stay in Hungary on new terms.
stages.turned: The troupe claims a castle site, or a grateful knight's friendship, from the wreck.

stages.title: The Cumans return
stages.clues: If history holds, with the passes unguarded the Cumans pour into the Danube basin, pressed from the east by the Great Khan's horde.
stages.ignored: The Cumans trouble Hungary for the rest of the century.
stages.stopped: The passes are held by other hands.
stages.turned: Magi who befriend the Cumans gain allies on the frontier.

secrets.title: A pious Order
secrets.text: A pious Teutonic Order is mundane.

secrets.title: A holier Order
secrets.text: A holier Teutonic Order makes Dominion auras of a brave temper on the land it conquers and keeps an inner circle of Divine wonder-workers.

secrets.title: A profane Order
secrets.text: A profane Teutonic Order serves Hell: its leaders are goetic sorcerers, its knights take part in infernal rites, it seizes shamans, witches and taltós for their lore, and its favoured knights carry great swords with a demon bound inside that whispers in their dreams.

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: The book offers three Teutonic Orders.

neighbours.name: The Mongols
neighbours.summary:
Beyond the Cuman steppe a greater power is stirring. If history holds, the Mongols come west in waves through the middle of the century, first breaking the Cumans, then driving whole peoples before them, and at last falling on Hungary itself. To the Tribunal's people they will seem as alien as any monster, a horde no one can defeat and few escape, which makes them the natural foe of a horror story.

Tablinum is rumoured to hide the Refuge, a network of regiones stocked with laboratories where House Tremere could outlast any calamity. True or not, desperate magi will flock there if the horde comes.

details.antagonist: The Mongol horde

stages.title: The Kalka
stages.clues: If history holds, the Mongols shatter the Cuman confederacy at the Kalka. Twenty thousand Cuman families enter Hungary, promising to be baptised and to fight the Mongols if they come back; other Cumans are swallowed by the Golden Horde.
stages.ignored: Hungary fills with uneasy pagan settlers.
stages.stopped: The Cumans are turned away, and the border burns.
stages.turned: Magi win the newcomers' shamans as friends, and news of the enemy beyond them.

stages.title: Thrace emptied
stages.clues: If history holds, a vast migration lays Thrace waste, and ten thousand Cuman families take service with the Nicene emperor for land.
stages.ignored: The south fills with refugees and raiders.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal's frontier oppida stand firm.
stages.turned: The troupe learns how the horde fights, before it arrives.

stages.title: The invasion
stages.clues: If history holds, the horde falls on Hungary and its neighbours, ending the Bosnian war and every other quarrel.
stages.ignored: Towns burn and oppida are overrun; magi run for the Refuge, if it exists.
stages.stopped: The horde is turned back or passes by.
stages.turned: The troupe shelters the realm's survivors and shapes what rises from the ashes.

neighbours.name: The Bosnian Crusade
neighbours.summary:
The Bosnian Church, heir to the Bogomils who survived Stefan Nemanja's purge, calls its faithful Patarians and keeps to itself. The King of Hungary has written ordering it to purge them; it answers that Bosnia has no heretics. Pope Honorius III has sent a legate to urge Andrew II on, clerics preach against the Patarians, and Hungarian knights are gathering.

House Tremere has not decided what to do. The Oath forbids meddling with mundanes, yet a crusade could remake the Tribunal, and the House remembers how the Fourth Crusade broke Thebes. Several of its leaders know Hungarians, Bosnians and Patarians personally, and the House watches the border for the small incident that could set it alight. In Vrhbosna the Mercere keep one of their oldest mansiones, a quarrelsome place where a brawl ended in murder a year ago.

details.antagonist: The crusaders of Hungary and Croatia

stages.title: The legate's sermons
stages.clues: Warriors muster across the Tribunal and preachers denounce the heretics; rumours of a crusade are easily believed.
stages.ignored: The muster goes on, and the House stays undecided.
stages.stopped: The troupe quietly takes the heat out of the border quarrels, within the Code.
stages.turned: Magi with friends on both sides become the House's go-betweens.

stages.title: The crusade
stages.clues: If history holds, after a dozen quiet years Pope Gregory IX persuades the Duke of Croatia to take the cross against Bosnia. The crusade loses its purpose and becomes a war between Bosnia and Hungary.
stages.ignored: Villages burn far from any heretic, and the war drags on.
stages.stopped: The crusade is turned aside before it reaches Bosnia.
stages.turned: The troupe protects what the House values in its path.

stages.title: Ended by the horde
stages.clues: If history holds, the Mongol invasion turns every ruler's eyes elsewhere, and the war ends.
stages.ignored: Bosnia is left exhausted.
stages.stopped: The war ends sooner.
stages.turned: The Bosnian Church survives, owing the troupe a debt.

secrets.title: An aura in the mansio
secrets.text: Some suspect an Infernal aura has grown in the Vrhbosna mansio; none has been detected yet.

neighbours.name: The Valley of the Thracian Kings
neighbours.summary:
Four years ago a Tremere necromancer, then a hoplite, found the burial ground of the ancient Thracian kings near Seuthopolis, their old capital. The House's necromancers are delighted, and House Verditius wants a dig too, since the Thracians worshipped smith-gods. Benilda, who never trusts a cheerful necromancer, is blocking access for now, but she knows the Tremere will win in the end and hopes to look first or to choose who digs and why.

Seuthopolis itself began as a covenant of Verditius magi of the Cabeiri cult; House Guernicus now forbids its members to worship the old chthonic gods, and has removed three from office for irrationality that looked like the cult's hubris.

details.antagonist: The magician-kings of Thrace and their guardians

stages.title: Benilda's survey
stages.clues: Benilda quietly asks trusted magi to look over the valley before the Tremere can force the matter.
stages.ignored: The Tremere win access on their own terms.
stages.stopped: The valley stays closed a while longer.
stages.turned: The troupe's report decides who leads the dig, and Benilda owes it.

stages.title: The dig
stages.clues: The excavation begins and must be hidden from mundanes; the tombs are cunningly trapped.
stages.ignored: Diggers die and the locals talk.
stages.stopped: The dig is halted.
stages.turned: The troupe brings out grave goods intact.

stages.title: The guardians loosed
stages.clues: Spirits the magician-kings set to guard their tombs wake when the robbers break in.
stages.ignored: The guardians haunt Seuthopolis and the pass.
stages.stopped: The spirits are laid or bound.
stages.turned: The guardians are pacified and their lore learned.

stages.title: The Cabeiri
stages.clues: The recovered items need assessing, and may serve Original Research. The trail leads to the Cabeiri, the Thracians' gods, perhaps through journeys into the Magic or Faerie realms, or to initiations in their Mystery.
stages.ignored: The Cabeiri's hubris spreads among the Quaesitors.
stages.stopped: The cult stays buried.
stages.turned: The troupe gains a breakthrough, or an initiation, from the kings' legacy.

neighbours.name: The Return of Zalmoxis
neighbours.summary:
The Geto-Dacians worshipped Zalmoxis before Christ, and his rich, secretive cult went into hiding in the Carpathians as the people converted. The cult says he learned magic from Pythagoras on Samos and the secrets of immortality in Egypt, then spent three years in a cave on holy Kogaionon and came out to teach that the soul does not die. Every five years it sends a messenger to its god by throwing him onto spear points: if he dies, the god has accepted him.

In the southern mountains around Maramures several groups of cultists each follow a vrajitoarea, a Vlach folk witch. One of them has the Gift and is slowly drawing the others to him, though his Gift keeps them at a distance. Then he learns that a wizard called Zalmoxis lives in the hollow mountain nearby.

details.antagonist: A Gifted vrajitoarea of the Cult of Zalmoxis

stages.title: The cults unite
stages.clues: The Gifted witch proclaims that the god has risen again and is held prisoner by the other wizards of the mountain, and the scattered cults rally to him.
stages.ignored: The cult grows bold and numerous.
stages.stopped: The cults stay divided.
stages.turned: The troupe learns of the cult before Lycaneon does.

stages.title: Pilgrims at the mountain
stages.clues: Strangers watch Lycaneon's approaches, ask after the old wizard among its servants and miners, and a messenger is sent to the spears.
stages.ignored: The cult finds a way in.
stages.stopped: The watchers are caught and questioned.
stages.turned: Zalmoxis himself, vain as he is, may be persuaded to play the god and send the faithful home.

stages.title: The rescue
stages.clues: The faithful try to free their god by force or guile, with folk witchcraft and the Gifted leader's spells.
stages.ignored: Blood is spilt at the House's manufactory, and the Tribunal's secrecy suffers.
stages.stopped: The cult is broken.
stages.turned: The witches become the Order's allies, or its informants.

secrets.title: Archmagus Zalmoxis
secrets.text: Archmagus Zalmoxis of Verditius, Lycaneon's longevity specialist, is only named after the god and has nothing to do with the cult.

secrets.title: What Lycaneon knows
secrets.text: The magi of Lycaneon know nothing of what is brewing among the cults of Zalmoxis.

secrets.title: The vrajitoarele's powers
secrets.text: The vrajitoarele belong to the Magic realm; none of their powers is Infernal.

neighbours.name: The Székely Taltós
neighbours.summary:
Serb and Croat legend says a hermit taltós of matchless power led the Slavs south from beyond the Carpathians, and that in hard times another will come to free the people from their masters. The tale is loved most in the poor communities of the forest glens and the upper Danube.

The Székely, Magyars thought lesser by their kin, were settled on the kingdom's eastern edge to hold off Cuman and Mongol raiders. They are reckoned the fiercest warriors in the Tribunal and once followed shape-changing taltós into battle. Now a mysterious man preaches in their villages, and the Székely have turned on their Vlach and Saxon neighbours. The Vlachs say a Magyar taltós has won back his tradition's old power, called lesser taltós to him and is building an empire. House Tremere ought to look into it.

The true taltós destroyed one another a thousand years ago, so a taltós of real power would be a marvel. Laniena trains its Fectores with initiation scripts taken from a taltós clan, and Tatiana, the Prima's spymistress, was born a Szekler.

details.antagonist: A taltós preacher among the Székely

stages.title: The preacher
stages.clues: Border raids by the Székely rise; a stranger preaches deliverance from village to village.
stages.ignored: The Székely find a common voice.
stages.stopped: The preacher is discredited or vanishes.
stages.turned: The troupe meets him and learns what he wants.

stages.title: The lesser taltós
stages.clues: Hedge wizards gather to him; spirit battles and shapechangers are reported along the frontier.
stages.ignored: A hedge tradition of power reborn on the Order's doorstep.
stages.stopped: The gathering breaks apart, or joins the Order.
stages.turned: The Fectores or the troupe win the taltós' lore.

stages.title: A new power
stages.clues: The Székely rise against their neighbours and their king under the taltós' banner.
stages.ignored: A new and volatile power stands in the east, and the frontier against the Cumans and Mongols cracks.
stages.stopped: The rising fails.
stages.turned: The taltós becomes a ruler who owes his throne to the troupe.

neighbours.name: Poena's Succession
neighbours.summary:
House Tremere's leader is chosen by appointment and certamen, a quick and plain method that does not stop magi from trying to sway it. Poena has been Prima for two years. Her legata, Monica Ierne, is her heir: if Poena dies or is unfit, Monica acts as Prima until an emergency council meets. Monica does not want the office and would take it only to keep out someone odious; as Prima she would push for the leader to be chosen by a duel of champions, then resign. Horatius, who helped Poena to power, would make a good compromise if the House split, and would plant oppida round the Black Sea. Janus will never stand, for fear of what would come out.

The previous Primus nominally leads the Burning Acorns hunt for Diedne survivors. The House has lost touch with him deep in the Novgorod Tribunal, and he knows the House's structure and Coeris's defences.

details.antagonist: The House's rival candidates

stages.title: The illness
stages.clues: Poena learns she has an illness that will weaken her and may cloud her judgement. Without alarming the House she sends envoys to size up possible successors, meaning to choose and train one for a deciding certamen at the next Decennial.
stages.ignored: The envoys' reports decide the House's future unseen.
stages.stopped: A cure is found, and the matter is shelved.
stages.turned: The troupe's candidate becomes Poena's choice.

stages.title: The lost Primus
stages.clues: Word comes that the past Primus is missing in Novgorod; what he knows of Coeris would be priceless to an enemy or a rival.
stages.ignored: His knowledge falls into other hands.
stages.stopped: He is found and brought home.
stages.turned: He backs the troupe's candidate.

stages.title: Failing strength
stages.clues: Poena weakens faster than she planned. Those who know can conceal it, so the House's rivals stay busy with their own work, or give her away and let a stronger hand take the House at once.
stages.ignored: Rumour spreads and the councilors begin to manoeuvre.
stages.stopped: The secret is kept until the Decennial.
stages.turned: The troupe chooses when the House learns of it.

stages.title: Prima pro tempore
stages.clues: Poena dies and Monica acts as Prima. The troupe is sent to summon the councilors and gauge each one's ambitions, policies and support; Monica uses the interval to finish Poena's plans and rush through a few of her own.
stages.ignored: The succession is settled by certamen among whoever pushes hardest.
stages.stopped: A worthy successor is agreed before the duel.
stages.turned: Loyal servants of Poena get to pitch their wildest schemes to a sympathetic Prima.

secrets.title: Why Janus will not stand
secrets.text: Janus is a lycanthrope, which is why he will never seek the office.

neighbours.name: The Papal Legate
neighbours.summary:
Across the Balkans and as far as the Emperor's court, people tell of the Devil's school in the mountains, whose ten pupils learn every secret of nature and magic in seven years, and one of whom the Devil keeps. In truth it is the Scholomance, an oppidum's school for agents, companions, future Redcaps and apprentices. The Church has sent a papal legate to look into it. He lodges with the Teutonic Knights while he builds his case, and has found only hearsay, since the only people who know anything are magi or their former pupils.

The school no longer wipes its mundane pupils' memories as it once did: its policy now is to make friends for the Order, neither boasting of its masters nor denying them. That leaves many former pupils who could talk.

details.antagonist: The papal legate, lodged with the Teutonic Knights

stages.title: Hearsay
stages.clues: The legate questions travellers, priests and nobles about the Devil's school; the knights, who have heard the same tale, help him.
stages.ignored: His questions draw nearer to former pupils.
stages.stopped: He is satisfied the school is a legend.
stages.turned: The troupe feeds him a harmless trail.

stages.title: A witness
stages.clues: A former mundane pupil, a bishop or a nobleman perhaps, is pressed to say what he learned in the mountains.
stages.ignored: The legate gains a sworn witness.
stages.stopped: The witness keeps faith with his school.
stages.turned: The witness becomes the troupe's man in the legate's household.

stages.title: The castle in the storm
stages.clues: The legate goes into the mountains south of Hermannstadt in search of the tower that shows itself only in storms.
stages.ignored: He finds the school, or something worse, and the knights learn where the Order lives.
stages.stopped: He goes home with nothing.
stages.turned: The school is shown to him in its best light, and he reports a harmless academy to Rome.

secrets.title: Sebastian and the zmaj king
secrets.text: Sebastian, the Scholomance's ageless caretaker, may be the zmaj king Aževastjepan; a legate who found him would find more than he bargained for.

neighbours.name: Danaslepih's Grove
neighbours.summary: A thick stand of horse-chestnuts on the Drina in western Serbia, the lair of the blind zmaj Danaslepih (see the Bestiary), who withers any crop sown near it.

characters.summary: Archmage, Prima of House Bonisagus, leader of Durenmar, leader of the Oak Gild and, as holder of Bonisagus's sigil, Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal: the most politically powerful maga in the Tribunal. Haughty and overbearing, she wants Durenmar and the Rhine restored to the first place in the Order, and so quietly favours the Ash Gild's war on the Norse wizards, which would draw mighty magi and loot to the Rhine. Brilliant in every Art, above all Rego and Imaginem; she wears a great cloak of white feathers enchanted with illusions, and there are theories about whom she has impersonated in it. Her familiar is the raven Kolkrabus.

secrets.title: Murion's raven
secrets.text: She sends Kolkrabus to spy on Dankmar and on others she takes for enemies, in breach of the Code.

characters.name: Andrus

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, Colens Arcanorum and librarian of the Great Library, Murion's first filius, about forty years past his Gauntlet. Thin and balding with a perceptive, commanding stare, he decides who may use the library and which gifts it accepts, so he is unwise to annoy. His duties keep him at the covenant and away from his own research. Many see him as Murion's puppet; rumour says he is preparing to challenge for Archmage within ten years.

characters.name: Tandaline

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, of the Trianoma lineage, Murion's closest confidante and her appointed Tenens Occultorum. Pale and slender, with eyes that shift colour hypnotically; a master of Muto and Auram for decades, she studies the air by turning herself into vapour. Politically Murion's ally, yet respected as a free thinker in her own right; she writes to many Bonisagus magi and uses those connections to punish anyone reported to have abused one of the House. Her apprentice is Petrus Virilis's Gifted son.

characters.name: Caecilius

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Archmage of House Bonisagus, the most venerable magus of Durenmar, senior Quaesitor of the Rhine Tribunal and the greatest living exponent of Intellego. Appointed Quaesitor long ago, it is said unwillingly and out of duty when the Tribunal's Quaesitorial presence was thin; his research extends the investigative rituals of House Guernicus. Reluctant and slow to act, with ever more frequent Twilight episodes, he is nonetheless a brilliant investigator with a spotless record who has solved many Hermetic crimes, and he adjudicates at Tribunal. His familiar is a silver-coated wolf.

characters.name: Occultes

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, leader of the Linden Gild and figurehead of Durenmar's outward-looking faction, which would admit exotic magic; a sizeable minority of the House would rather have him as Primus. A colourful man who researches manuscripts and items of every kind, has made a small golem that serves in his lab, enchanted many texts and quills, and collects news of artifacts and strange practices from far away. He was librarian until the former Primus Avarret removed him. Murion tolerates and watches him, judging his ambitions modest and fearing a schism in the House if she moved against him.

secrets.title: The restricted texts
secrets.text: He knows the restricted texts and has quietly copied or moved the most interesting into his own sanctum, passing them to close allies whose research they suit.

characters.name: Ricardus Caespuus

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Bonisagus, a recluse whose sanctum on the covenant's southern edge is a great building walled almost entirely in glass, thousands of lead-framed panes on timber beams, unlike anything else in the century. Inside is a Herbam laboratory full of exotic plants from which he cultivates several kinds of vis, much as others extract it. Earnest and friendly but understood by nobody; Murion's circle rate him little better than a hedge wizard and bear with him for his harvests and his steady gifts to the stores.

characters.name: Petrus Virilis

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Bonisagus, an otherwise mediocre magus whose seed is Vim vis, whether by faerie gift or through the obsessive research into fertility and the Gift of his liberal-minded mater Susanna, now in Final Twilight. Tandaline talked him into an experiment that fathered a Gifted son on a serving maid, now her apprentice, and on Murion's orders he has fathered four more, all Gifted, and all sons when born at Durenmar because of Philippus Niger's Twilight scar. Averse to sex and ill at ease with women, he would keep his vis to himself, but the covenant deems his talent too valuable; interested young magae write to him.

secrets.title: A longevity ritual
secrets.text: He plans to invent a longevity ritual that would probably leave him infertile; Murion would be furious.

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: A maga wanting a Gifted child must offer more than seduction; he might instead fall for a peasant girl and plan a wedding in a nearby town.

characters.name: Winfrida

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Guernicus and Quaesitor, young, inexperienced and timid, admitted some years ago because a Guernicus must always be at Durenmar; she passed her Gauntlet in the Greater Alps. She would secretly rather live the research life of a Bonisagus. She and Tabanus may be the only two Guernicus in the Rhine; Murion is grooming and indoctrinating her, confusing her loyalties, and Tabanus thinks her weak.

characters.name: Philippus Niger

description.biography: Equipment: clothes, a dagger and a long sword; Encumbrance 1 (1). Talisman: the Knife of Human Bone; he also owns the Wizard's Bridle and the Subtle Chain. Familiar: Sordus, a basilisk. Twilight Scars: he seems to swell when angry, his shadow sometimes moves of itself, he knows true gold from false, only boys are born where he has lived a year, he sours wine, loud noise pains him, black animals gather round him outdoors, and flames dim when he comes in. His focus and his Ambitious Flaw come with his Mythic Blood, whose feat lets him smell magic. Chaos of the Angry Waves came from a Twilight. He knows Demon's Eternal Oblivion and Wind of Mundane Silence at levels 25 and 50, and Dreadful Bane of the Fae and Sap the Griffon's Strength at 30 and 50. His two Shattering spells are versions of Shattering the Malicious (Rune), each aimed at one rune. From forty years past his Gauntlet he learned his spells as laboratory projects. The book prints Encumbrance 3 (3), Chaos of the Angry Waves 20, Flaws of the Weaponsmith 25 and one Shattering the Malicious Rune (30 and 50); the errata correct them.

characters.summary: Archmage of House Flambeau, of the Apromor lineage, leading figure of the Ash Gild and Protector of Durenmar, chosen by Murion, whose political ally he is. Called the Black: a smallish, well-built, cool and reserved man who looks ninety, somewhat deaf, bowed and creaky, in a black hooded cloak over darkest grey with a serrated dagger of human bone, his talisman, always at his belt. He has spent his life defending the Order against non-Hermetic wizards and is the Order's foremost master of Perdo; now, with Final Twilight near, he turns to politics, driving the Ash Gild's push for war on the Norse wizards beyond the Baltic and pressing Oculus Septentrionalis to investigate harder and to open a Mercere Portal to Durenmar, which would wound Fengheld. Most of Fengheld and its allies oppose him and several hedge wizards want him dead; he lives in the Watchtower on the cliffs, built apart so that his familiar Sordus, a basilisk whose gaze kills and whose presence withers plants and fouls water, should not blight the valley. His Twilight scars are many: he seems to grow when angry, his shadow moves on its own, flames dim when he enters, wine sours near him, black animals follow him, and only sons are born where he has lived a year. He has trained four apprentices and made the Wizard's Bridle, which binds a magus's words and gestures, and the Subtle Chain, a silver loop that lays six wards at once.

characters.summary: Master of House Verditius and Artificer of Durenmar, the honorary post that crafts items for the covenant's glory. She lives in Verditius' Forge, the half-buried laboratory the Founder built when he came to study with Bonisagus.

characters.summary: Master of House Mercere, the only Gifted Mercere in the Rhine and the Tribunal's archivist. He oversees the Mercer House in the basement of the Tower of Trianoma, which serves the southern Tribunal, and is content that Horst of Fengheld leads the Rhine's Redcaps from the other Mercer House.

characters.name: Sula
characters.summary: Autocrat of Durenmar: a wrinkled, gentle woman past ninety and still hale, who arranges lodging for guests and places visitors with uncanny ease.

characters.name: Schadrit

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Ex Miscellanea, co-founder and iron-handed ruler of Dankmar. Trained as a Bonisagus apprentice at Durenmar under Aschlaranda, expelled with her mistress a year before her Gauntlet and finished outside the House. A withered hag in a voluminous hooded black robe, her face a mass of wrinkles about a long mole-covered nose; her longevity ritual kept her alive but not her looks. An expert in Faerie Magic, taught by Orphedra, and perhaps its only practitioner outside House Merinita; malicious to the point of evil.

characters.name: Orphedra

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Merinita and the covenant's link to the forest fae. Apprenticed at Irencillia a hundred and twenty years ago, she found it stifling and sought the primeval dark instead. Stick-thin, hair in a tight bun, angular, with unnaturally smooth skin and an air that makes the covenfolk's skin crawl. She revels in Faerie Magic, which she taught Schadrit, leans to the dark fae, works in illusion, cold, darkness and fear, cast the covenant's Shrouded Glen, and has a deal with the local bockmen to patrol its surroundings.

characters.name: Jiphella

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Ex Miscellanea and master of Mentem, Schadrit's own daughter, conceived under a dark faerie charm long after her mother's longevity ritual, trained by her and wholly cowed by her. Immense and bloated, with lank greasy grey hair and a sickly orange left eye with a blood-red iris that bewitches with a glance; most of the covenfolk are under her spell and worship her. She was Dankmar's only delegate at the Tribunal of 1214, where she denied any part in St Georgen's fall.

characters.name: Larinda

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Ex Miscellanea, Jiphella's daughter and filia, conceived under the same charm. Pretty and sunny despite a cruel mother and a domineering grandmother, whom she obeys out of family duty. Her affinities are for the natural world, Animal, Herbam, Aquam and Auram, and she is becoming an expert brewer of potions. The rest of her traits are lost in the source.

characters.summary: Master of House Tremere, co-leader of the Apple Gild and princeps of Triamore. Stern, uncompromising and politic, she has kept the Quaesitores at bay and champions the Lotharingian Tribunal, courting the covenants of Normandy. She has trained two apprentices.

characters.summary: Master of House Jerbiton, a friendly, effusive polymath: scholar, fighter, hunter, musician and poet, mostly without recourse to magic, though he knows many useful spells.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Tremere, newly Gauntleted filius of Goliard, a famed maga of Stonehenge, and admitted on her recommendation. He has yet to prove himself.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Tremere and devious co-founder of Waddenzee, an Englishman trained at Blackthorn in Stonehenge. Scrupulously honest with Quaesitores, whom he secretly longs to join, and arrogant to everyone else, he lies, cheats and steals whenever it serves. Well groomed, looking in his late thirties, dressed to show his wealth; a Mentem specialist, above all Rego Mentem, who leans heavily on Aura of Rightful Authority.

characters.name: Eric Ribecus

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Tytalus, co-founder of Waddenzee and its most committed pirate: a black-haired Dane from Ribe, dashing, charming and extroverted, with a swollen opinion of himself, who looks far younger than he is thanks to illusions and a good longevity ritual. A generalist favouring Aquam and Auram, he fights beside his men with a magical sword; his familiar is Aegir, a long-tailed skua. His younger cousin Estrid Danesson of Oculus Septentrionalis is his bitter enemy.

characters.name: Lucas von Beck

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Flambeau, son of a German altgraf whose family believes him dead; he keeps a nobleman's habits. Very tall and stocky, always in black, and since a Twilight his clothes fall to pieces when he casts too much. A short-tempered expert in Perdo who kills troublesome mundanes with Perdo Corpus; he has lately taken up necromancy, using the pirates' victims and the Pirates' Graveyards.

characters.name: Hachim al'Khalejj

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Criamon, a quiet, naive Muslim, filius of Hassan El-Megrayhi of Fengheld, who fell in with the pirates by chance. His astrology helps plan their raids. He dresses in stolen cream and blue silks and walks with a limp.

characters.name: Aethelbald
characters.summary: A deputy of the magi who claims to be the Saxon heir to the English crown.

characters.name: Bjorn Ironside
characters.summary: Ship's master of the Nebelkönigin, Waddenzee's stolen flagship.

characters.name: Calum
characters.summary: A lapsed priest who gives the pirates a heretical spiritual ministry.

characters.name: Aelfhere
characters.summary: A Frisian shipwright of near-magical skill who keeps the covenant's five ships at sea.

secrets.title: A secret correspondence
secrets.text: He secretly corresponds with Marcus Navicularius of Oculus Septentrionalis.

characters.name: Henri de Tours

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Jerbiton, of the Apple Gild, and disceptator of Oculus Septentrionalis as its oldest remaining member. Corpulent, sociable and splendidly dressed, probably Lübeck's richest merchant and among the richest commoners in Germany, a respected administrator and diplomat who was apprenticed in Normandy and joined soon after the founding; he means his family to become a dynasty leading the covenant. A Mentem master who uses high-magnitude Mentem for subtlety, never force. His townhouse on the Holstenstrasse has shop and offices below, library and scriptorium above, then meeting rooms, dining hall and guest chambers, then the family's quarters, with three labs at the top for himself, Brunhilda and Gunhilda.

characters.name: Gunhilda Henrasdottir

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Jerbiton and of the Apple Gild, Henri's daughter and filia. Plump and over-sheltered, she specialises in housecraft and is married to Estrid Danesson.

characters.name: Estrid Danesson

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Ex Miscellanea and of the Apple Gild, a recent recruit and the second Scandinavian wizard the covenant has taken in. A man of Ribe who joined the Order late as a hedge wizard of sailing and weather, a flamboyant rogue whose sanctum and lab are aboard his ship; he gathers the covenant's vis around the Baltic and is married to Gunhilda. He is the younger cousin and bitter enemy of Eric Ribecus of Waddenzee; they have fought at sea, though no Wizard's War has been declared.

characters.name: Marcus Navicularius

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of House Verditius and of the Apple Gild, Lübeck's foremost shipwright: large and stern, with iron-grey hair and beard, owner of a shipyard that is also his workshop and lab, staffed by skilled craftsmen. A Terram master whose enchanting suits very large things such as ships and cannot work on anything smaller than a sword; he sells magical ships to covenants for vis and lost the Nebelkönigin to Waddenzee. He is designing the Baltic cog the Hanse will adopt.

secrets.title: A secret correspondence
secrets.text: He secretly corresponds with Aelfhere, Waddenzee's shipwright.

characters.name: Imanitos Mendax

description.biography: Equipment: fashionable fine clothes and costly jewellery; Encumbrance 0 (0). Twilight Scars: a forked tongue he keeps hidden, a voice people want to hear, and a faint smell of funeral incense. His Affinity with Finesse came from a Twilight, and his Compulsion is lying. He means to make his serpent-and-ruby ring his talisman. His longevity ritual gives only +2, but his apparent age rises only on an aging roll of 7 or more.

characters.summary: Master of House Jerbiton, lately so by the approval of three Fengheld magi, Apple Gild trained, Gauntleted at twenty-two after an apprenticeship at a powerful covenant of the Provençal Tribunal. Tall, lean and handsome, black-haired and blue-eyed, in fashionable blue or black, with a serpent-and-ruby ring he means for his talisman; a vanity longevity ritual keeps him looking thirty-nine. He poses as owner of the upmarket tavern Goldenes Kalb, above which a discreet brothel for rich clients is helped along by wine that heightens lust, and his third trade is the blackmail and extortion of citizens and magi. His focus is Mentem, with competent Imaginem for disguises; his Twilight has left him a hidden forked tongue, a compelling voice and a faint smell of funerary incense. His covenant-mates find him useful despite his morals; his sanctum on the top floors of his townhouse is secret and magically guarded.

secrets.title: Imanitos and the pirates
secrets.text: He sells Oculus Septentrionalis's ship movements to Eric Ribecus of Waddenzee for a share of the plunder.

secrets.title: Storyguide Notes
secrets.text: Optionally a diabolist of a hidden dark Jerbiton lineage, servant of the demon Radegast, corrupting Lübeck's notables through the Goldenes Kalb and posing as Radegast's prophet to the Mecklenburgs; he might swap the covenant's magestones for tainted copies.

characters.name: Carolus

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman of House Jerbiton and of the Apple Gild, well meaning and scatterbrained, who poses as an eccentric scholar tutoring the citizens. A naive visit to Crintera to mend relations went wrong when Caprea of Bjornaer, a guest there, blinded his raven familiar as a spy; the real spy was Kolkrabus, Murion's familiar.

characters.name: Boris of Novgorod

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Journeyman Redcap of House Mercere, not of the Apple Gild, a well-travelled, shrew-like Russian posing as an itinerant merchant who serves the northern Rhine and Novgorod. He owns the new Novgorod Inn at the north end of town, popular with Redcaps and Russian merchants, and hopes for Master rank within a couple of years so that it may become a Mercer House. He sells trinkets, trades books, items and vis, and gets Novgorod vis cheaply.

characters.name: Brunhilda
characters.summary: Henri's Swedish wife of more than thirty years, a seeress in the Norse manner who sends her spirit out in animal form while in trance. Not Gifted enough for the Order but treated as an equal by the magi; she runs the covenant's daily affairs more than Henri does, and her divination guides his luck in trade.

characters.name: Matilda
characters.summary: Gunhilda's elder, un-Gifted sister, autocrat of the covenant and Henri's housekeeper.

characters.name: Stentorius

description.biography: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Archmage of House Tremere, of the Oak Gild, authoritarian princeps of Fengheld and Tremere exarch of the Rhine, holding about three-fifths of the Tribunal's Tremere sigils, his filius's and the two Tremere of Triamore among them, while Severicus of Roznov holds the rest. Large and ageing well nearly a century past his Gauntlet, with a bushy iron-grey beard to his chest and a craggy nose; a famed master of Rego, able with most Forms, in showy deep-crimson robes covered in the symbols of Rego, the Forms and his House. His familiar of more than fifty years is Oswald, a hugely arrogant large grey cat in a jewelled gold pendant holding several uses of Aura of Rightful Authority among other effects, who believes he rules Fengheld if not the Tribunal. At Durenmar the cat is taunted by Murion's raven Kolkrabus; Oswald believes Murion has usurped his master's rightful place at the head of the Oak Gild, which she still leads.

characters.name: Horst
