description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Young, fair and sharp-tongued, a maga with the Gentle Gift whom Poena uses to speak for her to those the Gift unsettles. Trained as an Assessor, she wears strong illusions that make her seem older and male, the better to be believed, and the world grows sharper around her when she casts. She favours Muto and Imaginem, with some Creo and Mentem.

She tidies up trouble between magi and mundanes in the Tribunal, so she is the one who comes when characters have badly failed among mortals, and she checks on any who pass themselves off as nobles. She is Janus's chief aide.

characters.name: Dominic of Tytalus

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Archmagus and the aedile of Coeris, a hospes: the Tytalus who has set himself to read and forestall the schemes of every other Tytalus and warn the Tremere, a deadly serious game against his whole House. He believes his House badly underrates the Tremere, who once, in the Corruption, crushed it like an egg, and fears that their patience with Tytalus baiting may give way now that the Theban Tribunal's weakness leaves them magi to spare.

Very tall, black-clad down to his skullcap, with a devilish beard he knows looks overdone, which is the point; his sigil, a thunderclap, he privately finds funny. He favours weather magic and is a skilled necromancer. Close to the Prima but no Tremere, he always needs favours against some Tytalus plot and repays them with contacts, devious counsel and necromantic mayhem. Leontine of Tytalus of Old Histria is his protégé.

characters.name: Horatius

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Secretary for operations, seeing through what the last Decennial planned; under some Primi this post was mighty, but Poena's own grip on resources leaves him less, and he keeps things running and reports what goes wrong. Young for so high a post and plump for a Tremere, he worked beside Poena before her rise, helped arrange her succession, and is her husband's brother. A Signaler by training with his own sigil, comforting warmth; he favours Creo, Rego, Imaginem and Terram.

He seldom leaves Coeris, but magi abroad write to him with proposals, as the manager of House business; he is easier to reach than Poena and can arrange to see her. He does not seek the Primacy but would be a fine compromise if the House split, and would ring the north and east shores of the Black Sea with oppida to make it a Hermetic lake.

characters.name: Janus

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Secretary for contingencies: he keeps the House's stockpiles and asks for Tremere, or magi of the oppida, to be trained in odd skills in case one of his unlikely events comes to pass. Raised in the Rhineland, muscular and handsome, chaste and aloof with attractive women; his sigil is ribbons of scarlet light. He favours Creo, Intellego, Rego and above all Mentem, a well-known speciality that weakens him in certamen, and is a spiritual necromancer with a gift for spycraft and the Visions Flaw. He was secretary for operations under the previous Primus.

He watches characters whose doings might, however remotely, start a crisis, and quietly sets counterweights; years later he may call on skills he had them learn, to untangle a crisis born of several unlikely chances at once.

secrets.title: Janus's affliction
secrets.text: Janus suffers a lycanthropy that magic can hold back and that changes only his shape, not his mind. He is ashamed of it and keeps it secret, so he will never seek the Primacy.

secrets.title: Janus's coldness to women
secrets.text: Janus's lycanthropy passes by intercourse, hence his coldness to women.

characters.name: Isaac of Merinita

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 40 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary:
Coeris's expert on faeries, a cives, left deeply disturbed if not mad by the Tribunal's dark faeries; his mood swings from cheer to gloom without warning. He looks forty but has spent years in Faerie, so his true age is unknown. His skewed view and his hatred and vast knowledge of vampiric faeries make him Tatiana's adviser; she values his knack for surviving anything, if not always whole. He prefers gloomy faerie magic.

Frail-looking, yet his faerie blood makes him strong and nimble. Scars as if torn by madmen's teeth mark his wrists, ankles, neck and thighs, which Hermetic magic cannot heal, from a faerie curse or torture that harmed his Essential Nature. His sigil is the smell of burning pine cones, though he says it was not always so.

characters.name: Juturnus

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Horatius's troubleshooter, sent to find out why something in the House's operations went wrong and to put it right. Cocky, skilled and quick to violence, he is unlike a bureaucratic Tremere and may have risen too fast. Small objects near him arrange themselves into geometric shapes. He favours Rego, with some Perdo and Intellego, Animal and Terram.

He is black and athletic; decades ago a Primus had the Redcaps find Gifted Arab and African children, thinking they could work less conspicuously in Arab lands, and he was one of them. Like many he trained first as an Assessor, a kind of spy, and has since learnt more widely. The book gives no privilege for him.

characters.name: Tatiana

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Secretary for emergencies and Poena's spymistress: she warns the House of trouble ahead and finds answers when it is caught off guard. Of a Szekler family she has not seen since her apprenticeship; she turns briefly invisible whenever she casts, to her irritation. She favours Creo, Muto, Herbam and Corpus, and Isaac assists her.

She appears when something dreadful is close, takes over the characters' help and resources, and sends them into the worst of it to buy the House and Order time; magi who refuse her are tarnished for good in some circles.

secrets.title: Tatiana's society
secrets.text: Tatiana secretly belongs to the Keepers of the Silence of the Temple, a small, unofficial society named for the man who burnt the temple of Artemis at Ephesus to be famous and whose name was then forbidden. They hold that Tytalus magi too often do monstrous, foolish things for fame, and set out to destroy such vandals, then their memory.

characters.name: Monica Ierne

description.biography:
Stat block printed in Against the Dark, chapter two. Age 90, looking 55. Perception is left blank in the book and entered as 0. Soak +5 (Stamina and a bronze cord); Encumbrance 0. Combat: with a club, Init +1, Atk +5, Dfn +6, Dam +3; brawling, Init 0, Atk +1, Dfn +2, Dam 0. Hermes Lore 3 is entered as Organization Lore: Order of Hermes.

Leadworker lets her make small lead dolls or tablets that are arcane connections to the dead, or to animals that know their own names, and fix arcane connections without vis or lost study; she carries hundreds. The book lists no Flaw beyond Deficient Technique (Muto) and does not name her rank's Virtue.

Spells as the book lists them: Sudden Well appears there as ReTe 35 but is written up as PeTe 30, which the errata lower to PeTe 25, as the catalog holds; Diverting the River is a Ritual by the errata; Creeping Chasm is listed at 35; Gathering of the Stormy Might and Earth Shock are favourites to follow Sudden Well or Creeping Chasm. Necessary Monolith dams a river so that Diverting the River has water to turn; the chasm it cuts can also ring a camp in defensive circles nearly two miles across.

Equipment: a thigh case of flint spikes, slung with Wielding the Invisible Sling when nothing better is to hand, some dipped in arsenic and sealed with beeswax; the case is itself enchanted and keeps arsenic off its wearer. Several magic items from the House stores, the strongest a dragon banner whose pole was an archmagus's staff.

Talisman: a flint wand bound in bronze, with attunements for paralysis (+9), protection from faeries (+6), control, destruction and missiles at a distance, Ignem and Terram. Its effects, each 24 uses a day: The Earth Split Asunder (ReTe 35, holds concentration); Endurance of the Berserkers at Touch (ReCo 30); the Invisible Siege Engine, a Sling for things up to three feet across (ReTe 15), and a second copy with +20 Penetration; Object of Increased Size (MuTe 20); Obliteration of the Metallic Barrier (PeTe 25); Sense the Feet that Tread the Earth and Stone Tell of the Mind that Sits (InTe 40 each, holding concentration); and Wings of the Soaring Wind (Cr(Re)Au 40).

Familiar: Silexa, a wolf of Irish stock with the colour of flint, senior among the wolves bound to House Tremere (see the Bestiary). Through their bond Monica shares her sight, speaks mind to mind, and can call her from up to seven leagues; Silexa often fetches arcane connections to places for The Leap of Homecoming.

characters.summary:
Archmaga and legata, the House's field commander since Poena became Prima two years ago, and so her heir, who would act as Prima until an emergency council could meet. Raised at Blackthorn in England and marked from her first training as one of the House's heavy war-magi, she specialises in Creo, Rego, Terram and Corpus. Dark-haired and pale, with an athletic build rare in noblewomen; her sigil is flint. She holds her own sigil and Tatiana's. Her familiar is the wolf Silexa.

She comes into play whenever the House takes the field, though she often names another to command for her. She may ask characters to survey land as battlefields or staging grounds, and wants every detail of their fights with hedge magi, demons, faeries and stranger things. She does not want the Primacy and would take it only to keep out someone odious; if she did, she would have the Primus chosen by duel of champions and then step down for someone better at governing.

characters.name: Essedarius

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Leader of Kezdö Válasz since 1215 and the fourth in its history, filius of Macrobius, filius of Gasparus, filius of the founder Norsius; a cives (of Coeris). Tall, thickset and bald, with brown eyes, he looks thirty-eight and at ease, wears dark clothes for the saddle, and never goes without his talisman, an enchanted sword holding several powers to wound and to act at a distance. A Corpus specialist, he has not aged a day since his first longevity ritual.

Born in the Order, son of a warrior of Laniena, schooled at the Scholomance, he has known no life outside House Tremere; a steady rather than a brilliant pupil, he was picked as Macrobius's apprentice. When an angry griffin met by chance tore Macrobius apart in 1215, he took the lead.

Untested so far, he watches the growing quarrel between Bosnia and Hungary and dreads the slaughter a crusade would bring; he knows the Hungarian knights who cross the border to kill Patarians, tells his agents to keep clear of them, and will protect his Bosnian spies. To show his commitment he lives in the field, in a camp with six armed grogs, rather than in his fort; some say he should be in his lab instead. He has given Adulio a magic bridle that calms a horse so it will carry a magus.

characters.name: Leona

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Essedarius's partner, who took the place of her old partner Macrobius; a cives (of Coeris), looking fifty-six. Of middle height and stout, in riding clothes like most of her sodales, she is a master of Herbam who learns what she needs by questioning the trees and bushes wherever she goes; her sigil is a scent of lilac, stronger the greater the spell. People take her for slow and heavy, but she is quick to act and quicker to anger. She made many of the oppidum's signal charms.

She was not with Macrobius when the griffin killed him and still blames herself; killing that beast did not cool her rage, and she hunts griffins still, roaming the southern Dinaric Alps and the Prokletije, where he fell, and has built a fort there.

characters.name: Adulio

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A cives (of Coeris), looking thirty-six, who joined in 1204, two months after the Latins took Constantinople: the fall, at the end of his apprenticeship, convinced him Transylvania was in danger too, and he means to spare it what crusaders did to the Theban Tribunal. Thin as a reed and dark-haired, he looks ready for violence at any moment, and his familiar, a restless Eurasian lynx called Ucigas ('Killer' in Romanian), adds to the effect. He favours destructive Auram spells.

Sixteen years with no great threat have disappointed him; brushes with giants have not sated him. The loudest warmonger in the oppidum, he sees danger everywhere, and the Quaesitors have censured him twice, once for needlessly provoking local faeries and once for deliberately killing a band of Latin knights raiding out of Epirus; neither changed him. A horse breeder's son with an eye for good mounts, he rides with a magic bridle Essedarius made.

characters.name: Neculai

description.biography: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The oppidum's aedile and a socius (of Domostron), though the book also says every member is a cives; he looks thirty-nine. Born in the Carpathian foothills of Hungary, he was found by a wandering Bjornaer and raised and apprenticed in the Stonehenge Tribunal; once gauntleted he longed for home and asked several Transylvanian oppida to take him, and Kezdö Válasz, short of an aedile, took him at once, an offer he accepted without enthusiasm. Small, hawk-like and beak-nosed, with hair so black it looks blue, he is an Intellego specialist who can talk to nearly any bird, beast or fish. His heartbeast is a pern, the honey buzzard, and he travels on the wing.

He belongs to Clan Sirnas, the Bjornaer guardians, who distrust House Tremere and expect him to report on it. He resents that nearly as much as being paired with Adulio, and will not spy on anyone: he keeps the Gathering of Twelve Years' business to himself but tells his sodales he may speak there of what he has seen, and has attended twice since joining. Essedarius shrugs: the Tremere have nothing to hide and the Bjornaer nothing to fear. Essedarius has now sent him to visit Leona in the Prokletije, to keep her informed and to keep an eye on her.

characters.name: Thietmar

description.biography:
Stat block printed in Against the Dark (chapter nine), a storm wizard built as a Gifted hedge wizard. Age 37 (apparent 37). Soak +7 (Tough, Stamina and his hide clothes). Combat: dodge Init 0, Defense +2; fist (Init 0) Atk +3, Def +3, Dam +3; knife (Init 0) Atk +3, Def +2, Dam +5.

Equipment: warm furs and hides, a knife, and a satchel of magic ice worth 6 pawns of Auram vis.

His Personal Vis Source is an ice cave; his Feud is with a tribe of giants, taken on in the Heart of the Storm initiation that gave him Giant Blood. His Storm Calling is 5, +2 for Puissant. The book does not name his native language.

Hedge powers: Storm Calling raises a storm (Communication + Storm Calling + stress die against the storm's size and duration, paid in Auram vis) or moves any storm; Storm Riding sees from or travels to any point of a storm he can see; Storm Fighting attacks anyone within it with buffets, deluge, hail, erosion or lightning. Each season of ice harvesting yields (Int + Organization Lore + aura) / 3, rounded up, pawns of Auram vis. He risks the storm trance when he gains Warping (see the Storm Wizards faction).

reputations.name: Storm wizard of the high caves (Local)

characters.summary: A storm wizard: a tall, timid giant of a man hidden behind a wild beard, in stinking, badly cured furs and hides hung with ice. He lives in a cave above the snow and is known for it in the valleys below. He and the villagers at the mountain's foot fear and mistrust each other, and have worked out a round of paths and caches by which they leave him food and he turns storms away from their homes, so that neither ever has to meet the other.

characters.name: Tibor of Borša

description.biography:
Stat block printed in Against the Dark (chapter nine). Age 25 (apparent 25). Soak +9. Encumbrance -1 (3). Combat: short spear and buckler (Init +1) Atk +10, Def +6, Dam +7; fist (Init -1) Atk +6, Def +3, Dam +2.

Equipment: metal-reinforced leather armour, a short spear, a round shield, and several spare spears of black hawthorn.

Second Sight comes free with Dhampir, which also gives the +1 to his Faerie Lore (printed 4+1). His Faerie Antipathy is the Sympathy Trait Crossroads -1: at a crossroads every Ability roll he makes is at -1.

Hedge powers: the Hunters' Arts Slay 5 and Vampire 0 (the Foe Art free with his first Practice Art), in his Hunters chapter. With them he charges a new weapon in a day's chanting to kill one particular vampire (Dex + Slay + Vampire + aura + stress die against a level of 25, less 5 for each true fact he has learnt about it and more for each false one); a hit that penetrates leaves it Incapacitated.

characters.summary:
A dhampir vampire hunter, plain-looking in a peasant's smock and leather vambraces, his hauberk kept for trouble, a cloth tied over an empty eye socket and a spear carved from one piece of wood in his hand.

His father came home from a war unlooked for, and only later did his mother learn her husband had fallen in battle a month before. At eleven Tibor left the Transylvanian grain-lands to hunt that vampire down and has been a merciless hunter since. A few years ago he found it at last; it took his eye and left him for dead. The nearby village mourned him, and, not knowing the proper rites, thought nothing strange when his corpse came back to haunt them. Now one rumour says he is dead and another that he hunts vampires, and he must live with both.

secrets.title: What came back
secrets.text: The thing that came back was not Tibor: his father's vampire took his shape, and it still follows him.

laboratories.name: The Guest Laboratory in the Scriptorium

books.name: The Great Library of Durenmar
books.description: The Great Library fills the Tower of Bonisagus, which is enchanted against all decay of its books; a magus's familiarity with it is his Durenmar Lore. House Bonisagus swore to share it, so any magus may study here, but Durenmar adds that those who study must also give: each contribution the librarian accepts (a summa, a tractatus, a new spell, even a copy or a subtle variant, though low summae and common spells are refused as glutted) earns two free seasons of study, more for a weighty gift, and a season spent copying earns one season, which is how apprentices pay their way. Lab notes and Tribunal records may be consulted without contributing. Bonisagus magi and members study freely and indefinitely, and a Bonisagus who writes up his work here has met the Oath's duty to share. Rank decides a clash over a book, Bonisagus and members winning at equal rank, otherwise certamen; a few popular tomes have second copies. Nothing leaves the tower or is copied without the librarian's leave, though members may take Lab Texts to their labs; copies may be ordered by Redcap with vis for the scribing but come notoriously slowly, and the greatest summae are traded only with the most trusted, if ever. About a dozen magi study here in any season.

books.name: Mundane books of the scriptorium
books.description: First floor of the Tower of Bonisagus, where scribing, binding and copying are done with materials provided: an eclectic collection of mostly ancient mundane books from far places.

books.name: Lab notes of dead magi
books.description: First floor: endless lab notes of obscure, forgotten and unfinished research by magi long dead. Finding notes that bear on a project takes a season and a roll of Intelligence and Magic Theory; a named author's notes turn up within days unless they are restricted. Consulting them needs no contribution.

books.name: Records of the Rhine and Grand Tribunals
books.description: First floor: the complete records of every Rhine Tribunal and Grand Tribunal since the founding of the Order. A season extracts everything on a narrow subject, a covenant or a magus without a roll; a single entry takes a daily roll of Intelligence and Order of Hermes Lore, harder by one each day. Open to all without contribution.

books.name: House Bonisagus Folios
books.description: First floor: the Folios of House Bonisagus back to its first discourses.

books.name: Lab Texts of the standard spells
books.description: Second floor: copies of nearly every standard spell of the Order, many of which became standard by being written up here. Finding one is a stress roll against 3, or 6 for a particular version of a general spell up to level 40; a failure means someone of higher rank has it this season, a botch that it is not here, and an exact match a certamen with an equal.

books.name: Lab Texts of unique spells
books.description: Second floor: many unique spells. A non-standard spell is found on a roll against 6 to 21, depending on its rarity; a failure means it is not here, a botch that a flawed text exists.

books.name: Lab Texts of enchanted devices
books.description: Second floor: many enchanted devices. A similar enchantment is found on a roll against 6 to 21; beating that by six or more finds the exact effect.

books.name: Replenishing the Fount of the Magus
books.description: A Creo Corpus ritual of the thirtieth level held in the Great Library; nobody has ever cast it successfully.

books.name: Tractatus on Spell Mastery
books.description: Second floor: many tractatus on the mastery of spells. Each full six by which a spell is found beyond its ease factor turns up one Mastery tractatus, of Quality a simple die plus two.

books.name: Tractatus on the Arts
books.description: Third floor: dozens of tractatus on each Art, typically of Quality 3 to 9 and at most about 12 (a simple die plus two, with Durenmar Lore added at a cumulative penalty of one for each earlier use in that Art; capped at 12, never above 14).

books.name: Tractatus on Magic Theory and the Arcane Abilities
books.description: Third floor: several hundred tractatus on Abilities, chiefly Magic Theory, and on the other Arcane Abilities.

books.name: Principia Magica
books.author: Bonisagus
books.description: Bonisagus's own authority on Magic Theory; the third floor holds three copies. Level and Quality not given.

books.name: Summae on the Arts
books.description: Third floor: over a hundred summae, many in several volumes, with at least one outstanding high-level, high-Quality summa in every Art and a summa of at least level 17 in each of the fifteen; only a couple of dozen Art summae reach level 15 and levels above 20 are almost unheard of. Low summae run Quality 6 to 15 (at most about 24), high ones 6 to 9 (at most about 12). Availability is a simple die plus 10 against the level wanted (plus 3 for masters, Bonisagus and members, plus 6 for archmagi, never above 20); an exact match means certamen. Quality is a simple die plus 5 and Durenmar Lore at the usual penalty, capped at 30 minus the level or at 24, whichever is lower, and never above 28.

books.name: Summae on the Arcane Abilities
books.description: Third floor: summae on the Arcane Abilities. Availability is a simple die alone against the level wanted; an exact match means certamen. Quality as for the Art summae.

books.name: The librarian's restricted collection
books.description: Sixth and seventh floors, the librarian's sanctum, entered by invitation only: miscellaneous magical books and the lab notes on exotic theories and hedge traditions, heavily restricted under the present leadership and read only by House elders. The fourth and fifth floors between hold two cramped labs each, fitted so they work without penalty and always in demand.

books.name: Originals of the most precious tomes
books.description: The basement, behind a great enchanted iron trapdoor: the originals of the most precious tomes, of which only copies are read upstairs, with Durenmar's vis stores and countless items and relics including possessions of the Founders.

books.name: Triamore's library
books.description: A famous library, smaller than Durenmar's but a draw in its own right; no titles are given. Visiting magi are generally required to contribute a book.

books.name: Waddenzee's library
books.description: Poor: a few books following the interests of the present magi; no titles are given.

books.name: The Nebelkönigin's stolen books
books.description: The Hermetic books taken with the Nebelkönigin from Oculus Septentrionalis; their contents are not given. They may have been engineered into the pirates' hands and tainted.

books.name: Oculus Septentrionalis's library
books.description: Good-sized but below Fengheld's or Triamore's and far below Durenmar's, kept in Henri's townhouse on the Holstenstrasse. Mostly mundane books; its best Hermetic texts are in Rego, Mentem, Imaginem and Corpus. No titles or levels are given.

books.name: Fengheld's library
books.description: Vast, but dominated by lower-level books than a covenant of this size should hold, so that Fengheld-trained magi are generalists; the covenant makes up for it by hosting specialist guests. No titles or levels are given.

books.name: Horst's books
books.author: Horst
books.description: Horst of Mercere's famed, prolific, high-quality books on a great range of mundane subjects and on Magic Theory, the backbone of most Rhine apprenticeships and a mainstay of the library. No titles or levels are given.

books.name: Crintera's library
books.description: The book gives no titles or numbers. Crintera has a library in use: the guest maga Caprea is drawing on it to finish a bestiary for the Tribunal of 1221.

books.name: Appease the Queen of Winter
books.description: A laboratory text for the Muto Aquam ritual of the sixtieth level that thaws the Baltic each early spring by propitiating the Queen of Winter. Falke learned the ritual from it, with the help of the volkhvy of Arkona; cast at Arkona it gains a bonus of ten to the casting total, because the sun-god Svantovit opposes the Queen.

books.name: Irencillia's library
books.description: The book gives no titles or numbers. The library is one of the few communal spaces that every visitor sees much alike, and its faerie librarian summons books with a gesture.

books.name: The library of Laniena
books.description: No books are named. Its treasure is Murat of Terezin's store of initiation scripts for the Hunters' Arts, taken from a Gnostic scholar's record of a taltós clan, which Murat the Younger keeps to himself; the oppidum also keeps lore of vampires, ghosts and the walking dead from its founders.

books.name: The library of Evredika
books.description: No books are named. Each magus keeps what texts they have in their own distant sanctum; the Cult's lore is as much music and song as writing.

books.name: The Red Library
books.description:
It grew from the Red Book, first a list of the sigils of Diedne magi drawn up after the Schism War so that any who tried to rejoin the Order could be known by their magic; it later took in the sigils of every Renounced magus. The book itself troubles nobody. Benilda and those before her went further: the Library keeps copies of spells notorious for having been made to commit Hermetic crimes, kept as evidence of old crimes for young Quaesitors to learn from.

Among them are The Sleep of the Muses (Perdo Mentem; no other copy is known), an effect that makes magi forget for a while how to cast; The Curse of the Unportended Plague, which ruins cities; and The Trivialization of the Forgetful, which hides a spoken command in a magus's mind that makes him drop his Parma Magica. Kept with the Black Library in the Crypt of the Martyred Virgin.

books.name: The Black Library
books.description: One copy of each of the very few books the Order has made it a crime to own. It began after the corruption of House Tytalus, whose fallen Prima Tasgilla wove Infernal taint into spells and texts on magic theory that she spread through the Order. The Quaesitors and their allies burnt them after the House was cleansed, keeping a few so that new copies could be recognised; some magi think these seeds of corruption should be destroyed too. Kept with the Red Library in the Crypt of the Martyred Virgin.

books.name: The Transylvania Chronicle, 767-816 (Order of Hermes Lore)
books.description: The Transylvania Chronicle, kept at Tablinum: the Tribunal's record of events since the Order's founding in 767, richly illustrated, 90 volumes in 1220, two to a decade, three copies of each. It claims to be complete, but says little of the years before the Schism War or of House Tremere's founding; it is still the Tribunal's first source for Peripheral Code rulings and Hermetic history. It is an encyclopedia: every fifty years (ten volumes) counts as a quality 6 tractatus on Order of Hermes Lore (Transylvania) and one on Code of Hermes, nine sets in all. To look up a fact takes about an hour and a stress roll of Intelligence plus Code of Hermes or Order of Hermes Lore, +1 for each full fifty years one can consult that bear on the question (+9 for the whole). The scribes in the Scriptorium copy it.

books.name: The Spell Hall
books.description: Tablinum's archive of Lab Texts, hundreds of filed scroll cases: every spell of the core rules, most of the supplements' (as the troupe allows), and few original spells, nearly all in a form other magi can use without translation. Tremere copy freely; others pay by donating a usable Lab Text (one copy for each magnitude) or in vis, a pawn per magnitude copied. Texts may be copied but not taken away or worked from in the hall, which has no laboratory. With the exhibits, which are studied as realia, it makes up the oppidum's library.

books.name: The library of Old Histria
books.description: No books are named. The Mercere House keeps the records of the Redcap families and their messages, and the Histrians' own working books; the spell Incantation of Lightning was first written here.

books.name: The Register of Vis Sales
books.description: The Tribunal's record of every sale of vis and magic items by its magi, kept at Old Histria, with the notarised matching letters of sales made elsewhere and the master of vis trading's list of promissory notes on offer.

books.name: The library of Shrouded Bay
books.description: No books are named; the villa holds the working books of the magi who winter there and of Accursius's laboratory.

books.name: The books of Lycaneon
books.description: The book names no library at Lycaneon; the oppidum's strength is its laboratories. Its leader keeps one of the twelve secret copies of the Book of Legacies (see Coeris), the white register of every item the House controls.

books.name: The library of the Scholomance
books.description: No books are named. Two collections: on the second floor a broad library of mundane and esoteric learning, the best anywhere on magic outside the Order's, swelled by the copies and treatises each pupil must make, with nothing on the Hermetic Arts or the Order; on the guarded third floor the oppidum's Hermetic texts, among them Simium's many primers. The House hopes the hedge-magic books may one day help Hermetic magic grow.

books.name: The Book of Legacies
books.description:
A huge white tome listing every item, magical or mundane, that House Tremere controls, the Blessings of the Dead among them. Only twelve copies exist and many are kept at Coeris; the others are held by the exarchs abroad, the Prima, her chosen successor and the leader of Lycaneon. Its very existence is a secret, and Poena knows every line of it.

Each copy is guarded by layered defences: its case destroys the pages if the right passwords are not spoken, if it is laid on certain surfaces, or if Mentem magic cannot confirm that the one touching it is a loyal Tremere, which means lowering one's Parma to the other Mentem spells woven into it.

books.name: The Book of Placements
books.description: The companion to the Book of Legacies: where each item is, recorded only by its number in the Book of Legacies and a number for each magus, covenant and oppidum, so a stolen copy tells a thief nothing. Some nosy Mercere have intercepted parts of it, grasped what it is, and guessed that a key like the Book of Legacies must exist. Keeping it is why no two Tremere in the Tribunal may share a name.

books.name: The Book of Places to Avoid
books.description: The Earnest Sons of the Grid and Chain's record, compiled over centuries, of every place that resisted their survey teams and what stopped them: perhaps the longest list of places best left alone in Mythic Europe. Magi hoping to make a name as slayers of beasts or tamers of faeries write asking for a fitting challenge, and the vexillation searches it for one, an unsanctioned rite of passage for some young magi. The book does not say where it is kept; it is entered at Coeris.

books.name: The war plans
books.description: House Tremere's official plans for invading covenants, kept at Coeris and named by colour (Red, Blue, White, Black and their shades), revised whenever a young magus's exercise plan shows a better idea. See Coeris's notes.

books.name: The casting tablets of Kezdö Válasz
books.description: No books are named. The oppidum keeps many casting tablets at Sarmizegethusa: several of the ritual that raises a fort, others that make an ordinary laboratory, and others that bring a fort down to rubble (Destroy the Fort), with Norsius's old spells for calming horses under a Gifted rider.

books.name: Arms of the Salamander
books.description: Restores the most recently lost limb; 6 pawns of vis. (Against the Dark pp. 98-99)

books.name: The Rite of Healing
books.description: Heals all Wounds of a group; a rook of vis. (Against the Dark pp. 98-99)

books.name: Universal Poultice
books.description: Cures a group of every disease; a rook of vis. (Against the Dark pp. 98-99)

creatures.name: The Courts of the Seasons
creatures.appearance: Four faerie rulers, each bound to a fragment of one broken forest spirit: the shy, red-hued Alder Prince in a misty western vale, generous but touchy King Oak beneath a great oak in the south, the scheming Willow Maiden in the east, and iron-willed King Holly in his northern holly grove.
creatures.notes:
Faerie Might 15-35 by the time of year: the book prints 20-50, which its errata reduce (20 to 15, 30 to 20, 35 to 25, 40 to 30, 50 to 35). Each ruler keeps a Might score of 30 for Magic Resistance and Penetration all year, but the Might Pool swings: 35 (and an aura of 3 across the wood) in the month of its own solstice or equinox, losing about 5 a month to the next court down to 15 at the opposite season, then gaining it back.
Special Powers: Alder Prince: Shroud, Grant Virtue (Rapid Convalescence). King Oak: Guide, Grant Virtue (Inspirational). Willow Maiden: Guide, Grant Flaw (Weak-Willed). King Holly: Shroud, Grant Flaw (Depressed). All four: Control Weather, Regio. Each ruler should also have faerie powers of the storyguide's choosing.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 34

creatures.name: The King Fir of the Black Forest
creatures.appearance: A great dark fir alone on the bare summit of the Feldberg; the spirit, the King of the Black Mountain, is said to show itself as a huge man in a black cloak with a dreadful face.
creatures.notes:
Faerie Might 60: the book prints 90, which its errata corrects.
Special Powers: Control Weather, Grant Flaw (many, among them Depressed, Fear, Lame and No Sense of Direction), Grant Victory (very seldom used), Grant Virtue (unknown, very seldom used), Possession, Regio, Shroud.
The splintered, faerie-twisted wild half of the Black Forest's first genius loci. Its regio under the Feldberg has several levels of Faerie aura 3 to 8 and a vast dungeon of enslaved trespassers; no mortal who sees the fir may leave the forest. It cannot reach the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls or the Fane of the Founders, and wants Durenmar destroyed so that the oath binding its other half lapses.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 50

creatures.name: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls
creatures.appearance: A stream falling over seven waterfalls down a steep valley of hazel and beech at the heart of the Black Forest; the spirit of the glade is peaceful and is spoken of as she.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 50: the book prints 80, which its errata reduce.
Special Powers: Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker), Guide, Oath-Swearing, Regio, Shroud.
What remains of the Black Forest's original genius locus, bound long ago by the Cult of Mercury's oath. Each waterfall is a level of its regio, and the spirit lets a visitor climb past one only after a Quest (and perhaps a Sacrifice), each granting deeper understanding of the Forest. The glade has never been found; some magi think its spirit has been replaced by a maga in Final Twilight, perhaps Merinita herself.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 51

creatures.name: The Ash of Nortorf
creatures.appearance: A small ash seedling in the churchyard of Nortorf in Holstein.
creatures.notes:
Infernal Might 10, with the potential to reach 40 once the ash is grown: the book prints 15 and 60, which its errata reduce to a range of 10-40.
Special Powers: Grant Victory, Grant Virtue (Entrancement), Grant Virtue (Inspirational), Grant Virtue (Tough).
Every New Year's Night a white horseman cuts the shoot down while a black horseman tries to stop him; if the black rider ever wins, the tree will grow, a king will tether his horse under it, and he will be unbeatable in a terrible battle while the horse stays there. Grown, it would be a rich source of vis.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 69

creatures.name: The Teutoburger Forest
creatures.appearance: A ring of ancient trees of different kinds round a great clearing at the forest's heart, which guard the wood together.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 40: the book prints 50, which its errata reduce.
Special Powers: Grant Flaw (Simple-Minded), Grant Victory, Regio, Shroud, Stasis.
In the top level of its regio the Roman legionaries who fled into the forest after Hermann's victory still hold a fortified camp in the clearing: the guardians let them neither die nor leave, though they may hunt beyond the clearing and have come to revere the trees.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 77

creatures.name: The Apple of the Kyffhäuser
creatures.appearance: A withered apple tree at the foot of the Kyffhäuser's tallest peak, guarded by men-at-arms.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 45: the book prints 70, which its errata reduce.
Special Powers: Grant Victory (to whoever hangs a shield on the tree), Grant Virtue (Unaging, to keep its men-at-arms in their prime), Heal Wounds, Possession (of any who fail to beat the men-at-arms).
Whoever hangs his shield on it becomes lord of the West; those who try and fail serve forever among its guards. Clovis, Charlemagne and Barbarossa succeeded and cut it down, and each time it grew back and withered with their fortunes. It last bore fruit under Barbarossa.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 86

creatures.name: The Donar Oak
creatures.appearance: The stump of the great oak of Geismar, a plain cross set in its centre, with offshoots growing round it in a hidden glade.
creatures.notes:
Special Powers: Grant Virtue (various, rarely used), Healing.
Once the heart of the Hercynian Forest's pagan power, until St Boniface felled it into four pieces. Wild beasts grow docile in the glade; its acorns are Creo vis, tame any animal that eats one, and tame a forest where one grows to maturity. Some think the glade a gate to Eden.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 88

creatures.name: The Linden of Neustadt
creatures.appearance: A great spreading lime tree whose broken boughs are held up by stone columns carved with the arms of the nobles who once defended the town.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 25: the book prints 30, which its errata reduce.
Special Powers: Grant Victory, Grant Virtue (Berserk), Grant Virtue (Tough), given to the town's defenders.
Alone among the forest spirits it has taken a town's people into its realm, which weakens it but keeps them sparing of the woods. It is said the town's freedom ends when the tree dies.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 88

creatures.name: The Drudenbaum of Harberg
creatures.appearance: A tree of no known kind atop the Harberg above Nuremberg, a great black bird perched in its crown.
creatures.notes:
Special Powers: Grant Virtue (Magic Sensitivity), Grant Virtue (Second Sight), Possession.
The spirit possesses any tree of its domain, which then takes on the Drudenbaum's look and gifts, the black bird settling in its top. Its golden drops are Creo vis and the milk from its roots Vim vis, which is why wizards gather beneath it; the guarding dragon and treasure of the tale are only legend.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 89

creatures.name: The Holm Oak of Romowe
creatures.appearance: A massive evergreen oak in the sacred grove of Romowe, hung with ribbons and talismans, a fire kept burning under its boughs.
creatures.notes:
Magic Might 35, currently 20 while it is trapped: the book prints 45 and 30, which its errata reduce.
Special Powers: Grant Flaw (Depression, on anyone who breaks a branch or kills a beast in the grove), Possession (of anyone who takes a branch).
St Adalbert of Prague drove the tyrant spirit back into the oak and lit the fire that holds it; a band of foresters keeps the fire fed, for if it goes out the spirit is free.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 99

creatures.name: Holzfrau
creatures.how_many: many, in the forests of Germany

powers.name: Control Plants
powers.description: Any Creo or Rego Herbam effect up to 20th level, for 1 Might per magnitude; the cost doubles in winter.

powers.name: Fertility
powers.description: As The Bountiful Feast: fruitful, protected crops. She can take the blessing back if her kindness is abused.

powers.name: Healing
powers.description: Her kiss eases pain, cleans infection from a wound or speeds healing: it cures a Light Wound from disease or gives +9 to recovery rolls.

creatures.appearance: Always a woman, often young and lovely, barefoot in peasant dress, with some telling detail of clothing that marks which kind of wood-wife she is.
creatures.notes:
A wood-wife, a usually kindly faerie of growing things; many serve the Alder Prince of the Courts of the Seasons.
Faerie nature: untouched by disease and age, understands and is understood in any tongue, has Second Sight, and its powers take the aura's bonus or penalty by the Realm Interaction table.
Vulnerable to iron: cold-forged iron pains her and she shuns its touch, though it does her no harm.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 36

creatures.name: Bockman

powers.name: The Patient Stance
powers.description: Init n/a. Standing still in a forest it cannot be told from the undergrowth, in effect invisible.

powers.name: Unease of the Still Forest
powers.description: Init n/a; costs 2 points per hour. A hush and creeping dread for 100 paces round it: each hour gives a cumulative -1 to brave or bold Personality Traits and a like boost to ones such as Short-Tempered or Suspicious, and no one in it can sleep or recover Fatigue.

powers.name: Fear
powers.description: Victims who fail a stress roll against 6 (adjusted by Brave) flee until exhausted, or cower until sunrise if they cannot run. Up to ten who can see it, or one target if it is unseen.

creatures.appearance: Man-shaped only in chest and arms, with a goat's head and legs, sharp swept-back horns, wild eyes and a drooling mouth of sharp teeth.
creatures.notes:
Lurks by the Black Forest's paths (and in many old German forests) to frighten travellers away: it spooks them and their mounts with its unease, then springs out with Fear. Weak and cowardly in a real fight. Its claws include the Ways of the Forest bonus.
Faerie nature: untouched by disease and age, understands and is understood in any tongue, has Second Sight, and its powers take the aura's bonus or penalty by the Realm Interaction table.
Vulnerable to iron: iron weapons do it 2 extra damage.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-4), -3 (5-8), -5 (9-12), Incapacitated (13-16).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 50

creatures.name: Loreley

powers.name: Infatuation
powers.description: Her song makes up to ten hearers a round long to reach her at any cost, into the river or onto the rocks. Resisted by an Intelligence stress roll against 9; women and those with waxed ears get +3, and a dripstone lets its wearer ignore it on a Perception roll against 6.

powers.name: Control Person
powers.description: On a man who meets her eyes, one at a time: unless he makes an Intelligence stress roll against 12 he does whatever she says, even leaping to his death.

powers.name: Control Water
powers.description: Any Creo or Rego Aquam effect up to 30th level, for 1 Might per magnitude.

powers.name: Form of Water
powers.description: She becomes water and slips into the Rhine, regaining 5 Might an hour (four times her usual rate) and healing Light, Medium and Heavy wounds in minutes, hours and days; she is all but unkillable.

creatures.appearance: A maiden of great beauty, clad only in long golden hair that she combs without end with a jewelled comb.
creatures.notes:
Faerie nature: untouched by disease and age, understands and is understood in any tongue, has Second Sight, and its powers take the aura's bonus or penalty by the Realm Interaction table.
Vulnerable to iron: the least touch of cold iron gives her a Light Wound, and an iron weapon that gets past her Soak raises its wound by one level.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 127

creatures.name: Sordus, a Basilisk

powers.name: Gaze of Death
powers.description: Anyone his gaze falls on, if he wills it, takes an Incapacitating wound.

powers.name: Horrid Wilting
powers.description: Init n/a; always on. Plants within 5 paces die, food rots and grows worms, and wood starts to decay within a day.

powers.name: Pollute Water
powers.description: Init n/a; always on. Standing water within 5 paces stagnates, other liquids putrefy, and running water turns black until he moves on.

creatures.appearance: A huge lizard about knee-high and six feet from snout to tail, with tiny diamond scales of grey, dark green and black and a crown-like fleshy crest; every movement slow and deliberate.
creatures.notes:
Familiar of Archmage Philippus Niger of Durenmar, who keeps him mostly out of sight but lets him prowl a room to underline a threat. Presence and Communication n/a. Too lazy to fight.
Bond (PeVi Lab Total 81): Bronze +2, Silver +2, Gold +4. Familiar power: Mental Communication (level 15), constant mental contact with Philippus, which either can shut off.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-3), -3 (4-6), -5 (7-9), Incapacitated (10-12).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 61

creatures.name: Boglin
creatures.how_many: a few, each in its own foul pool

powers.name: Abominable Stench
powers.description: A cloud of choking swamp gas from beneath the waterline spreads 15 yards over 3 rounds and takes 3 more to clear. Anyone in it fails a Stamina roll against 9 and can do nothing but reel back; a botch leaves them retching on the ground.

powers.name: Paralysis
powers.description: Init n/a; Corpus or Animal. A tentacle hit that wounds injects venom: unless the victim makes a Stamina roll against 9, his muscles cramp for -5 to physical actions for about an hour. Once per tentacle per fight.

powers.name: Writhing Grasp
powers.description: Init n/a; Corpus or Animal. A tentacle hit worth a Medium Wound or worse does only a Light Wound but wraps the victim. Each round he may try an opposed Strength roll to break free or an opposed Dexterity roll to free his hands; held, he is hauled to the maw in 3 rounds, and only then can it Bite.

powers.name: Regeneration
powers.description: Init n/a. It hibernates and regrows one lost tentacle a season.

vis.where: in its brain, a black and stinking nodule

creatures.appearance: Eight slimy dark-brown tentacles twelve feet long round a huge, lumpy, shell-covered body that seldom leaves the murky water, with a wide toothed mouth somewhere within.
creatures.notes:
A foul primeval spirit of the north German swamps; a stink and faint murmuring betray its pool. The book gives Size +3 for the body, 0 for each tentacle. Its Greater Immunity makes it immune to damage from bludgeoning weapons; its attacks include the Ways of the Swamp bonus.
Each tentacle fights as a separate creature with its own wounds; an Incapacitating blow may sever it, which costs the body a Light Wound. Wound penalties: body -1 (1-8), -3 (9-16), -5 (17-24), Incapacitated (25-32); each tentacle -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 79

creatures.name: The Mice of the Mäuseturm
creatures.how_many: about ten swarms, endlessly renewed by the aura

powers.name: Swarm
powers.description: A swarm of about a thousand mice engages about three people and bites bare flesh with no attack roll. Damage a round by protection (armour does not add to Soak): none, stress die +6; sturdy clothes, +3; winter garb or partial armour, +0; half armour, -3; full armour, -6; full armour with helm and gauntlets, -9.

creatures.notes: Size -10 each; a swarm counts as one Size 0 creature. A victim kills 10 mice for every 5 points of his Brawl Attack Total each round, and the swarm flees once over half are dead. Area spells (Group, Room) can strike a whole swarm but will catch its victims too; an Animal spell at Voice, Concentration, Group affects one swarm, and one magnitude higher clears the island for a while. Their teeth burn and they are immune to fire. The island's Infernal aura breeds them anew until it is cleansed.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 122

creatures.name: Bishop Hatto

powers.name: Lurk in Shadows
powers.description: Hidden wholly in a shadow; even moving in, the dark patch is seen only on Perception + Awareness against 12 (9 by day). His attacks can be dodged only once he is seen.

powers.name: Fear
powers.description: Up to ten people a use are filled with terror of the island; repeated, it can drive the trapped mad or kill them of fright, the fate of any who stay the night.

powers.name: Chill Touch
powers.description: Init +3, with his attack. An icy touch that takes a Fatigue level from the target and gives the bishop 5 Might.

vis.where: in his crosier, found only once he is destroyed

creatures.appearance: A ragged shard of darkness, roughly man-shaped; close up, the bishop's demon-twisted face and mitre show in it.
creatures.notes: The damned ghost of the bishop who haunts the Mäuseturm. His touch can be defended against only with Brawl: weapon defences fail as the blade passes through him. Its damage is his Chill Touch.
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 122

creatures.name: Marcus the Valiant
creatures.equipment: Round shield, manica on the right arm, greave on the left leg, gladius, ornate brimmed bronze helmet.
creatures.appearance: The stocky leader of the three, armed as a hoplomachus.
creatures.notes:
One of three ghostly gladiators who form in the amphitheatre of Trier when the Trumpet of Ghostly Summoning is blown there at night. Each challenges all comers to a duel to the death, staking a trinket (worth 2 pawns of Mentem vis) against something of like value; the fight feels real but is truly non-lethal, a killing blow leaving the loser unconscious. A gladiator fades whether he wins or loses and cannot be called again that year.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 134

creatures.name: Cyrillus of Argentoratum
creatures.equipment: Trident, net, galerus (metal shoulder guard), manica of quilted linen on the left arm, copper mask of Poseidon.
creatures.appearance: A wiry, dark-haired retiarius.
creatures.notes:
One of three ghostly gladiators who form in the amphitheatre of Trier when the Trumpet of Ghostly Summoning is blown there at night. Each challenges all comers to a duel to the death, staking a trinket (worth 2 pawns of Mentem vis) against something of like value; the fight feels real but is truly non-lethal, a killing blow leaving the loser unconscious. A gladiator fades whether he wins or loses and cannot be called again that year.
His net attack is resolved as a scuffle, to pin a foe or entangle a weapon.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 134

creatures.name: Caudelix the Gaul
creatures.equipment: Long-hafted axe, hatchet, iron skull cap with a spectacle mask, leather bracae on the thighs, bracers.
creatures.appearance: A huge, burly man with fair braided hair.
creatures.notes:
One of three ghostly gladiators who form in the amphitheatre of Trier when the Trumpet of Ghostly Summoning is blown there at night. Each challenges all comers to a duel to the death, staking a trinket (worth 2 pawns of Mentem vis) against something of like value; the fight feels real but is truly non-lethal, a killing blow leaving the loser unconscious. A gladiator fades whether he wins or loses and cannot be called again that year.
Wound penalties: -1 (1-6), -3 (7-12), -5 (13-18), Incapacitated (19-24).
creatures.source: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p. 134

creatures.name: Upokorituma

powers.name: Claws as Sharp as Satan's
powers.description: Hardens his claws for a day, adding +4 to their Damage.

powers.name: February's Frosty Bite
powers.description: A cold so fierce it burns, striking a target he can see for +10 damage.

powers.name: Flight of the Raven
powers.description: Always on: gives him wings strong enough to fly.

vis.where: one in each of his four biggest fangs

creatures.appearance: Squat and heavy as a thick-legged horse, dark grey with pink eyes and gums the red of blood, with eight heads on eight thick necks and wings that look far too small for him, though he flies well.
creatures.notes:
An aždaja, an Infernal dragon: a corrupted beast rather than a demon, and, unlike most Infernal beasts, intelligent. The book builds him from Infernal Virtues and Flaws laid over beast Qualities (Realms of Power: The Infernal). His Fear is of doves. He hides in the ravines along the upper Danube and lies under the water waiting for merchant boats; once one has passed above him he rears up behind it, kills everyone aboard, sinks the hull and hauls the cargo home. Wound ranges: Light 1-7, Medium to 14, Heavy to 21, Incapacitated to 28, Dead from 29.
The aždaje rank themselves by raw strength, the stronger taking the best lairs and hunting grounds and punishing the weaker; their lairs are bleak, rotting places, mostly in Infernal auras, and some pass themselves off as Magic dragons to keep the magi away.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 105

creatures.name: Danaslepih

powers.name: The Beast with Five Heads
powers.description: Always on: five more heads, six in all, each able to talk and bite. Lost or hurt heads do not grow back. Bought as three Personal Powers and Improved Powers.

powers.name: Assuming the Horse-chestnut
powers.description: Becomes a horse-chestnut tree, upright if he rears onto his hind legs first, or a fallen trunk if he lies down.

powers.name: The Field Made Fallow
powers.description: A touch of his claw withers a field: as many as ten thousand plants at once.

powers.name: The Captive Encased in Bark
powers.description: His breath, from nostrils almost touching the victim, turns a person into a smaller horse-chestnut.

powers.name: Inquiry of the Leafy Sentinel
powers.description: Lets him talk with trees and bushes.

vis.where: in the five largest scales along his back

creatures.appearance: Long, lean and low: forty feet from snout to tail but only six feet at the shoulder, his green scales looking mouldy though that is just their colour. His six heads weave and flick like tasting tongues, and fall still only when he stalks.
creatures.notes:
A young zmaj, a Magic dragon, blind from birth, who finds his way by smell and hearing and knows the scent of every plant in the Tribunal. His lair is in a dense stand of horse-chestnuts by the Drina in western Serbia. He hunts deer along his borders and drives off farmers: grain sown too near his home is destroyed, and a farmer he meets loses his crop and becomes a tree. Rude but not violent, and, like most zmajevi, in search of a wife. He may bite many times a round, but a Size 0 foe only twice, plus once more for each point of Size above 0. Wound ranges: Light 1-9, Medium to 18, Heavy to 27, Incapacitated to 36, Dead from 37.
The zmajevi want what the aždaje want, wives and gold, but do harm without noticing or caring. Some walk on their hind legs with small clawed hands. Their lairs are lavish, and their pecking order is one of remembered favours and insults, much like a noble court.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 107

creatures.name: Georghe and Ladislau
creatures.how_many: two giant brothers, who share these statistics

powers.name: Shrinking
powers.description: In a moment he shrinks to Size +2 or grows back to +4, his arms and armour with him. The book prints no Init.

vis.where: one in each ear and one in the nose

creatures.equipment: Full chainmail, heater shield, long sword.
creatures.appearance: Two plain local knights grown to giant size, their armour undecorated but kept in good order.
creatures.notes:
Brothers with farms side by side, next to their mother's, each forever edging the shared fence onto the other's land; when one notices, they fight, and being equally strong they can go at it for hours. Their quarrels spill onto the road that runs past the farms, and after a few blows one of them will ask a passing traveller to judge between them, or to take up arms against the other. Their scores are Pretenses, as for any faerie. Wound ranges at Size +2: Light 1-7 to Dead from 29; at Size +4: Light 1-9 to Dead from 37.
Transylvanian giants (also called ogres) are no fools: they bear arms like knights, keep homesteads and horses, and can be witty. Many change Size between +2 and +5, shrinking to ride and growing just before a fight, and many can take other shapes (a pear tree, a brook, a poisonous flower), in which they can still be hurt. Each has a sorceress mother, and giant blood shows as hair growing inside the mouth.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 112

creatures.name: Costache

powers.name: Rousing the Castle's Curiosity
powers.description: Everyone in the building is gripped by curiosity and goes poking into every passage, room and locked door.

powers.name: Flee like a Bird
powers.description: As Wings of the Soaring Wind: once let out, he flies off through a window.

powers.name: The Shock of Consequence
powers.description: Freezes up to ten people where they stand; he uses it on his rescuers the moment he is free, scolds them and makes off with something valuable.

creatures.appearance: A big captive prince or lord in ragged robes, unkempt and filthy, his eyes glittering with spite; moments after his release his clothes are new again and he is clean and well groomed.
creatures.notes: The giant locked in the forbidden room of a king's palace, held in a barrel lined with spikes and bound with three iron chains. He is easily caught and hard to keep, for his power makes the household curious, and he feeds on the thrill and dread of people prying where they have been told not to. Scores are Pretenses. Wound ranges: Light 1-8, Medium to 16, Heavy to 24, Incapacitated to 32, Dead from 33.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 113

creatures.name: Nicoleta, a Giant's Mother

powers.name: Assume the Shape of the Spinning Wheel
powers.description: Turns her into a great stony cartwheel that runs her foes down, adding +5 to her Brawl damage.

powers.name: A Mother's Fury
powers.description: Wraps her in flames that do +20 damage to whoever she touches, if they penetrate.

creatures.appearance: Tall, lean and dirty, with wiry hair, warts and boils, and a great boar's tusk jutting from each side of her mouth; she wears a grimy patterned dress under a stained apron.
creatures.notes:
A shadowy figure deep in the woods whom the locals know of and keep away from. She spurs her son to do his neighbours every harm he can, and people put up with him because killing him would bring her fury down on them. She breeds horses on a farm hidden in a valley of the Madara Plateau (the book's reference to chapter 3 means Bulgaria's chapter 4), and among them is a faerie horse she keeps dirty and half-starved so no one sees what it is. Stories have someone trying to win that horse from her with impossible chores. Roused, she becomes the burning wheel and tries to crush her enemies. Scores are Pretenses. Wound ranges: Light 1-6, Medium to 12, Heavy to 18, Incapacitated to 24, Dead from 25.
A giant's mother is always a sorceress, cleverer than her son: she picks the home, runs the household and the herd, steers his choices and hunts down whoever beats him; without a son she pines or rages until she adopts another. No two are alike: others breathe fire, shake the earth, turn into poison clouds or throw mountains, and not all are giant-sized.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 112

creatures.name: Fet-Frumos, a Faerie Horse

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: Always on: he can fly (Realms of Power: Faerie).

creatures.appearance: Held captive, a worn-out, filthy old nag, sway-backed and bow-legged; once freed and serving his hero, a young, healthy horse whose coat gleams. Smaller than a warhorse, he still carries an armoured knight with ease.
creatures.notes: A faerie horse's tale: languish dirty and hungry on a giant's mother's ranch (or as a giant's mount) until a hero finds him, then carry and counsel the hero, and leave just before the final victory so the hero wins it alone. More aware of his part than most faeries, he can foresee how other faeries will play theirs (that a thwarted giant's mother will storm the maiden's castle, say), which mortals take for prophecy; he knows nothing of what other realms will do. Scores are Pretenses. Wound ranges: Light 1-7, Medium to 14, Heavy to 21, Incapacitated to 28, Dead from 29.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 113

creatures.name: Human-like Vampire
creatures.how_many: a template: the commonest vampire of the Tribunal

powers.name: Sap the Life
powers.description: A touch that saps the victim's vitality: a disease beginning with a Light Wound and two Fatigue levels lost until it passes. Each week a Recovery roll of 12 holds steady and 18 improves; Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.

creatures.appearance: A fresh corpse, often with red eyes and red nails, in a burial shroud or nothing at all.
creatures.notes:
Called platenik or ubour by Bulgarians, drakus by the Thracians of the Rhodopes, moroi by the Vlachs, oiocoi by the Transylvanians, lampir in Bosnia and upir among the Ruthenians. The kukudhi are the old ones that have lost their fear of daylight (though direct sun still hurts them) and live among people. 5 points of Virtues and 3 of Flaws; a template to tailor. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
A Transylvanian vampire is a faerie, not the dead man's spirit: it takes the shape of someone recently dead and feeds on blood and on the fear it stirs. Each is unique, with its own one to three precautions that stop it forming, one to three limits it must obey and one rite that ends it for good (lists in chapter 8 and in the vampire hunters of chapter 9); killed any other way it forms again after days or weeks, and while the community's wound is unhealed another faerie takes its place. Every vampire has Feast of the Dead, a Traditional Ward of sunlight and the Lesser Power Sap the Life (PeCo 15: a disease starting at a Light Wound that also takes two Fatigue levels).
The life cycle: an unseen haunting of the family (zduhacz) for seven or forty days, then a shapeless gadja for forty days, then the dead one's own shape (platenik), preying first on its kin; after seven years it moves far away as a kukudhi, takes a trade and a family, and its children are dhampirs. Vampires are busiest from St Andrew's Eve to St George's Eve.
creatures.source: Against the Dark: The Transylvanian Tribunal p. 118

powers.name: Transform into Animal

creatures.notes:
Vukodlaci to the Slavs (a word also used of living werewolves), farkaskoldus to the Hungarians, blautsauger to the Saxons and pricolici to the Vlachs; a few look like bears or dragons instead. For all their strength they have no bones. Dying by a wolf, eating from a wolf's kill or a violent crime such as murder draws them, and every varcolac becomes one when he dies. 8 points of Virtues and 5 of Flaws; the single Lesser Power covers both its lesser powers. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

creatures.how_many: a template: the ghostly zduhacz, luderc and their kin

powers.name: Eidolon

powers.description: A touch that saps the victim's vitality: a disease beginning with a Light Wound and two Fatigue levels lost until it passes. Each week a Recovery roll of 12 holds steady and 18 improves; Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.

powers.name: Ghost Touch
powers.description: Its Focus Power: moves loose objects, 5 pounds for 1 point and double for each point more; thrown, an object does +5 damage a point, and every physical attack must penetrate. The cost varies with the weight.

vis.where: in the object its Ghost Touch is moving

creatures.appearance: Unseen, or a glowing speck of light, or the dead one's face and form made by its Eidolon.
creatures.notes:
Haunts the dead one's family, smashing pots and making a nuisance of itself, visits people in dreams and may father children on a widow; it shows as points of light or burning shafts. Being bodiless it need not really dodge. The Hungarians call it luderc; the nekrstenik or ustrel comes for an unbaptised child's death and threatens newborns and young mothers, the sjanka rises from the blood of a man knifed to death, and the ljugat is a gentler kind that feeds only briefly. 7 points of Virtues and Flaws. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

creatures.name: Gadja
creatures.how_many: a template: the formless stage of a young vampire

powers.name: Calm the Sheep of the Field
powers.description: Keeps a beast from running away as it rolls up to feed.

powers.name: Sap the Life
powers.description: A touch that saps the victim's vitality: a disease beginning with a Light Wound and two Fatigue levels lost until it passes. Each week a Recovery roll of 12 holds steady and 18 improves; Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.

vis.where: in the jelly of blood inside it

creatures.appearance: A limp bag of skin about a pace across, with little beady eyes and a sharp snout.
creatures.notes:
The second stage of a human-shaped vampire's life: a swollen sack of hide and hair full of blood like jelly, rolling from place to place, sometimes likened to an ox's head, that sucks blood mostly from animals through its snout. Thorns and piercing weapons do it fearful harm. 4 points of Virtues and 7 of Flaws. Its Init values are the book's Qik-based ones worked out. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

creatures.how_many: a template: a venomous snake turned vampire

powers.description: A touch that saps the victim's vitality: a disease beginning with a Medium Wound and two Fatigue levels lost until it passes. Each week a Recovery roll of 12 holds steady and 18 improves; Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.

creatures.appearance: An unusually big red-eyed snake, a good two paces long and thick as a man's thigh.
creatures.notes:
Venomous snakes are the likeliest animals to turn vampire; stallions, lambs and others may too, but never dogs or wolves. +6 more Defense against grapples. 3 points of Virtues and 3 of Flaws. Wound ranges: Light 1-2, Medium to 4, Heavy to 6, Incapacitated to 8, Dead from 9.

creatures.name: Vampire Tree
creatures.how_many: a template: a tree turned vampire, most often a hanging tree

abilities.name: Stealth
abilities.specialty: pretending to be a normal tree

powers.name: Sap the Life
powers.description: A touch that saps the victim's vitality: a disease beginning with a Light Wound and two Fatigue levels lost until it passes. Each week a Recovery roll of 12 holds steady and 18 improves; Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.

creatures.appearance: A white willow some twenty feet high with every branch pointing skyward until they whip down after blood; its silvery-green leaves are flecked with blood and bones lie among its roots.
creatures.notes:
A plant that killed a man, or grew from ground soaked with his blood, may turn vampire, even a gourd or melon kept too long; trees are the worst, above all one a suicide hanged himself from. Thorn trees never do, so they serve as gallows. It understands speech but cannot talk. It fights like a trained group with up to four limbs, always adding its +9 group bonus to Attack, grapples one victim at a time and adds +5 Grapple Strength for each further branch holding on (ArM5 p. 174). Its Passes for Human stands for the book's Passes for Plant, and Limited Movement is from Realms of Power: Magic. Sap the Life's Init is Qik-3 worked out. Not for a player. Wound ranges: Light 1-10, Medium to 20, Heavy to 30, Incapacitated to 40, Dead from 41.
